plugins.description: Android companion for DeepSeek Harness | chat, goals, approvals & notifications from your phone, over your LAN. Kotlin + Jetpack Compose.
plugins.readme_text:
DSH Mobile — DeepSeek Harness Remote

An open-source Android companion that puts your DeepSeek Harness in your pocket.
Drive sessions, review plans and goals, answer approvals and questions, and get notified when the harness finishes — from your phone, over your network or a relay.

English · 中文 · हिन्दी · Español · Français · ไทย

DSH Mobile is an **unofficial companion app** for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (MIT). It mirrors the web GUI feature for feature and uses the harness's own visual language. Android only, Kotlin + Jetpack Compose. Its companion on the other end is [**dsh-relay**](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-relay), a harness plugin that adds the authentication layer the harness says it lacks, so this app can reach a harness with a real credential and a pinned key instead of an open port. See [Relay](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Relay). **[dshm.zyphite.com](https://dshm.zyphite.com)** is the project site: what the app is, what it looks like, and how to get it running, on one page. The [**wiki**](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki) is the user-facing guide: [getting started](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Getting-Started), [connecting](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Connecting), [troubleshooting](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Troubleshooting), a [feature tour](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Feature-Tour) and an [FAQ](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/FAQ). --- ## Screenshots | Connect | Chat | Trajectory | |:--:|:--:|:--:| | | | | | Recent harnesses with live reachability, LAN discovery, manual `host:port`, auto-connect. | Streamed turns, a glyph per tool, expandable tool cards, permission picker. | The same session as a per-turn ledger with usage totals. | | Session details | Subagents | |:--:|:--:| | | | | Context breakdown, goal, plan mode, background jobs, queued turns, host info, session-log export. | The subagent catalog — open a child's transcript, follow up, or interrupt it. | ## Features - Connecting — finds a harness on your Wi-Fi with an active subnet scan and a readiness handshake, remembers hosts and probes them for liveness on the way in, takes a manual `host:port`, handles loopback for same-device setups, and auto-connects when you tell it to (last used, LAN, or same device). - Navigation — the drawers work like Discord's: swipe right from the left edge for the workspace-grouped chat list, swipe left to close it, swipe left from the right edge for the session details panel. - Chat — streamed turns with reasoning disclosure, markdown, terminal/diff/read/search/web tool cards, a queue dock where you can edit, remove or steer a queued turn, history paging, and multi-photo and file attachments. Drafts are kept per host and session. - Workspace panels — tabbed text, Markdown, image, PDF and isolated HTML previews; native terminal controls with a bundled xterm renderer; archived-session restore in Settings. - Message feedback — confirmed ratings and retraction, with version-conflict handling. - Slash commands and skills — typing `/` lists the session's commands and skills above the composer. The composer checks a `/` line against the session's own command catalog and runs it through the harness's command gateway. Anything the catalog does not claim is sent as a prompt, which is how skills get invoked. With the dsh-rewind plugin on the host, `/rewind` opens a picker. - Everything the GUI does — goals (phases, rounds, pause/resume/edit), plan mode and plan review, permission approvals, user questions, todo dock, subagents (catalog, follow-ups, interrupt), background jobs, workflow runs, skills, model selection, agent presets, session search, trajectory ledger, session export, message feedback. - Notifications — turn complete, goal complete or blocked, review or question waiting for you. A foreground service keeps the connection alive in the background. - Harness look — the exact DeepSeek Harness design tokens (colors, type, radii, disclosure rows, shimmer, ink buttons), with light, dark and system themes. - 11 languages — English, 中文, हिन्दी, Español, Français, العربية, বাংলা, Português, Русский, اردو, ไทย (RTL aware). ### Added in 0.15.0 - A Check now button for updates in Settings > About. The automatic check also runs again when you come back to the app after a few hours. - Workspace links in replies drawn as file and folder pills; a folder opens in Files. - A redesigned Details panel, Workspace screen and Settings, with archived sessions on a tab of their own. ### Added in 0.14.0 - A `/` menu above the composer with the session's commands and skills. - A picker for the dsh-rewind plugin's `/rewind` and `/undo` that asks for confirmation before it restores files. The transcript hides what a rewind withdrew and marks the cut. ### Added in 0.13.0 - Automation catalog, timing edits, delivery history and session shortcuts. - Plugin installation, updates, toggles, removal, progress and recovery. Create plugin stages an unsent draft with the Creator preset when the host offers it. - Timed questions, continued replies, saved answer drafts and reopenable plans. - Draft text and file, folder and session references saved across app restarts. - Model search, YAML document properties and multiline goal editing. - Reverse-proxy path support and tool argument previews while the model is writing. ## Requirements - Android 8.0+ (minSdk 26). - A running [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) at `0.2.1-alpha.2`, the protocol baseline for DSH Mobile `0.16.0`. Existing protocol fallbacks remain for `0.2.0-rc.1`, `0.1.7-rc.x` and `0.1.6-alpha.x`; new management features need host support. See [compatibility](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) and the [0.13.0 validation status](docs/VALIDATION-0.13.0.md) for what has been checked on this baseline. ## Quick start 1. Install the latest APK from [Releases](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/releases/latest). 2. Open the app and choose how to connect. Relay and local network are two different setups, not two settings of one, so pick the one that matches wha

plugins.description: Fork of jeffcwj/dsh-preset-switcher updated for DSH 0.2.1: switch the current session agent preset (mode) at any time, plus repair for sessions whose preset was deleted.
plugins.readme_text: # dsh-preset-switcher > [English](#english) | **中文** > **Fork 说明**：上游 `jeffcwj/dsh-preset-switcher` 最后提交是 2026-08-17，未适配 > DSH 0.2.1。该版本移除了宿主 `webRuntime` 服务（现在提供 `webApp`），而上游插件 > `inject: ['webServer', 'webRuntime']` 因此永远不挂载、`/preset-switch/api` 404， > 前端下拉菜单随之失效。本 fork 只做兼容修复（见 CHANGELOG.md），功能与上游一致。 > 已在 **DSH 0.2.1-rc.2** 上验证：插件正常挂载，`list` / `switch` / `repair` 三个方法 > 均按预期返回。安装方式见下方「安装 / 更新」，一条 `dsh plugin add` 即可。 --- ## 概述 DSH Web 插件：在**任何时候**切换当前会话的代理预设（模式），包括对话已经开始之后 — 原生 UI 不允许这样做（"已开始的对话的代理预设已固定"）。 ### 核心功能 - **顶部下拉菜单**：会话标题操作栏中的「当前模式 ▾」按钮，列出所有预设（如 `standard`=标准模式、`code`=PTC 模式、`minimal`=极简模式、`cordis`=创造模式），用 ✓ 标记当前预设，点击即切换。 - **失效预设修复**：如果会话记录的预设已被删除（自定义预设被移除），恢复将失败导致会话不可用。下拉菜单中的「修复失效模式会话」操作（及 `repair` API）会扫描所有会话日志并重写失效引用 — 最后一个 `agent-preset/selected` 事件，否则是标题 — 重置为默认预设，操作前自动备份日志并跳过活跃会话。切换未加载的会话时若引用失效也会自动修复。 - **受控路由**：`POST /preset-switch/api`，参数 `{ method: 'list' | 'switch' | 'repair', sessionId, presetId, target? }`（回环/可信主机限制，与 dsh-sounds 相同）。 ### 工作原理 原生 API（`agentPresets.select`）通过空白会话检查来保护切换操作。本插件底层调用同一原子原语 — `agentPresets.recompose(agent.ctx, presetId)` — 将代理的作用域重新链接到目标预设的常驻挂载点。新组合在链接移动前确保完成，因此损坏的预设不会影响会话。成功后插件追加与代理记录相同的 `agent-preset/selected` 会话事件，使投影和标题标签同步更新。 **限制**：仅已加载的活跃会话可切换；子代理拥有的会话将被拒绝；新的工具集/人设从下一个模型步骤生效。 ## 安装 / 更新 需要 DSH 0.2.1-rc.2（或同代 0.2.x）。插件是纯 JavaScript，没有构建步骤，装完即用。 ```powershell # 方式一（推荐）：直接从 GitHub 仓库安装 dsh plugin --profile web add github:neutronslime/dsh-preset-switcher-fork # 方式二：克隆到你自己选的目录，再从该目录安装（不依赖作者机器上的任何路径） git clone https://github.com/neutronslime/dsh-preset-switcher-fork.git dsh plugin --profile web add .\dsh-preset-switcher-fork ``` 安装或升级后重启 `dsh web`（profile 启动时会合并 `cordis.patch.yml`），刷新页面， 会话标题栏右侧就会出现「当前模式 ▾」按钮。 `dsh plugin` 把参数转交给 profile 目录里的 pnpm，不需要全局 npm；想自己检查打包内容， `npm pack --dry-run` 也可以（node 20.17+ 或 22.9+ 即可，npm 11 实测无碍）。 ## 文件结构 | 文件 | 说明 | |------|------| | `cordis.patch.yml` | Bundle 补丁：将插件行插入 profile 的 cordis 树（`dsh.bundle.patch`） | | `lib/index.js` | 服务端：受控 `/preset-switch/api` 路由（list / switch / repair）及会话日志修复逻辑 | | `lib/client.js` | 浏览器端：顶部下拉菜单（ClientModuleSystem bundle，React 通过 module-table externals） | | `scripts/` | `restart-web.ps1`（通用版重启+探测，路径自动推导）、`inspect-session.mjs` / `repair-session.mjs`（独立日志工具） | ## 许可证 MIT --- # dsh-preset-switcher > **English** | [中文](#概述) > **Fork note**: upstream `jeffcwj/dsh-preset-switcher` was last committed on 2026-08-17 and does not run on DSH 0.2.1: that release dropped the host `webRuntime` service (the web runtime now provides `webApp`), so the upstream `inject: ['webServer', 'webRuntime']` never mounts, `/preset-switch/api` answers 404, and the header dropdown is dead. This fork is the compatibility fix only (see CHANGELOG.md) — same features as upstream. Verified on **DSH 0.2.1-rc.2**: the plugin mounts and `list` / `switch` / `repair` all answer as expected. Install is a single `dsh plugin add`; see "Install / update" below. --- ## Overview DSH web plugin: switch the current session's agent preset (mode) at **any time**, including after the conversation has already started — the stock UI refuses that ("a started conversation's agent preset is fixed"). ### Features - **Header dropdown**: a "当前模式 ▾" button in the session header action row lists every preset (e.g. `standard`=标准模式, `code`=PTC 模式, `minimal`=极简模式, `cordis`=创造模式), marks the session's current one with ✓, and switches on click. - **Stale-preset repair**: if a session's recorded preset was deleted (a custom preset removed), resume fails and the session becomes unusable. The dropdown's "修复失效模式会话" action (and `repair` API) scans every session log and rewrites stale references — the last `agent-preset/selected` event, else the header — to the default preset, backing up the log first and skipping live sessions. Switching a not-loaded session whose reference is stale auto-repairs it too. - **Fenced route**: `POST /preset-switch/api` with `{ method: 'list' | 'switch' | 'repair', sessionId, presetId, target? }` (loopback/trusted-host fence, same as dsh-sounds). ### How it works The stock API (`agentPresets.select`) guards its swap with a blank-session check. This plugin calls the same atomic primitive underneath — `agentPresets.recompose(agent.ctx, presetId)` — which re-links the agent's scope to the target preset's standing mount. The new composition is ensured before the link moves, so a broken preset leaves the session untouched. On success the plugin appends the same `agent-preset/selected` session event the proxy records, so projections and the header label follow. Limits: only live (currently loaded) sessions can switch; subagent-owned sessions are refused; the new toolset/persona applies from the next model step. ## Install / update Requires DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 (or another 0.2.x build). The plugin is plain JavaScript — there is no build step. ```powershell # Option 1 (recommended): install straight from the GitHub repository dsh plugin --profile web add github:neutronslime/dsh-preset-switcher-fork # Option 2: clone into a directory of your choosing, then install from it git clone https://github.com/neutronslime/dsh-preset-switcher-fork.git dsh plugin --profile web add .\dsh-preset-switcher-fork ``` Restart `dsh web` after installing or upgrading (the profile boot merges `cordis.patch.yml`), reload the page, and the "当前模式 ▾" button appears in the session header. `dsh plugin` forwards to the pnpm inside the profile directory, so no global npm is needed; `npm pack --dry-run` works too if you want to inspect the tarball (node 20.17+ or 22.9+; npm 11 is fine). ## Layout | File | Description | |------|-------------| | `cordis.patch.yml` | Bundle patch: inserts the plugin row into the profile's cordis tree (`dsh.bundle.patch`). | | `lib/index.js` | Host half: the fenced `/preset-switch/api` routes (list / switch / repair) and the session-log repair logic. | | `lib/client.js` | Browser half: the header dropdown (ClientModuleSystem bundle, React via module-table externals). | | `scripts/` | `restart-web.ps1` (port-agnostic restart + probe; all paths derived at runtime), `inspect-session.mjs` / `repair-session.mjs` (standalone log tools). | ## License MIT

plugins.description: Put a translate button into the page the agent is looking at: one click replaces every visible text node in place, another click restores the original. Long pages are chunked, repeats are translated once, and the host LLM service does the work (the plugin holds no API key).
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-inpage-translator（整页翻译）

**你把页面给 AI 看，它替你把整页翻成中文。**

**按钮是常驻的**：插件后台每 1.5 秒扫一遍所有活着的浏览器会话，自动把「🈯 译」放进每一张有内容的页面 ——
你**不用先叫 AI 做事**，看到它点一下，页面上**每一个可见文本节点原地换成译文**；再点一下，回到原文。
页面导航了？下一次巡场会把按钮重新装上去。

按钮可以**长按拖动**（按住 320ms 进入拖拽），拖到左右边缘 48px 内会**自动吸成贴边的小把手**，点一下再展开 —— 它不会一直挡着你的正文。

> 它是第 8 个作品，也是**第一个"动别人的网页"的插件**：
> 前 7 个动的是本机、文件、窗口、发布链路，这个动的是一张陌生的页面 ——
> 所以两条边界写在最前面：**只改文本、只加内联样式**；**插件自己不持有任何 API key**。

---

## 它做什么

| 步 | 动作 | 细节 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ① | 找会话 | **枚举所有活着的浏览器会话**，自动挑最活跃、有页面的那一个（`session` 参数可显式指定） |
| ①' | **后台巡场** | 每 1.5 秒扫一遍：补按钮（**导航后重装**）+ 读点击（**点了就翻，不用等工具调用**）—— 这就是"常驻" |
| ② | 装浮层按钮 | 内联样式 + `position:fixed` + `z-index:2147483647`，**不注入 `<style>`**（页面 CSP 管不到它） |
| ③ | 打标 | `TreeWalker` 遍历文本节点，可译的父元素记下原始文本与编号（`data-dsh-pt="12"`） |
| ④ | 等点击（`action=install`） | 每 1.2 秒读一次页面状态，默认等 60 秒；用户点了就在**同一次调用里**翻好 |
| ⑤ | 分块送翻 | 相同字符串只翻一次；**翻过的串按「语言+原文」缓存**（同页翻第二次几乎瞬时）；**分块 3 路并行**；译文由**宿主 LLM 服务**生成 |
| ⑥ | 回填 | 按编号写回 `textContent`，并记下译文（再点按钮即还原） |
| ⑦ | 还原 | 点按钮或 `action='restore'` → 全部回到原文 |

**回执里一定有**：送翻条数、回填条数、模型调用次数、送翻字符数与本次上限、唯一串数、
缓存命中数、超限丢弃段数、兜底原文条数、跨域 iframe 个数，以及任何一条警告。**不编数字，不静默丢**。

## 已知边界（先说清，再说好用）

| 边界 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| **不是原生工具栏按钮** | 内置浏览器的工具栏是宿主硬编码的 HTML（`dsh-builtin-browser/host-main.js:123` 的 `TOOLBAR_HTML`），宿主不读任何外部字段 —— 第三方插件**没有**加工具栏按钮的扩展点。所以按钮做进页面里。 |
| **导航后按钮会消失（但位置会记住）** | 注入本身是运行期一次性的（宿主没有 `addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument` 这类通道）。**v0.2 起由后台巡场自动重装**；位置按站点记在 `localStorage`（`dsh-ipt-pos`），导航/重开都落回原处。 |
| **跨域 iframe 翻不到** | 只能进当前文档的 DOM。**回执会明确报「这一页有 N 个跨域 iframe 没翻」**，不静默跳过；同源 iframe 里的文字目前也不在整页翻译范围内。 |
| **只翻可见文本节点** | 图片、`background-image`、canvas 里的文字不动；`<input>` / `<textarea>` 的值不动。 |
| **字符上限默认自适应** | `maxChars` 不传时按页面唯一文本量自适应（`4000 ~ 24000` 字符）：小页面不被预留浪费、大页面不被 6000 硬截断；超出自适应上限的部分**如实回报**并跳过。给正数则按该值硬截断。 |
| **文本节点被包了一层 `<span>`** | 元素上只打标、不重排子树（`span` 用 `display:inherit`），但页面自己重写这段 DOM 时译文可能被覆盖 —— 那时重跑一次即可。 |

## 它依赖什么

- **内置浏览器插件**（`ctx.get('browser')`）—— 没有时明确报错，不会假装能用。
- **宿主的 LLM 服务**（`ctx.get('llm')`）—— 翻译由它完成，**插件不读任何 API key、不直接调任何 HTTP**。
  调用形状与宿主里已验证的两个先例一致（`dsh-meme` 的识图、`dsh-better-sidebar` 的提交信息）：
  `resolveCallConfig` → `prepareCall` → `stream`。

## 安装

市场收录后在 DSH 里搜 `dsh-inpage-translator` 安装。手动安装：

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Junction -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\desktop\node_modules\dsh-inpage-translator" -Target "D:\dsh\projects\dsh-inpage-translator"
# profile 的 package.json：dependencies 加 "dsh-inpage-translator": "link:D:/dsh/projects/dsh-inpage-translator"
# 并把 "dsh-inpage-translator" 加进 dsh.profile.bundles（漏了不加载）→ 重启 DSH
```

## 用法

```
translate_page action=install        # 确保按钮在，并等用户点（默认等 60 秒）
translate_page action=translate      # 不等点击，立刻翻
translate_page action=restore        # 回到原文
translate_page action=status         # 只读状态（含活会话清单）
translate_page action=sessions       # 只读：列出所有活着的浏览器会话
```

> v0.2 起 `install` **不再是必须的前置步骤**：后台巡场会自动把按钮装到每张有内容的页面上。
> `install` 现在只用于"想在同一次调用里等用户点一下"的场合。

可选参数：`target`（`zh` 默认 / `en` / `ja` / `ko` / `ru`）、
`mode`（`replace` 默认 / `bilingual` 双语对照）、`maxChars`（不传 = 自适应）、`waitSec`、
`session`（不传就自动用最活跃的那个会话）、`provider`、`model`。

## 怎么点这个按钮

| 手势 | 结果 |
| --- | --- |
| **点一下** | 翻当前页面（原文 → 译文）；已经是译文时点一下回到原文 |
| **长按 320ms** | 进入拖拽：松手前拖到哪，它就停在哪 |
| **拖到左右边缘 48px 内** | 自动吸成贴边的小把手（只留 🈯，不挡正文） |
| **点一下贴边的小把手** | 展开回正常胶囊形状（不触发翻译） |
| **拖过一次之后** | 位置按站点记下来（`localStorage`），导航/重开都落回原处 |

拖拽时**松手那一下不会误触发翻译** —— 这是"长按才拖"的设计目的。

典型流程：

1. AI 打开你要读的页面（浏览器窗口就在你眼前）——**按钮已经自动在上面了**；
2. 你点右下角的「🈯 译」；
3. 大约一两秒，页面就变成中文了；
4. 想对照原文，再点一下按钮（或让 AI 调 `restore`）。

## 三条设计取舍（都被现场逼出来的）

1. **按钮为什么在页面里、而不是工具栏里**
   宿主工具栏没有第三方扩展点（见上表），而"往页面里放一个浮层"是宿主自己就在用的姿势
   （`dsh-builtin-browser` 的 `virtual-cursor.ts:69-81` 就是这么画那个虚拟光标的）。
   零宿主改动、可随时卸载、升级不会被打回。

2. **按钮点击为什么由插件处理，而不是页面自己翻译**
   页面里没有到宿主的 bridge（也没有凭据，也不该有）。所以按钮只写一个**请求标记**
   （`data-dsh-pt-req`），插件轮询读到后去翻译 —— 这样凭据永远留在宿主侧。

3. **为什么"相同文本只翻一次"，还要按串缓存**
   网页里菜单/按钮/表头经常重复几十次。去重发生在**限额之前**，
   所以同样的字符额度能覆盖的页面比不去重时大得多。
   v0.2.2 又加了一层**跨调用缓存**：翻过的串在进程内记住（按「模型路线 + 语言 + 原文」，LRU 4000 条），
   同一页面翻第二次、或另一个页面有相同的串，都不再请求模型。
   键里带模型路线而不带 llm 对象 —— 宿主每次给到的 llm 不一定是同一个对象，按对象分桶会永远不命中（真机踩过）。

4. **为什么会话是"枚举"出来的，而不是靠 `open()` 传进去**（v0.2 的关键改动）
   `BrowserProvider.open(label)` 的语义就是**每次新开一个会话**，服务也没有 `listSessions` 之类的接口 ——
   插件根本拿不到"用户正在看的那一页"，上一版就卡在这儿：按钮装到了另一个窗口。
   v0.2 改成**只读地枚举运行时里真实存在的会话表**（`runtime.providers → provider.sessions`），
   严格 try/catch：宿主内部结构一变就当作"没发现"，退回 `open()` 的旧路径 ——
   **绝不因为读了一层私有结构，就把插件弄崩**。

## 安全与隐私

- **不发外部请求**：插件自己只做两件事 —— 在页面里跑脚本、调用宿主 LLM 服务；
  没有任何 `fetch`、没有本地 HTTP 端口、没有凭据读写。
- **不改页面结构以外的东西**：只写文本、只加内联样式与三个 `data-dsh-pt*` 属性；
  位置记忆只写 `localStorage` 的一个键（`dsh-ipt-pos`，存 left/top/edge，不存页面内容）。
- **翻译内容会经过你本机配置的模型**（DSH 的 provider）—— 这是这类功能的固有代价，
  页面上若有敏感信息，请自行判断要不要翻。

## 测试

```powershell
node test/smoke.mjs        # 75 项：纯逻辑 / 页面脚本 / 编排层（假 LLM）/ 驱动层（假浏览器与假页面）/ 会话发现与后台巡场 / 输出 schema 对齐
```

测试**不联网、不碰真实浏览器、不读任何凭据**。
在活代码树（`D:\dsh\projects\dsh-inpage-translator`）里跑会**直接退出**，
请先复制到 `D:\dsh\sandbox\` 再跑（避免在真宿主上生效）。

## 许可

MIT

plugins.description: DSH plugin: keeps streamed answers free of red (broken) KaTeX regions - validates every maths region with the client's own renderer before it is written
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-math-tex

让 DSH 的数学回答始终可读：给模型一套排版规则，再在文本落盘之前拦截并修好每一个会被渲染成红字的公式区域。

这是一个 host 侧插件，**没有客户端部分**——渲染器改不了，所以修复发生在文本还属于我们的最后一刻。

---

## 它解决什么问题

DSH 的对话渲染用 KaTeX 渲染 Markdown 数学，只要遇到它解析不了的东西，就把**原始源码**用 KaTeX 的错误色 `#cc0000` 直接吐到屏幕上。**没有崩溃，也没有日志**：一个位置不对的 `$$` 足以让整篇推导变成"一片血红"，而用户只会看到一片红字，不知道哪一步错了、也不知道原因。

前端是 `app.asar` 里的一个整体 bundle，给 KaTeX 传的选项是空的（没有 `errorColor`、没有 `maxExpand`、没有 `trust`），所以**事后无法配置**。文本一旦落盘，屏幕上和会话记录里就都是坏的。

`dsh-math-tex` 因此在文本落盘之前动手。

## 两道防线

| | 机制 | 作用 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `systemPrompt.section` | 事前规则：行间公式单独成段、`$$` 内只有公式、标题不粘公式……让模型少犯这个错。默认只注入给**已经出现过数学**的会话（`promptRules: auto`） |
| 2 | `llm/stream` waterfall | 兜底：用**客户端同版本**的 KaTeX 逐个区域判定，把会渲染成红色的区域改写掉，然后才落盘 |

第 2 道是关键：`llm/stream` 是每一次流式模型调用外面的 waterfall，改写过的 chunk 会同时进入持久化的消息体、实时前端帧和上下文压缩，所以**屏幕和记录一起修好**。

第 2 道认**两种定界符**：`$…$` / `$$…$$`，以及 LaTeX 原生的 `\(…\)` / `\[…\]`。后者不是可选项：2026-10-18 的一个会话里，模型两篇回答 11883 字、205 个反斜杠公式、**零个 `$`**，而界面照样把它们渲染成公式——只认一种定界符的守卫，等于只保护一半的回答。

## 判定不是正则，是问渲染器

直觉上的启发式（公式太长、嵌套太深、用了重型宏）经实测**两个方向都会错**：300 字符的公式、8 层 `\underbrace`、`\substack`、公式里的中文都渲染正常，而一个 99 字符的公式却死了。

更麻烦的是，"渲染器抛没抛异常"也不是判据：

| 输入 | 第 1 段调用（严格） | 第 2 段调用（宽松） | 读者看到 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `\foobar{x}` | 抛错 | 不抛错，把 `\foobar` 用 `#cc0000` 画出来 | 红字 |
| `x_1_2`（双下标） | 抛错 | 不抛错 | 红字 |
| `\htmlClass{red}{x}` | **成功** | — | **红字** |

第三行是最阴的一种：严格调用完全成功，输出里却带错误色。**只看异常的实现会把它判成健康。** 所以判定看的是**渲染产物里有没有错误色**。

## 修复原则：不猜数学

一个区域会被渲染成红色时，按顺序尝试：

1. **重新排版**——公式本身没问题、只是框架错了（例如 `$$` 开在段落中间），改成规范的 `$$\n…\n$$` 块；
2. **定点施救**——只在两种有确定语义的情况下动：删掉渲染器不认识的命令的反斜杠（`\foobar` → `foobar`），或给重复的算子重新分组（`x_1_2` → `x_{1_2}`）。改完必须**重新渲染验证"严格通过且无红色"**才接受，所以永远不会出现"改一下只是把错误挪了个位置"的循环；
3. **降级**——修不了的（括号不闭合、`\begin` 没有 `\end`）原样给出源码：块级区域包成代码围栏，行内区域只去掉定界符（围栏是多行结构，用在行内会把一条表格行切成三段）。

**数学永远不会被删掉。** 最坏情况是读者看到公式源码（可复制、可恢复），而不是红字。猜结构性损坏等于替作者编造数学，这件事不做。

## 安装

```bash
node tools/install.mjs              # 复制到 profile 并注册 bundle
node tools/install.mjs --dry-run    # 只说会改什么
node tools/install.mjs --uninstall  # 从 bundle 列表移除
```

装完**必须开新会话**：bundle 栈是会话的 runner 进程启动时读的，当前会话不会重新加载。

手工挂载也可以：把本包放进 `<profile>/node_modules/`，再把名字加进 profile `package.json` 的 `dsh.profile.bundles`。

## 配置

在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里按 id 设置：

```yaml
- id: dsh-math-tex
  name: dsh-math-tex
  config:
    repair: auto
    logFile: C:/tmp/math-tex.log
```

| 选项 | 默认 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true` | `false` 时两道防线都不挂载 |
| `promptRules` | `auto` | `auto` 只给已经出现过数学的会话注入 / `full` 每个会话都注入完整九条 / `minimal` 只留防红字的两条 / `off` 不注入 |
| `repair` | `auto` | `auto` 改写 / `check-only` 只记日志不改写 / `off` 完全放行 |
| `tailBuffer` | `15` | 最少扣住多少个字符，避免完成记号被逐字泄漏 |
| `maxHold` | `600` | 单个未闭合区域最多等多少字符，超了就把该块原样放行、并从此不再修复这一块（宁可不管，不可卡住） |
| `logFile` | `''` | 诊断日志路径；留空则只走 host logger |
| `katexPath` | `''` | 指定 KaTeX 位置，默认自动按 profile 解析 |
| `macros` | `{}` | 传给渲染器的宏，与客户端行为保持一致 |

未知键**报错而不是静默忽略**——写错的选项看起来像生效了，比没有这个选项更糟。

## 日志能证明它真的在工作

```
oracle: katex 0.16.47
prompt section "math-output-format" registered (auto)
llm/stream hooked model=deepseek-flash mode=auto
prompt rules now apply to session session-8c6a99cc-…
guarded stream: 214 text delta(s) in, 231 out
```

最后一行是**真实回合**的判据：`in` 必须远大于 1（自测喂的假流是 1）。

## 测试

```bash
npm test
```

| 文件 | 测什么 | 断言 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `guard-test` | 判定与区域切分是否和渲染器一致；两种定界符（`$…$` 与 `\(…\)`）是否都认；修复不许破坏周围的 Markdown 结构；释放点不许落进未闭合的行内代码、也不许被前面的围栏骗过去；裸 HTML 是否被记一行日志（标签被切到多次释放时也要报） | 106 |
| `red-render-test` | 三类红字是否都能抓到；`$$` 块的围栏是否和内容分处不同行（宿主只在这一形状下闭合）；回显是否从正确的账本读 | 87 |
| `e2e-test` | 真实事故文本端到端是否可读 | 39 |
| `wire-test` | 流式输出是否等于整篇修复 | 107 |
| `fuzz-test` | 该性质在 236 种任意切分下是否成立 | 236 |
| `config-test` | 每个文档化选项是否真的有效 | 36 |
| `smoke-test` | 包是否按宿主的加载方式加载 | 23 |
| `installed-test` | profile 里那份**安装副本**（不是源码目录）能否加载并自修；与源码逐字节一致 | 12 |
| `regression-test` | 已修缺陷不再回归（用例逐字引自真实会话） | 23 |
| `live-path-test` | **验收**：装好的那份 + profile 的真实配置 + 宿主的挂载路径，坏答案是否真的变成干净文本 | 28 |

合计 10 个文件、697 条断言，约 4 秒，不需要网络。

最有说服力的是 `fuzz-test`：它要求**真实事故文本的任意切分**（1 字符一帧到 1600 字符一帧，外加随机切分）最终都重组为**逐字相同**的整篇修复结果。

`live-path-test` 是唯一一个把"装好的副本、profile 的配置、宿主的挂载路径、真实的增量流"接起来测的文件。它每个用例跑两遍：关掉修复时缺陷必须原样到达读者，开着时必须消失——前一遍是后一遍的前提，否则一个根本没坏的用例也会"通过"。

`regression-test` 是唯一断言"**输出来的文本**渲染后没有红色"的文件——其余文件盯的是判定与结构，它是最后一道"判定对了、但改完仍然红"的防线。把修复回退掉，它会红 4 条。

### 关于 `test/fixtures/real-broken.txt`

这份夹具复刻的是**事故文本的结构**（同一批缺陷形态：段落中间的 `$$` 配错对、`##` 粘在行间公式里、未闭合的 `\begin`、结尾的代码围栏），内容已替换为与具体题目无关的通用推导，因此它测的是缺陷形态而不是任何一次具体事故。

想直接看一份文本是怎么被判定的：

```bash
node tools/inspect-fixture.mjs                    # 默认检查上面这份夹具
node tools/inspect-fixture.mjs path/to/text.md    # 换成任何一份文本
```

它会打印区域数量、被标记的区域及其原因、修复动作，以及修复后是否还有区域会被渲染成红色。

排查真实会话时有这几件工具：

```bash
node tools/find-red-session.mjs                   # 扫本机所有会话，列出还会渲染成红色的回答
node tools/strip-sentinel.mjs --list              # 列出正文里还留着哨兵的记录
node tools/strip-sentinel.mjs --id <前缀> --yes   # 把那些哨兵清掉（逐帧改写，改完自验，失败自动回滚）
node tools/inspect-session.mjs <session.jsonl>    # 单条会话逐条消息：区域、判定、守卫会怎么修
node tools/probe-region.mjs 'd\alpha=0'           # 把候选写法逐个送进渲染器，看哪种被接受
```

**注意**：记录里存的是**修复前**的原文——守卫改的是往外发的流，不改落盘的模型文本。
所以"记录里还有坏公式"不代表屏幕上还有红字，判断要看同一次流的出口。

## 设计边界

- **渲染器不可改**：这是设计前提，不是让步。前端是打包好的 bundle，没有数学相关的 slot 可以替换。
- **只做 host 侧**：唯一能同时影响屏幕、会话记录和压缩的拦截点在 `llm/stream`。
- **宁可不管，不可卡住**：所有等待都有界（`maxHold`），超限即原样放行——那正是没有插件时的行为，因此安全。
- **不改写非数学文本**：不含 `$` 和 `\` 的文本逐字节直通。

## 文档

- `STATUS.md`——现在装了什么、证明了什么、还差什么（交接用）。
- `docs/`——判据的来源：`FINDINGS.md`（到底坏在哪）、`KATEX-MEASUREMENTS.md`（逐个用例的实测数字）、`DESIGN.md`（方案怎么定的、否掉了什么）。

## License

MIT

plugins.description: Bilingual DeepSeek Harness changelog, security-advisory and storage panel — version timeline, CVE/GHSA records and disk usage in one sidebar panel.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-changelog-panel

[简体中文](README_zh.md)

> Primary repo: <https://github.com/HLhhh/dsh-changelog-panel> ·
> Gitee mirror: <https://gitee.com/huang-lin-java/dsh-changelog-panel>

**A bilingual changelog, security-advisory, and storage panel for DeepSeek Harness.** Install it and the
sidebar gains one entry: what changed in every release, which CVE/GHSA records affect your install, and how
much disk space DSH itself is holding.

- Version timeline with category-grouped feature cards and keyword search
- A **Security** tab: 13 advisories with severity, affected range, fixed version, and source links
- An installed-version badge that tells you how it compares to the official latest
- Per-panel language switch (zh / en) that neither follows nor changes the rest of the shell
- A companion storage dashboard: what DSH leaves on disk, what each item costs, which conversation owns it,
  and which parts are reclaimable

## What it looks like

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Changelog & Security   7 versions · 50 records  [Changelog][Security]│
├──────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Versions     │ 0.2.0-rc.2   latest   2026-09-29                      │
│ ┌──────────┐ │ One-line summary…                                     │
│ │0.2.0-rc.2│ │ ● Agent · 6                                           │
│ │latest·33 │ │   ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│ └──────────┘ │   │ ● Title / summary / related packages          │   │
│ 0.2.0-rc.1   │   └───────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│ 0.1.7-rc.2   │ ● Tools · 8   ● Sessions · 5   ● UI · 7 …             │
└──────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Install / Update

> Not published to npm yet — install straight from GitHub.

### With the `dsh` CLI

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:HLhhh/dsh-changelog-panel
```

Replace `web` with your profile name (`desktop` for the desktop app).

### With the `plugin_manager` tool (inside an agent)

Call `install_bundle` with `target` set to:

```
github:HLhhh/dsh-changelog-panel
```

### From a local checkout

```sh
git clone https://github.com/HLhhh/dsh-changelog-panel.git
dsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/to/dsh-changelog-panel
```

The prebuilt `lib/client.js` is committed, so **no build step is required to install**.
Restart DSH (or let HMR pick it up) and refresh the page.

Uninstall:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-changelog-panel
```

## Features

### Changelog

- Version timeline on the left, opening on the version **you actually have installed**
- Entries grouped by category: agent, UI, tools, sessions, security, platform, plugins
- Search across titles, summaries, and related package names
- At most 12 release entries rendered per version; older ones are reachable from the timeline

### Security

- 13 advisories and CVE/GHSA records with severity, status, affected range, fixed version, and links
- A "search scope" note stating what was searched and what was not found — no unsupported claims

### Live data

The panel talks to two public endpoints **directly from your browser**; no third-party server is involved:

| Source | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| `registry.npmjs.org/@deepseek-ai/dsh-base` | Version list and publish times |
| `api.github.com/repos/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases` | Official release notes |

- Refreshes once on the first open of each day, plus a manual refresh button with the last refresh time
- New versions are merged into the timeline but never overwrite the verified built-in dataset
- Rate limiting is reported explicitly instead of failing silently

### Storage dashboard

The same plugin also ships a storage view: what DSH has written to your disk (session logs, attachments,
caches, runtime binaries), how much each item costs, which conversation owns it, and what can be moved to
the OS trash. It **only reports** — it never deletes on your behalf — and categories that must not be
reclaimed say why.

## Configuration

None. Language is the panel's own state (the 中文 / EN toggle in its header); it follows the shell locale by
default and only affects this panel.

## Compatibility

| Surface | Status |
| --- | --- |
| DeepSeek Harness | `0.2.x` (developed and tested on `0.2.1-rc.2`) |
| Node | `^22.19.0 \|\| >=24.0.0` |
| Platforms | Web (browser and desktop) |
| Dependencies | Only the peer dependency `@deepseek-ai/cordis ~4.0.4`; no host package is bundled |

## Known limitations

- **No npm release yet** — GitHub or a local path only
- The built-in dataset is a point-in-time snapshot; use the manual refresh for current data
- Live refresh needs `api.github.com` and `registry.npmjs.org` to be reachable; otherwise only the built-in
  dataset is shown
- Storage figures come verbatim from the scan report; nothing is extrapolated
- Chinese entries are paraphrases, not quotations of the original advisories — consult the linked sources
  for compliance decisions

## Development

```bash
npm run build        # regenerate lib/client.js from src/
npm run data:verify  # validate the dataset
```

`lib/client.js` is generated — edit `src/` and rebuild; do not hand-edit the bundle.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

plugins.description: A desktop pet that shows what your coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, DeepSeek Harness) are doing — and lets you answer their permission prompts
plugins.readme_text:
# agent-pet

A floating desktop pet for coding agents. One character per active agent (Claude Code, Codex, DeepSeek Harness, or anything that can run a shell command); her mood follows the agent, and when an agent asks for permission the pet shows the prompt in a bubble you can answer without switching windows.

![agent-pet showing a permission bubble](docs/screenshot.png)

Pets appear only while a session is working, waiting for you, or just finished. Everything is local: agents append JSON lines to a file and the overlay tails it. Nothing is sent over the network and there are no accounts; the optional DSH plugin opens a loopback-only port (127.0.0.1) for the overlay's open-session commands.

## Requirements

- macOS 14 or later
- Swift 6 toolchain (Xcode or the Command Line Tools)
- Python 3 (ships with macOS; used by the installer)

ChatGPT (the chat app) has no local plugin API, so there is no integration with it. Codex running inside ChatGPT.app is covered by the Codex plugin below.

## Install

```sh
git clone https://github.com/rpegorov/agent-pet.git
cd agent-pet
scripts/install.sh                  # build, install to ~/.local/agent-pet, hook up Claude Code and Codex
scripts/install.sh --launch-agent   # also start the overlay at login
```

`install.sh` also accepts `--no-claude-hooks` and `--no-codex-hooks` (use these with the plugins below), and `--uninstall`.

## Connect your agents

Use **either** the plugin **or** the `install.sh` hooks for a given agent, not both. Both together would deliver every event twice and ask every permission twice; the emitter does not de-duplicate because it cannot tell which hook fired first. Plugins carry only the hook wiring, so run `scripts/install.sh --no-claude-hooks --no-codex-hooks` once for the binary and the overlay.

**Claude Code.** `install.sh` adds hooks to `~/.claude/settings.json`. Or, as a plugin:

```
/plugin marketplace add rpegorov/agent-pet
/plugin install agent-pet@agent-pet
```

**Codex.** `install.sh` adds hooks to `~/.codex/hooks.json` and trusts them in `~/.codex/config.toml`. Or, as a plugin:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add rpegorov/agent-pet
codex plugin add codex-agent-pet@agent-pet
```

Codex does not trust the plugin's hooks on a command-line install, so they stay silent until you approve them (see Troubleshooting). The `install.sh` route has no such step.

**DeepSeek Harness (DSH).** `plugins/dsh-agent-pet` is a standalone DSH plugin. In your profile's `package.json` add a dependency `"dsh-agent-pet": "link:/path/to/agent-pet/plugins/dsh-agent-pet"` and add `"dsh-agent-pet"` to `dsh.profile.bundles`, install, and restart DSH. It reports session state and lets the overlay open a session or start a chat in the Harness UI.

**Anything else** (scripts, task runners, other agents):

```sh
agent-pet-emit send --agent glm --session task-1 --label "refactor" --mood working
agent-pet-emit send --agent glm --session task-1 --mood complete
```

## Event protocol

`agent-pet-emit` appends one line per event to `~/.agent-pet/events.jsonl` (override with `AGENT_PET_LOG`); the overlay tails the file. The file is rotated to `events.jsonl.1` above 512 KiB.

```json
{"v":1,"agent":"claude","session":"5e9d","mood":"working","label":"Bash","ts":1792276251.42}
```

`mood` is `idle`, `working`, `attention`, `complete` or `ended` (removes the session). `label` is at most 40 characters. Optional fields, omitted when unknown: `cwd`, `app` (bundle id of the hosting app), `tty`, `detail` (permission summary, at most 200 characters), `permission` (id of a pending request).

Decay: working with no event for 120 s is hidden, complete is hidden after 10 s, attention after 10 min, a session silent for 30 min is dropped. An agent's pet shows the highest-priority mood of its live sessions: attention, working, complete.

## Permission bubble

With the overlay running, `agent-pet-emit permit` (the PermissionRequest hook) shows the pending tool call in a bubble with **Deny**, **In agent** and **Allow**, and a countdown.

- The bubble shows the whole tool input (pretty-printed JSON, capped at 8 KiB). If the input is capped or unreadable, Allow is withheld.
- **In agent** hands the prompt back to the agent's own dialog. If nobody answers before the countdown ends (at most 40 s, `AGENT_PET_PERMIT_WAIT` seconds, default 30), or the overlay stops running, the native dialog appears as usual. The pet never auto-allows.
- Tools that ask you something (`AskUserQuestion`, `ExitPlanMode`) are never turned into a bubble.
- Requests live in `~/.agent-pet/permissions/` (owner-only) and are removed when answered, expired or when the hook is killed.
- The overlay's own texts (Deny, In agent, Allow, status labels) are English and not localised; labels that come from agents (tool names, session titles) appear as sent.
- To turn the bubble off, quit the overlay (the hook then stays silent), or change the `PermissionRequest` command from `permit` to `hook` in the agent's hook config.

## Privacy

agent-pet keeps everything on your Mac and sends nothing over the network.

- **What is written.** `~/.agent-pet/events.jsonl` holds one line per hook event: agent name, session id, mood, a short label (tool name, session title or notification text), the working directory, the hosting app's bundle id, the terminal tty and, for permission requests, a summary of the tool call (at most 200 characters). Prompts, tool output and file contents are not recorded.
- **Permission requests.** While a request is pending, `~/.agent-pet/permissions/` holds its full tool input (at most 8 KiB). The file is deleted when the request is answered, expires or the hook is killed; leftovers older than 2 minutes are cleaned up.
- **Access.** The directory is owner-only (0700) and the log is 0600. The log is rotated at 512 KiB, keeping one previous file.
- **What is read.** The overlay reads the event log, and, to open a Claude Desktop session, the session index in `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude-code-sessions` (read only). Selecting a Terminal or iTerm2 tab uses AppleScript and asks macOS for Automation permission once.
- **System log.** Clicks and jumps are logged under the subsystem `agent-pet` with agent, session id, app and the opened URL; no tool input or paths.
- **Network.** None outbound. The DSH plugin listens on a loopback-only port and accepts commands only from local processes and the Harness web UI; the overlay talks to it over `127.0.0.1`.

Delete `~/.agent-pet` to remove all recorded data.

## Uninstall

```sh
scripts/install.sh --uninstall
```

Removes the binaries, hooks, trust entries and LaunchAgent. A no-op `agent-pet-emit` stub stays behind so sessions that are still open do not report a missing command; restart them and delete the stub. Plugins are removed with `/plugin uninstall`, `codex plugin remove` or by editing the DSH profile.

## Troubleshooting

- **Nothing appears.** Is the overlay running (`pgrep -x AgentPet`)? Does `~/.agent-pet/events.jsonl` grow when an agent works? If not, the hooks are not installed or the agent was started before they were; restart the agent.
- **Codex plugin hooks do nothing.** Codex 0.163 does not trust hooks from a plugin installed with `codex plugin add`; they ran only with `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`. Approve them in Codex (`/hooks`) or use `scripts/install.sh`, which writes the trust entries itself. Re-run `install.sh` after changing a hook command: the trust is tied to its text.
- **DSH changes are not picked up.** DSH caches plugin ES modules; restart it after installing or editing a plugin.
- **DSH commands are refused.** The plugin's bridge answers only the Harness web UI origin (`http://127.0.0.1:50306`) and local processes; a UI served from another origin cannot read its queue.

## License

MIT. The sprite art in `Sources/AgentPet/Resources` is included under the same license.

plugins.description: 轻量化的QoL插件，可在助手消息元数据行追加本轮 token 费用估算（¥）。
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-costview | 轻量化QoL插件

本插件在助手消息的**元数据行**追加了 `¥x.xx` 的显示功能：
按 DSH 记录的每轮 token 用量和官方**高峰 / 空闲**两档单价，估算这一轮花了多少钱。

> 兼容性：在 DSH 桌面版 **0.2.1-rc.2** 可运行

## 效果

![效果](./screenshot.png)

- 金额统一**保留两位小数**（精确到「分」）。不足半分钱的用量会显示成 `¥0.00`；
- 注意：**数字以 DeepSeek 账单为准，此处为估算值**。

## 估算方式

- 单价只覆盖 `deepseek-flash`。assistant 节点的 `usage` 里不带模型名，
  换用 `deepseek-v4-pro` 等其他模型时金额是错的（会严重偏低）；
- 一轮对话若是跨过 `12:00` / `18:00` 这种档位边界，整轮会按**最后一次请求**的档位计价；
- 缓存写入官方没有单独定价，这里并入「缓存未命中输入」计算；
- 取不到单轮数据时会退回到**整会话累计**，那一条会明显偏大。

## 计费规则

高峰时段（北京时间）：**周一至周五**（不含中国法定节假日）`09:00–12:00`、`14:00–18:00`；
其余时段——**含周末与法定节假日全天**——都算空闲时段，空闲价恰好是高峰价的一半。

单价在 `client.js` 的 `RATE_CARD`（人民币 / 百万 tokens，deepseek-flash）：

| 项目 | 高峰时段 | 空闲时段 |
|---|---|---|
| 输入（缓存未命中） | 2.00 | 1.00 |
| 输入（缓存命中） | 0.04 | 0.02 |
| 输出 | 8.00 | 4.00 |

数值取自官方价目页 <https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/quick_start/pricing/>。

## 法定节假日

- 覆盖 **2025–2026 两年，共 61 天**（2025 年 28 天、2026 年 33 天）；
- 不需要任何外部数据源，断网 / 全新安装都是同一套结果，不会静默算错；
- 只列「放假」日期，**调休补班的周末不在表里** —— 按官方字面「周末全天算空闲」照旧处理；
- 判定顺序固定为 **周末 → 节假日 → 钟点**，所以表中落在周末的日期不会改变结果。

法源：

- 《国务院办公厅关于 2025 年部分节假日安排的通知》国办发明电〔2024〕7 号
- 《国务院办公厅关于 2026 年部分节假日安排的通知》国办发明电〔2025〕7 号

## 已知问题

- 金额统计只覆盖了 `deepseek-flash`；
- 一轮跨峰谷边界时整轮按后一档计价；
- 部分插件的安装卸载过程可能会导致本插件的 GUI 界面暂时失效，重启即可。

## 安装 / 卸载

### 方式一：直接从 GitHub 安装（推荐）

```powershell
# <DSH 安装目录> = DeepSeek Harness 的安装位置，dsh.cmd 在其 resources\runtime\cli\bin\ 下
& '<DSH 安装目录>\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd' plugin --profile desktop add github:Yulu224/dsh-costview
```

### 方式二：clone 后挂载本地目录

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/Yulu224/dsh-costview.git
& '<DSH 安装目录>\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd' plugin --profile desktop add '<克隆目录>'
```

### 卸载

```powershell
& '<DSH 安装目录>\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd' plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-costview
```

plugins.description: DSH community plugin: ask any set of models to draw a pelican riding a bicycle on a schedule, then lay every drawing out on a read-only board. No scoring — the pictures are the result. Pausable, with a settable interval.
plugins.readme_text:
# @mi-lu-uncle/dsh-pelican-watch

English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) | [日本語](README.ja.md)

A DeepSeek Harness **community plugin** that runs a long-term
**model-quality probe** (降智监测) on a schedule, across **any number of
models**:

- **Pick your models** — the gear in the panel's top-right corner lists every model the
  configured providers report (live `/models` discovery, merged with the models
  in your DSH profile) and probes a multi-selected set, each model through its
  own provider and API key.
- **Scheduled drawing** — every 30 minutes (configurable) each selected model is
  asked to draw an **animated** *pelican riding a bicycle*: a single-file HTML
  page with an inline SVG whose motion is SVG declarative animation (`<animate>`
  / `<animateTransform>`).
- **No skills, no tools** — each run is a bare `chat/completions` request with
  no tool definitions and no agent loop, so the result measures the model
  alone, never your local skills.
- **Everything flat, nothing to click** — the main board is read-only: one band
  per model, its status and figures on the left (when its newest drawing landed,
  runs, average duration, how many came back without a drawing, and the failure
  reason) and every drawing it ever made on the right, all laid out at once —
  nothing collapsed, filtered, or hidden behind a click.
- **Run state in the header** — while probing: “n/m done”, which models are in
  flight, how long the slowest has waited (m:ss) and the timeout cap (m:ss), so a
  slow model and a stuck one are told apart at a glance.
- **One gear button** — the panel's own top-right corner opens a settings sheet:
  pick models, pause or retune the schedule, stop the pass, see one drawing
  bigger. The board below stays pure viewing, so nothing has to be clicked to be
  read. To probe **one** model, press 「单独检测」 on its band: one request for
  that model — and several bands can be probing at the same time.
- **Stop it, retune it** — that same sheet can **pause / resume automatic
  probing**, change the **interval** (1–1440 minutes), and **stop the pass that is
  running right now**: requests in flight are aborted, models that had not started
  are skipped without a request being sent. Pausing is written to
  `settings.json` immediately and survives a restart, so a plugin you only probe
  by hand never costs a token on its own.
- **Bounded history** — keeps the newest N drawings **per model** (10 by
  default); the cap never gets divided between the models you are probing, and
  two providers serving the same model id keep separate histories. Same prompt,
  same model, over days: degradation shows up as worse structure, refusals
  (saved and badged 「未检出 SVG」), or latency growth.

## Install

From this GitHub repository (recommended):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add https://github.com/mi-lu-uncle/dsh-pelican-watch.git
```

Or from a local path or tarball:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add /absolute/path/to/dsh-pelican-watch
```

Note: `link:`-installed plugins are not watched by HMR, so editing
`lib/index.js` or `lib/client.js` requires an app restart to take effect.

## Choosing models

The gear in the panel's top-right corner opens the settings sheet, which lists
**every provider route registered in DSH** — the signed-in 「DeepSeek 账号」
account, the official API-key route, and any third-party provider you configured
— grouped by the display name DSH uses, each with the models it advertises. Tick
any number of models and **Save models**: from the next cycle on each selected
model draws its own picture and gets its own band on the board.

**The board shows exactly the selected models**, in the order they were saved —
a band never jumps around. Unticking a model and saving **deletes its drawings**:
anything the board cannot show is only invisible dead weight on disk, and these
probe drawings are meant to be re-drawn anyway. The save toast says how many went.

A model id is not unique: the signed-in account and a third-party provider can
both serve `deepseek-flash`. A band is therefore a **provider + model** pair, and
it carries the provider's display name next to the model name — two providers
never share one band, nor one another's drawings.

The plugin never touches key material: calls go through DSH's model service
(`ctx.llm`), which resolves the credential itself. That is why the
account-backed provider (no API key at all, just a signed-in account) can be
probed here, and why any provider that works in DSH works here. A provider that
cannot list its models (not signed in, expired key) still appears, with the
reason attached.

That selection lives in `dir/settings.json` and is what the scheduler uses;
`config.model` / `config.targets` only seed the first run. The same file holds
two knobs that decide what you spend, both changeable from the panel's gear
without touching any config file:

| key | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `autoEnabled` | `true` | Off disarms the timer at once (`nextRunAt` goes empty); only the manual “probe now” then spends anything, and the choice survives a restart. |
| `intervalMinutes` | follows `config.intervalMinutes` (30) | Changing it in the panel re-arms the countdown immediately — no restart. |
`config.model` / `config.targets` only seed the very first run. At most 12
models are probed per cycle — `concurrency` of them at the same time (3 by
default), one drawing each.

## Speed and timeouts

- **Models run in parallel** (3 at a time by default), so one slow model no
  longer delays the others: every drawing is written to disk the moment it
  arrives and shows up in the panel within seconds.
- **Each request has its own timeout** (`timeoutSeconds`, default 600). A model
  that exceeds it is reported as `超过 N 秒没有返回` on its own band instead of
  hanging the whole pass. Reasoning models can genuinely be slow — measured
  against one provider: `qwen3.7-max` ~52s, `deepseek-flash` ~121s (15k of those
  completion tokens were reasoning), while `glm-5.3-flash` sometimes exceeded
  4 minutes.
- **A timeout or HTTP error is not a drawing**: nothing is saved and it does not
  count as a drawing, because that is an infrastructure fact rather than model
  behaviour. A model that *answers* without an SVG (a refusal) is saved and
  marked `没出图` — that is the signal worth looking at.
- `maxTokens` is not sent by default: reasoning models spend tens of thousands of
  completion tokens before they draw, and a tight ceiling would truncate the SVG
  instead of speeding anything up.
- **A truncated drawing is reported as such**: when the answer stops at the
  output ceiling (an `<svg>` without its closing tag), the band says
  「回答被截断（已输出 N tokens）：SVG 没有画完，多半是达到模型的输出上限」 instead of the
  vague 「未检出 SVG」, and the half-drawn page is not kept as history. Raise
  `maxTokens` in the config to give a verbose model more room.

## Configuration

Defaults match the usual profile setup; override any of them on a
`pelican-watch` row in your profile patch (`cordis.patch.yml`):

```yaml
- id: pelican-watch
  config:
    # initial selection (the panel's picker wins once used)
    provider: deepseek-account           # a DSH provider route; account by default
    model: deepseek-flash                # model id
    # targets:                           # optional: seed several models at once
    #   - { provider: deepseek-account, model: deepseek-flash }
    #   - { provider: taotoken, model: glm-5.3-flash }
    intervalMinutes: 30                  # drawing cadence
    maxImages: 10                        # drawings kept per model (1–100; ≈5h at 30min)
    timeoutSeconds: 600                  # per-request ceiling (5–3600); lower it if a model hangs
    concurrency: 3                       # how many models are probed at once
    # maxTokens: 8192                    # optional; unset by default (see below)
    dir: ~/.dsh/pelican-watch            # where drawings are saved
    runOnStart: true                     # draw once ~8s after boot
    # temperature: 0.7                   # optional; omitted by default
    # prompt: …                          # only if you must change the benchmark
```

plugins.description: Live per-session cost badge for DeepSeek Harness (top-right), with peak/off-peak (time-of-day) pricing.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-plugin-cost-meter

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-plugin-cost-meter)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-cost-meter)
[![license: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![dsh-plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/topic-dsh--plugin-2ea44f)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that puts a **live cost badge in the conversation header (top-right)** and prices every request with **peak / off-peak (time-of-day) tiers**.

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Session title                                [¥0.0042]      │   ← badge here
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  … conversation …                                            │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Features

- **Live** — the badge updates as the host reports provider usage; no polling, no timers.
- **Historically correct** — each request is priced by its **own wall-clock timestamp**, so a session that spans peak and off-peak stays accurate even if the page sits open overnight.
- **Weekday-aware peak tiers** — DeepSeek bills peak only **Monday–Friday**; weekends are off-peak all day. The schedule is configurable (windows, weekdays, multiplier, time zone).
- **Silent price sync** — a bundled price catalog plus an out-of-band remote catalog refreshed on an interval. Push a new `catalog/prices.json` and every installed copy picks it up **without a plugin release**; a failed refresh keeps the last good rates.
- **Explicit peak/off-peak rates** — models may carry an explicit discounted pair (`cacheMiss` + `cacheMissOffPeak`), not just a multiplier.
- **Route-aware matching** — `provider/model`, `provider/*`, `*`-model wildcards, and case/space/punctuation-insensitive model ids.
- **Never fakes a number** — an unpriced route renders `未配置` (`unpriced`) instead of a made-up fallback rate.

## Install

### From npm (recommended)

```cmd
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-cost-meter
```

The package declares `dsh.bundle`, so `dsh plugin add` activates it as a profile layer automatically — no manual `cordis.patch.yml` row is required.

### From a local checkout

```cmd
dsh plugin --profile web add "link:E:/path/to/dsh-plugin-cost-meter"
```

`link:` keeps the checkout live, so edits apply after a `dsh web` restart without reinstalling.

Restart the server afterwards:

```cmd
dsh web
```

## Configure

The bundled `cordis.patch.yml` inserts the plugin row with defaults. Override it by adding a `cost-meter` row with the same `id` in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`):

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: cost-meter
      name: dsh-plugin-cost-meter
      config:
        currency: CNY                 # display currency; empty = catalog currency
        fx:
          cnyPerUsd: 7.1              # used when the catalog is USD and you display CNY
        catalogUrl: ""                # "" = this package's own catalog (derived from repository)
        refreshMinutes: 360           # silent refresh interval; 0 disables it
        pricingTimeoutMs: 4000
        pricingUrl: ""                # optional legacy { models, default } document
        models:                       # manual overrides (highest priority, display currency)
          deepseek-official/deepseek-flash:
            inputPerM: 1.06           # off-peak base
            cacheReadPerM: 0.021
            cacheWritePerM: 1.06
            outputPerM: 4.26
        default:                      # optional fallback; omit to report unknown routes as unpriced
          inputPerM: 1
          outputPerM: 4
        peak:
          enabled: true
          multiplier: 2               # used only when a rate has no explicit off-peak value
          timezoneOffsetMinutes: 480  # UTC+8
          days: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]       # ISO weekdays; weekends are off-peak
          windows: [[9, 12], [14, 18]]
```

Two rate styles are accepted everywhere:

- **Catalog style** (peak base + optional off-peak): `cacheMiss`, `cacheHit`, `cacheWrite`, `output`, and `cacheMissOffPeak`, `cacheHitOffPeak`, `cacheWriteOffPeak`, `outputOffPeak`.
- **Legacy style** (off-peak base): `inputPerM`, `cacheReadPerM`, `cacheWritePerM`, `outputPerM` (with optional `*Peak` fields).

## Automatic price updates

Prices resolve in this order (highest wins):

1. `config.models` / `config.default`
2. `config.pricingUrl` (legacy document)
3. the **remote catalog** at `config.catalogUrl` — default: this package's own `catalog/prices.json` on GitHub, derived from `package.json.repository`
4. the **bundled** `catalog/prices.json` (offline fallback)

A timer re-reads the remote catalog and `pricingUrl` every `refreshMinutes` (default 6 hours) and swaps the live table in place:

- a failed refresh **keeps the last successful data**;
- a source that never loaded does not clear anything;
- **historical amounts are frozen**: a sample is priced when it is folded and the amount is stored, so a price change applies only to samples folded after it — a past session's total is never rewritten;
- the frozen amounts ride the persisted projection cache, so they survive restarts; only a cold replay without a checkpoint prices the log at the then-current table.

This makes the catalog the single place to maintain rates: **edit and push `catalog/prices.json`, and installed copies update themselves** — no new plugin release. Forks get their own update channel automatically because the default URL is derived from `package.json.repository`.

To point at a private mirror or a local file, set `catalogUrl` (`https://…`, a path, or `file:///…`). Set it to `""` to disable remote syncing.

## Peak / off-peak

- Tiering uses the **request's own `event.time`**, never "now".
- Peak applies only on the configured weekdays (`days`, default Monday–Friday); weekends are off-peak all day.
- The schedule comes from the catalog's `peakSchedule` (time zone, days, windows, off-peak ratio) and can be overridden field by field in `config.peak`.
- `peak.enabled: false` bills one flat rate; `peak.timezoneOffsetMinutes` shifts the wall clock for the window check.

The hover tooltip shows the current tier, the multiplier, the route, and the token breakdown.

## Pricing model

```
cost = Σ_routes [ cost_off(route) + cost_peak(route) ]

cost_tier(route) = (uncachedInput × miss
                  + cacheRead     × hit
                  + cacheWrite    × write
                  + output        × out) / 1_000_000
```

Totals are accumulated per `{ provider, model }` route and per tier, so switching models mid-session keeps each route on its own price. A repeated usage sample for the same `(turn, step)` replaces the earlier one instead of double-counting.

## Compatibility

| Surface | DSH ≤ 0.1.0-rc.6 | DSH ≥ 0.1.5 |
|---|---|---|
| Projection contract | `schema` + `view` | `stateSchema` + `wire: { viewSchema, view }` |
| Client deps | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-renderer`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-session` |
| Compatibility gate | — | `engines.dsh` / `peerDependencies` must satisfy the running version |

The badge uses the additive `conversation.session.header.utilities` slot; `…header.corner` is a `single` slot already occupied by a shipped plugin.

## Development

```cmd
npm install
npm test
```

`test/contract.test.mjs` covers the projection contract, weekday peak, catalog parsing, explicit dual rates, currency conversion, normalization/wildcards, unpriced routes, and manual overrides. It runs offline (`catalogUrl: ""`).

## Notes

- Costs are **estimates**: they depend on the provider-reported `usage` and on the price table.
- The badge is **per session**; it does not aggregate sub-sessions or the whole account.
- The bundled catalog is a dated snapshot — verify it against the [official pricing page](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing) and update `catalog/prices.json` when rates change.
- The plugin is a Web surface plugin; compositions without `sessionProjections` (e.g. headless) skip registration.

## Li

plugins.description: Second-opinion review for DeepSeek Harness sessions: a restricted child session re-reads the Executor's work with read-only tools and delivers severity-ranked advice.
plugins.readme_text:
# @wweir/dsh-advisor

English | [简体中文](README.zh.md)

An automatic second opinion for DeepSeek Harness sessions.

On a configurable step rhythm, a **restricted sub-agent** re-reads the
Executor's recent work with read-only tools. Concrete defects are recorded and
delivered to the Executor's inbox; when there is nothing to point at, the
reviewer stays silent — silence is the normal outcome, not a failure.

The plugin never runs its own model loop: the review is a real child session,
so the host's turn/step machine, tool pipeline, streaming, cancellation and
persistence apply to it unchanged.

## What it does for you

- **Catches hallucinations.** The reviewer reads the actual files (read-only):
  changes claimed but not made, APIs that do not exist, values never written.
  The note points at the mismatch while the work is fresh; delivery is
  advisory, interrupting only as configured.
- **Keeps sessions on track.** At most one review every N completed steps
  (default 10), never concurrently — a step boundary that arrives mid-review
  waits for the next cadence instead of stacking reviews. A step is one model
  call plus its tools, so one cadence covers work inside a long turn and work
  spread across many short turns; `everySteps: 0` turns automatic review off.
  Drift is reported inside the running turn; idle sessions can be woken by
  severe findings (budgeted, severity-gated). Silence is reported as a result,
  not an error.
- **Bounded cost.** The reviewer's context is a compiled projection capped at
  32K tokens by default (≈ **25% of a 128K window**), never a copy of the
  Executor's. The projection marks where the work since the last review that
  concluded (a silent or finding outcome) begins, and the prompt asks the
  reviewer to judge that part first —
  concluding within three steps and batching independent reads. The boundary
  line carries a nonce minted per review, so a phrase quoted inside the
  evidence cannot pose as it. A stable instruction prefix lets the provider's
  context cache
  hit across reviews (cache-read tokens are shown in the tab and billed at
  cache rates). Output is a single advice of at most 2K characters.

## Why

Most advisor plugins hand the transcript to one extra LLM call and inject
whatever comes back. This plugin makes the reviewer a **real child session with
its own read-only tools**, which buys four concrete things:

- **It verifies instead of guessing.** The reviewer opens the files the
  Executor actually touched, so a note points at a defect it looked at — not
  a pattern inferred from a transcript summary, which is all a
  transcript-only reviewer can ever offer.
- **The host's rules apply to the review itself.** Turn/step accounting, the
  tool pipeline, streaming, cancellation, persistence, and a real audit
  trail: the review is a session you can inspect, and its cost is reported
  usage, not an estimate.
- **Isolation is enforced, not promised.** One reviewer claim per process, a
  read-only tool surface, a protected-path guard deliberately stricter than
  the upstream advisor (workspace-root private keys and `.envrc` included),
  and no shared context with the Executor.
- **Delivery is accounted.** A **follow-up** note counts as delivered only when
  the host proves it was processed (that turn's model reply); an unconfirmed
  note is requeued, never silently dropped. A note steered into a running turn
  counts as delivered at the hand-off. Repetition is suppressed by finding
  identity plus similarity, with hash-based mutes.

## Install

The package is a Cordis plugin (`dsh.bundle.patch` → `cordis.patch.yml`) and is
published on npm with a provenance attestation, so it installs like any other
profile bundle:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @wweir/dsh-advisor
```

A development checkout can be linked instead (`dsh plugin … add /path/to/checkout`);
its deploy path is described in `docs/OPERATIONS.md`.

Then give it a model route. It is **disabled until a model is configured**, and
it never falls back to the Executor's model:

```yaml
- id: advisor
  name: '@wweir/dsh-advisor'
  config:
    enabled: true
    model:
      provider: opencode-go
      model: glm-5.3-flash
      reasoningEffort: low
    instructions: ''            # extra review instructions, appended to the prompt
    review:
      everySteps: 10            # minimum completed steps between two reviews (0 = off)
      timeoutMs: 180000         # wall-clock bound for one review
      maxContextTokens: 32000   # material sent to the reviewer
      maxAdviceChars: 2000      # one advice body
      maxPending: 32            # queued, not-yet-delivered notes
    delivery:
      activeIdleSeverities: [concern, blocker]   # severities allowed to wake an idle Executor
    security:
      additionalProtectedPaths: []      # extra paths the reviewer may never read
```

A patch entry is **replaced, not merged**, per row id: an overlay that sets
only the extra instructions drops the model route, so the row loads **disabled**;
it fails loudly, with a validation error, only when the overlay also asks for
`enabled: true`.

## Behaviour worth knowing

- **Trigger** — one cadence: a completed *step*, i.e. one model call plus the
  tools it ran. Steps are the host's progress unit, so the same counter covers
  work inside a long turn (which crosses no reply boundary for dozens of steps)
  and work spread across many short turns; there is no second, reply-based
  interval that could disagree with it. A review starts once `everySteps` steps
  (default 10) have accrued since the previous one finished. The cursor moves
  when a review *finishes*, so a slow review cannot chain into the next one; the
  counter and cursor are absolute and persisted, so a reload continues the
  cadence instead of forgiving the steps that accrued since the last review. A
  fresh session is first reviewed after a full cadence, not immediately. The
  turn's final answer starts no review of its own: the steps that produced it
  already had their chance, so the tail of a session that stops mid-cadence is
  reviewed by the next steps that accrue. Sub-agent sessions (including the
  review children) are never reviewed. Turns this plugin opened itself are never
  reviewed either.
- **Delivery** — while the Executor is running the note is handed into the
  next step boundary; while it is idle the note may open an exclusive turn,
  but only for a severity allowed to wake an idle session (by default
  concern and blocker), at most 5 times per session; anything else waits for
  a later flush. A note delivered into a running turn is recorded as
  delivered once the host accepts it. A note that opened an exclusive turn is
  recorded **only after that turn emits a model reply**: the hand-off alone
  does not prove the note was read, so a turn that closes (restart,
  interrupt, empty turn) without a reply puts the note back in the queue,
  marked as already attempted — it will not open a second follow-up turn, but
  the next running turn can still receive it. The confirmation is persisted
  immediately, and an unconfirmed claim found in the sidecar on load is
  requeued the same way. A delivered finding is suppressed by identity, so a
  reworded repeat is not re-delivered.
- **Failure pause** — three consecutive *real* failures (model error, timeout,
  bad tool surface) pause automatic review. Cancellations are counted separately:
  they are recorded but never pause. A pause holds for the life of the loaded
  plugin; **a plugin reload (a profile-row change or a process restart) clears
  the tripwire** and re-arms review. Saving the page's configuration form is not
  a reload and leaves a paused advisor paused.
- **State** — one JSON sidecar per Executor session under
  `$DSH_HOME/advisor/` (default `~/.dsh/advisor/`). It holds the step counter
  and its cursor, the dedupe table, the pending queue, the mute list, and the
  failure accounting as diagnostics. A file that does not parse is never
  overwritten and is reported in the host log.
- **Mutes** — add `{ "hash": "<64-hex hash of the finding>", "label": "..." }`
  to the sidecar's `mutes` list. Identity is the full ha

plugins.description: Offline HAR diagnostics with minimal evidence for DeepSeek Harness
plugins.readme_text:
# HAR Triage

Offline network evidence for DeepSeek Harness. Find failed and slow browser requests without handing the agent your URLs, cookies or response bodies.

浏览器网络排障插件：读取本地 HAR，生成可回查原始请求索引的离线诊断报告。默认不把网址、请求头、Cookie、参数值或正文带进报告和 AI 工具结果。

![Synthetic HAR diagnosis: signals, source indexes and timing evidence](docs/report-demo.jpg)

The screenshot uses the bundled synthetic scenario, not real browser traffic.

## What it does

- Reads an existing HAR 1.2 capture; never records traffic, sends requests, or changes the capture.
- Groups requests into endpoint aliases, highlights HTTP 4xx/5xx, unavailable responses, slow requests and long waiting phases.
- Produces a self-contained HTML report: signals → request row → measured timing phases. Filters, pagination and source locators work offline.
- Returns at most 20 evidence entries to the agent, with a count of omitted evidence. The full numeric projection stays in the local JSON/HTML files.

Request #43 corresponds to `log.entries[42]` in your original HAR. Endpoint aliases deliberately do not reveal names. Keep the original capture private and use its index to look up the actual request locally.

## Install in Harness

Node 22.19+ is required. Install the prebuilt bundle into your chosen profile:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile YOUR_PROFILE add https://github.com/po-et/dsh-har-triage/releases/download/v0.1.0/dsh-har-triage-0.1.0.tgz
dsh --profile YOUR_PROFILE --dump-config
```

The configuration should contain the `har-triage` row. Start that profile, put your HAR inside its session workspace, and ask:

> Inspect capture.har with har_triage. Save reports in a new har-review directory. Explain the measured evidence and cite the original HAR entry indexes. Do not guess root causes.

Tool arguments:

```json
{"input":"capture.har","outputDir":"har-review","slowMs":2000}
```

The tool uses Harness filesystem and sandbox services. It requires write permission to create the reports and refuses input/output paths outside the session workspace. Existing report files are never overwritten. Uninstall with `dsh plugin --profile YOUR_PROFILE remove dsh-har-triage`.

## Try without Harness

The CLI and analysis/report modules use Node built-ins only. From a source checkout:

```sh
node src/cli.js capture.har --out new-report-directory --slow-ms 2000
```

Open `new-report-directory/report.html`. The output directory must not exist. The original capture is unchanged.

For a reproducible synthetic example:

```sh
npm run demo
```

This creates a new directory under `artifacts/` with a deliberately synthetic capture and its report. It is not evidence of real browser traffic or real users.

## Evidence, not root-cause claims

`503` means the capture records a server-error response. `status: 0` means it did not record a valid HTTP response. Neither identifies a failing service, proves CORS, or proves an expired token. A high wait/TTFB share is an observation, not proof that the backend or database is slow.

Start offsets include submillisecond differences and are expressed in relative milliseconds. Absolute source timestamps are never included in the report.

Unknown phase timings and byte sizes remain `-1`, displayed as “Unknown.” TLS is part of the HAR connection timing and is not added a second time. Contradictory phase durations are flagged; the report hides misleading proportions.

Ollama's [`application/x-ndjson` streaming responses](https://docs.ollama.com/api/streaming) are classified as JSON. This is a MIME-based content category, not validation of the response body; model output remains excluded from reports.

## What is retained and removed

Retained: source entry index, sequential endpoint alias, controlled method/status/content classes, relative offsets, numeric durations/sizes, and fixed diagnostic codes. Aliases group the same method/origin/path within one capture; query strings and fragments do not affect grouping.

HTTP method identity is case-sensitive: `GET` and `get` receive separate aliases. Only the allowlisted uppercase methods receive named display values; all other method tokens appear as `OTHER`. Private method tokens are used only for grouping and are not included in reports, tool evidence or report ID hashes.

Removed: complete URLs including origins and paths, query values, headers, cookies, request/response bodies, page titles, initiator data, IP addresses, absolute timestamps, extension fields, raw error text, and the original file digest. The report ID hashes only the retained projection. Arbitrary source strings are not copied to reports or tool evidence.

This is a minimal diagnostic projection, **not** a scrubbed HAR, an anonymization guarantee, or a replacement for reviewing an artifact before sharing it. Status patterns, sizes, timing, request counts and grouping can still identify an application. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

## Limits

- HAR JSON only: version `1.2`, UTF-8, at most 16 MiB and 10,000 entries. Invalid supported entries fail with fixed errors rather than silently truncating the evidence.
- HTTP and HTTPS requests are analyzed. Other protocols are excluded and counted. Missing timing/size values are retained as unknown; a valid request URL, start timestamp, duration, status and response content object are required.
- Synchronous bounded analysis: cancellation is checked before parsing and between entries, not an interruptible worker. The slow threshold defaults to 2,000 ms and is configurable per call.
- Reports are created exclusively. If HTML creation fails after JSON creation, the JSON is retained and the tool reports the partial result; retry using a fresh destination.
- No upload, traffic replay, header inspection, body analysis, automatic source lookup, or edits to the original HAR.

## Development and validation

```sh
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm test
npm run smoke:host
npm pack --dry-run
```

48 tests passed on Node 24 and 26. They cover actual CLI subprocesses, controlled output and failure text, input limits, phases, original-file preservation, and real Cordis tool dispatch/filesystem/sandbox/Loader integration. `smoke:host` is a real service composition, not a CLI profile boot or a live-LLM test.

The packed bundle was separately installed through the actual CLI into fresh temporary Profiles on Harness `0.2.0-rc.2` and `0.2.1-alpha.2`, then booted with `runProfile` and exercised through `har_triage`. Source bytes were unchanged; output omitted the synthetic canary; overwrite and workspace-escape attempts were refused. HMR was disabled only in those temporary Profiles. The alpha host emitted three unrelated Typert activation warnings; rc.2 did not. No LLM or real credentials were used.

Browser checks covered status filtering, signal-to-request navigation, correct source locators, no console errors, and a 390-pixel layout without page-level overflow. The demo and regression captures are synthetic; real-user usefulness is not yet validated.

## Related tools

[net-debug](https://github.com/JohnXu22786/net-debug) is an existing Harness HTTP client with history, replay and HAR export. [harlite](https://github.com/brucehart/harlite) already offers extensive HAR analysis, SQL, waterfall and HTML reporting. This plugin does not replace those tools: its narrower purpose is a Harness-native, no-external-binary, allowlisted evidence path for agent-assisted debugging.

MIT licensed.

plugins.readme_text:
# 设计与代码的建模/自动化审查（dsh-model-everything）

English · 中文

把设计与代码里的断言抽象成模型，交给引擎跑一遍：结论带出处与哈希，能复算、能比对。让结论来自一次运行，而不是一次通盘推理：把「想清楚」变成「跑一遍」。 DeepSeek Harness 原生插件。把设计与代码里**关于行为的断言**变成可运行、可审查、可导出的模型： - **核验断言**：逐条对着源码检查，引用到 `file:line`。 - **跑模型**：状态机、协议、多机协作、数据模型先建成可执行模型，再交给引擎跑。 - **审图**：UML 图按模型读、按模型审，并与模型对照。 - **对照重构**：重构前后各建一份模型，两份报告摆一起比。 - **留痕**：结论固化成带哈希的报告，可复算、可比对、可导出。 ## 能力范围 | 域 | 做什么 | |---|---| | 事实核验 | 把一份设计/规格/评审意见里的可验证断言列出来，逐条对着代码核验并给出出处。核不了的直接说明 | | 行为验证 | 状态机与协议：结构检查、对抗性探测、预算与时限、before/after 回归。多机组合查死锁，以及永不发生的会合（握手事件） | | 图 | UML 2.5 各图族的渲染、解析与建模审查（含 render→parse 往返一致性对照），覆盖 Mermaid 与 PlantUML 两种记号 | | 结构 | 组件/包/类/部署图按依赖图审计：孤立节点、悬空引用、环、矩阵与分层违规、缺失的必需边 | | 数据 | 数据模型与迁移：结构、迁移覆盖、拷贝一致性、回滚对称、前后数据回归 | | 并发 / 同步 / 异步 | 挖掘"工作怎么被执行"的断言（线程安全、锁、中断、async/await、事件循环…）并路由到能判定它的工具；它自己不证明 | | 导出 | 已验证模型导出为 UPPAAL / TLA+ / PRISM / SPIN 的输入 | | 报告 | 报告正文渲染、基线比对（`report_diff`）、哈希规范 | ## 典型用法 ### 重构 harness 重构可以改实现，不能改行为。这个判断交给引擎，不必通读 diff： 1. **重构前**：从当前代码抽出 BEFORE 模型（`uml_parse` 读已有的图，或按 schema 手写）。 2. **重构**。 3. **重构后**：抽出 AFTER 模型。 4. **回归**：`model_verify` 带 `beforeModel` 与 `stateMapping` 跑前后回归：行为是否保持、不变式是否连续、状态映射是否自洽。数据侧用 `model_datamodel_verify` 的 `beforeModel` / `fieldMapping` / `migrationMappings` 做同一件事的**数据版**。 5. **判定与留痕**：`report_diff` 拿基线报告比对。新增的 error 发现，就是这次重构不接受的理由。报告里的哈希让结论可复算。 它比较的是**你给的两份模型**，不是两份代码。每份模型是否忠实于对应代码，由第 1、3 步负责，它不代替你做。它也不读 diff、不改代码、不跑你的测试。它回答的是"行为还一样吗"，不是"重构得好不好"。 ### 代码流程审查 先把分支逻辑画成流程，再看这张图到底说了什么： 1. **抽流程**：把函数或服务里的分支写成 `LogicModelV1`，或者手画一张 `stateDiagram-v2` / PlantUML 图。 2. **读回模型**：手画的图交给 `uml_parse` 转成模型。读不动的行会变成警告，不会悄悄跳过。 3. **审查**：`uml_review` 报结构缺陷——不可达状态、死端、分支有歧义或没穷尽、自环没有出口、孤立节点、环——以及文档缺口。 4. **落回源码**：每条发现都回到代码核验。图画对了，不等于代码写对了。 它审的是你给的那张图和那份模型。图与代码是否一致，由第 1 步的抽取负责。 ### 状态机审查 把状态机建成可执行模型，让引擎去跑，而不是通读代码判断它会不会卡死： 1. **建模型**：手画的 `stateDiagram-v2` 或 PlantUML 状态图交给 `uml_parse`；也可以直接按 schema 写 `LogicModelV1`。 2. **跑检查**：`model_verify` 找的是不可达状态、吸收环、被静默忽略的事件、没有恢复路径的资源申请、预算超限，以及无法满足的时限。每一项都作为一个**带码**的发现报出，而码的前缀说明它属于哪一族。 3. **写清"永远/绝不"**：把这类断言写进 `invariants`，引擎会在全部可达状态上搜反例，并给出它找到的最短路径。 4. **落回源码**：报告里的 error 发现逐条回到代码。 并发断言分两半：**两个模型都碰同一个共享位置**这一类，由我们自己的 `model_compose_verify` 判（声明 `shared` 与 `accesses` 之后的 C3/C4/C5，包括丢更新）；源码级数据竞争、中断延迟、阻塞调用与漏掉的 `await` 仍路由到 TSan/Helgrind/CBMC/TLA+。硬实时语义（deadline、period）不在它的范围内。 ### 审计一张依赖图 组件图是关于「哪些模块可以依赖哪些」的断言。把它当图读，再问那些边是否被允许： 1. **给图**：PlantUML 的组件/包/类/部署图源码，或 Mermaid 类图。`uml_structure_verify` 把它解析成节点与边。 2. **说清什么被允许**（如果有规则）：一个含 `layers` 与 `rules` 的矩阵，每条规则点名一个 `source` 并给 `allow` / `deny` / `require`，再用 `default` 管其余。没有矩阵时，它只报结构缺陷。 3. **读发现**：孤立节点、从未声明过的端点、带最短路径的环、越过层的边、缺失的必需边，以及——一个节点都没声明时——**这份输入没有任何可审的东西**。 4. **换一种图就换个工具**：如果这张图是状态图或活动图，那是 `uml_review`，不是它。 它审的是**图**，不是代码。一张自洽的图仍可能画错了系统，所以要和源码侧扫描配对。手画的图报「标签漂移」时，`uml_explain_labels` 会打印该记号下解析器接受的标签写法。 ### 让设计对自己作出的声明负责 设计会对自己作出断言：这一层在那层之上、这个组件拥有那条依赖、这个接口比它的调用方窄。`model_design_review` 判定设计是否守住了这些承诺： 1. **把设计写成模型**：架构（节点与边），加上它声明的——分层、边界、允许与必需的边、带职责的类型、操作、转移、父类型。 2. **跑它**：`model_design_review` 报出设计与自相矛盾的地方，并**另外**报出它图的形状——环与打断环所需的最少边、承重元素、层级、扇入扇出。 3. **读那三个列表**：`violations` 决定判定；`signals` 值得一看但不使任何东西失败；`facts` 是**测量**，不是发现。`checksSkipped` 说明哪些原则因为**没声明任何可对照的东西**而没有检查。 **它从不按外部标准评判设计。** 它报的是：设计**与它自己声明的某件事**矛盾，或关于它的图的一个结构事实。问「这个设计好不好」是评审者的问题；这个工具回答的是另一个：**它就自己的说法而言，站得住吗**。 ### 两台必须互相配合的机器 一台机器**不会因为另一台**而死锁。当两个组件握手时，真正有意思的失败在**组合**里： 1. **各自建模**，然后一起给：`model_compose_verify` 收一个模型数组。 2. **点名共享事件**：如果一个握手只有在双方都就绪时才合法，把它写进 `rendezvous`。没写进去的事件只推进一台机器，所以等握手的机器可以先走任意多步自己的路。 3. **读 C1 与 C2**：一个可达节点上没有任何机器能前进、且有机器不是终止态（C1），以及一个**永远不会触发**的会合（C2）。两者都逐机给出理由，C1 还给最短反例。 模型里**没有速率比，也没有公平性约束**。单台机器自己的问题——不可达状态、不变式、成本对预算——用 `model_verify`。 ### 并发声明：挖掘并路由 「线程安全」「lock-free」「ISR 安全」都是需要某个能判定它们的工具的断言，而第一步是**把它们找出来**： 1. **扫文本**：`model_interleaving_scan` 收文档、计划或笔记，报出风险点——那条声明、共享状态、中断、临界区，以及异步的那些（`async`、`await`、`promise`、事件循环、回调）。每条发现都带 `family`（threads / synchronization / async / interrupts / shared-state），绝对式断言按 error 报。 2. **看每条绝对声明欠着什么**：「不可能有数据竞争」这类声明会被报为 error，要求**专门的**验证，且每条发现都点名能判定它的分析——竞争用 TSan 或 Helgrind，有界证明用 CBMC，协议用 TLA+，中断用 RTOS 感知的分析。 3. **去做那个分析**：本插件不运行它，也不对并发安全作任何证明。 它读的是**文本**。它看不见你的线程，而**一次干净的扫描不是健康证明**——它的含义是没找到声明，这是另一个命题。 ### 一次迁移：前后两份模型 迁移是两份模型，加一个「数据活下来了」的断言。把两份都给出去，这个断言就变成可核查的： 1. **两份模型**：改动前的 schema 与改动后的 schema，各自是含实体、字段、键与关系的数据模型。 2. **说清字段怎么走**：`fieldMapping` 从旧路径到新路径，加上 `migrationMappings`——用于来源不是它自己旧名字的字段。 3. **跑比对**：`model_datamodel_verify` 带 `beforeModel`，检查迁移覆盖、拷贝一致性、回滚对称，以及前后数据回归。 4. **读那条警告**：新 schema 里声明为 `required`、却没有任何东西供给它的字段，会报 `DS2_REQUIRED_FIELD_UNSOURCED`。它是 **warning**，所以判定停在 `pass_with_findings`——**这是一个要做的决定，不是引擎可以替你宣布的失败**。 它比较的是**你给的两份模型**。任一份是否忠实于它所描述的数据库，是抽取那一步的事，这个工具不做。 ### 图的导入与导出：设计冻结与长期迭代 这里存的是**源文件**，不是截图：`uml_render` 写出 Mermaid / PlantUML 源，`uml_parse` 把源读回模型。一份图因此能当两种东西用： - **设计冻结的留档**：把图源、模型和那一次的验证报告一起提交进仓库，作为某个时间点的设计记录。模型里可以放 `_` 前缀的元数据（单据号、日期、负责人、抽取时留下的保留意见），这些键不参与哈希，补档案信息不会改变结论的身份。 - **长期迭代的参考**：下一次改动时重新抽出模型、重跑验证，再用 `report_diff` 与冻结的那份报告比对。新增的 error 是这次改动引入的，消失的说明旧问题已经解决；哈希让"还是不是同一份模型"可判定，不必肉眼比图。 需要交给外部检查器时，同一份模型可以用 `model_export` 导出成 UPPAAL / TLA+ / PRISM / SPIN 的原生输入。 界线：它保存并比对的是**模型与图的源文件**，渲染出来的图片只是副产品。图变了模型没变、或模型变了图没变，都会在下一次解析或比对时暴露。 ## 工具 | 工具 | 做什么 | |---|---| | `uml_render` | 模型 → 图源（Mermaid / PlantUML），可指定图族。记号表达不了的视图会被拒绝，并说明理由 | | `uml_parse` | 图源 → 该图族的模型；不属于状态机/流程的族会按名拒绝，而不是硬当作状态机解析 | | `uml_review` | 审查建模：结构缺陷、文档缺口、render↔parse 往返一致性；给模型、给图，或两者对照 | | `uml_explain_labels` | 打印解析器接受的标签与注释契约，不需要图 | | `model_verify` | 状态机 / 协议的可执行验证（结构检查、对抗性探测、预算、时限、前后回归） | | `model_compose_verify` | 两台及以上机器的组合检查（死锁、永不发生的会合；声明了共享位置后还有无序写 C4 与非原子更新 C5） | | `model_datamodel_verify` | 数据模型与迁移验证 | | `model_interleaving_scan` | 并发 / 同步 / 异步声明的挖掘与路由 | | `model_export` | 导出到外部检查器（UPPAAL / TLA+ / PRISM / SPIN） | | `uml_structure_verify` | 依赖图审计（含依赖矩阵与多层级细化） | | `model_design_review` | 设计审阅：依赖图形状 + 设计自身声明的契约（分层、职责边界、可替换性、接口宽度） | | `report_diff` | 两份报告比对：新增/消失/变化的发现 | ## 怎么读报告 工具的产出是一份报告，结论只在 `verdict` 里：**看 `verdict`，不看 `ok`**。`ok` 在各族的含义不同——多数族在评审失败时仍是 `true`，组合族在出现 error 级发现时是 `false`——所以它不能当判定读；把它当判定读，会得出与报告相反的结论。 | 字段 | 说明 | |---|---| | `verdict` | 判定：`pass`、`pass_with_findings`、`fail` | | `verdictReason` | 一句话说明为什么是这个判定 | | `hashes` | `hashSpec` 与 `modelHash`；前后回归另带 `beforeModelHash`、`afterModelHash`。同一份模型永远得到同一个哈希 | | `nextSteps` | 引擎建议的下一步 | | `schema` | 报告的版本化契约，例如 `model-everything/verify/v1`。要按字段分支，就分支在它上面 | |
