See the bilingual [release notes](docs/release-v1.3.0.md), [complete PR audit](docs/release-v1.3.0-pr-audit.md), and [verification record](docs/release-v1.3.0-verification.md). ### What's new in 1.3.0 - Access native Session actions, plans and artifacts, MCP resources, Team information, schedules, timed/continued questions, and account/model information from the terminal. - Browse Host workspace files with text/binary views and available file watching. Plugins can add terminal Session actions and guarded draft input activities with undo. - Install optional Creator, Browser, or Computer companion Bundles when you need them. With the official voice-input Bundle enabled, `/speech wav` provides reviewed WAV transcription; it does not record from the microphone. - Fix current-Host preset/forms/tool-result handling, stale targets, approval display, watcher cleanup, and bounded shutdown. Keep native Harness ownership and the existing terminal workflows. The release notes also fill gaps in the `1.2.6` summary: Agent Tree navigation, semantic transcript copying, target-specific context menus, Provider configuration, VS Code theme discovery, independent appearance controls, native scrollback, and long-session rendering fixes. Those features were already shipped; the [audit](docs/release-v1.3.0-pr-audit.md) identifies their original PRs and versions. ## Interface | DeepSeek light | DeepSeek dark | | --- | --- | | ![SeekTTY DeepSeek light start screen](assets/seektty-tui.png) | ![SeekTTY DeepSeek dark start screen](assets/seektty-tui-dark.png) | | TypeScript in the light interface | Tools, file reads, and Diff in the dark interface | | --- | --- | | ![SeekTTY light TypeScript syntax highlighting](assets/seektty-code-light.png) | ![SeekTTY dark tool and Diff syntax highlighting](assets/seektty-code-dark.png) | Full mode uses a fixed alternate-screen viewport and keeps the composer and status at the bottom. Its mouse support browses history, selects text, and clicks existing controls inside SeekTTY. F3 or `/mouse native` switches while idle to terminal-native mode: SeekTTY leaves the alternate screen, writes the complete loaded conversation to ordinary terminal scrollback, disables mouse reporting, and lets the terminal or tmux own scrolling, search, and selection. Backfill is sequential and reports progress; Esc stops it without stopping the Session, while Ctrl+L refreshes only the active tail. `/transcript` opens transcript browsing and `/transcript replay` explicitly writes the available conversation again. Images use a textual attachment row in native mode. Already-written history is not recolored or reflowed by SeekTTY; the terminal owns that history. An empty session now opens with a responsive Fastfetch-style welcome page rather than sendable task suggestions. The default uses a packaged, original-color DeepSeek pixel whale plus runtime facts from the current Profile; it does **not** execute Fastfetch. The first-time API-key prompt remains higher priority and finishes before option

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-model-select-skin

给 DeepSeek Harness Web UI 的模型选择器换皮肤：胶囊芯片触发器 + 重做的下拉菜单。

## 截图

浅色主题：

![浅色主题下的模型选择器](docs/preview-light.png)

深色主题：

![深色主题下的模型选择器](docs/preview-dark.png)

## 效果

- **触发器**：胶囊芯片，含提供商彩点、`提供商 · 模型名`、思考档位标签
- **下拉菜单**：与官方弹层一致的半透明毛玻璃表面；分组标题显示提供商名 + 数量徽章
- **打开时自动定位**到当前选中的模型

## 安装

```bash
# 在 profile 的 node_modules 下软链本目录
ln -s /path/to/dsh-model-select-skin ~/.dsh/profiles/web/node_modules/@local/dsh-model-select-skin
```

随后在 `cordis.patch.yml` 中插入插件行（本仓库已自带该补丁），重启 `dsh web` 即可。

## 结构

| 文件 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `client.js` | 浏览器端：注册低优先级席位，遮蔽官方选择器 |
| `index.js` | Host 端：仅承载 bundle 身份，`apply` 为空 |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | bundle 补丁，插入插件行 |
| `locale/` | 中英文案 |
| `icon.svg` | 插件图标 |
| `docs/` | 界面截图及其生成脚本 |

## 原理

`conversation.input.model` 是单槽席位，默认由官方 `client-ui-model-selection` 占据。
本插件以 **-1 优先级**注册同一个槽位，遮蔽官方入口（最低优先级先渲染）。

数据与提交**不重新实现**：组件通过 `modelDirectories` 服务读取按会话共享的目录
（与官方选择器、`/model` 弹窗同一份存储），选择走 `directory.select()`，即
官方的 `session/selectModel` 链路。因此在任何位置做的切换都处处可见。

禁用或卸载本插件即可恢复官方 UI。

## 关于截图

上方两张图是**真实运行中的 DSH Web GUI 截图**（由 `docs/capture-screenshot.mjs`
驱动无头 Chrome 抓取），不是示意图。

脚本通过 CDP 注入一个本地自签的浏览器 cookie 来访问 `127.0.0.1:3080`，
随后展开模型下拉并裁剪到菜单区域。用法与前置条件见脚本头部注释。

plugins.description: Session cost and billing metrics for the DSH Web GUI: what this conversation cost, what the cache saved, and whether the current hour is peak or off-peak. A companion to the shipped stats pills, never a duplicate of them.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-session-metrics

Session **cost and billing** metrics for the DSH Web GUI — what this conversation cost, what the
cache saved, and whether the current hour is peak or off-peak. Built as a companion to the shipped
stats pills, never a duplicate of them.

## Why

The shipped stats pills report tokens and context, and stop short of money. That leaves three
questions unanswered, and the obvious answer to each is a lie:

**A model with no rate card is not free.** An unpriceable provider reads `unpriced` and shows its
tokens; a genuinely free model ships a card of zeros and reads a real `$0.00`. The two must not
render alike — `unpriced` means *no card*, and an unpriced pair is never rendered as a number.

**A newly integrated provider arrives silently.** DSH reports usage per provider and model; rates are
configuration. Integrate a provider before its rates are entered — the case that happened with
OpenRouter — and every figure for it is missing with nothing on the page saying why. The session
detail names the pair it observed with no card, and the tokens it used.

**Peak pricing is invisible until it is a surprise.** DeepSeek bills peak and off-peak at different
rates, in the provider's own timezone. Whether *right now* is peak is not something a user should
have to derive.

## Agent Skills

Installing the plugin registers the **`session-metrics`** skill, so an agent can explain the figures
and reconfigure the rates without reading the source. Ask it what a session cost, whether a model is
priced, or how to add a rate card for a provider it has seen.

## Quick Start

The plugin installs into your DSH **profile** by link — it is not published to npm, so the clone is
the source. Both routes end with a **restart**.

### Option A — the script

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mrdhira/dsh-session-metrics.git ~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-session-metrics
cd ~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-session-metrics
./install.sh                 # builds, registers in your profile, runs pnpm install
```

It accepts `--profile <dir>` to target a profile other than `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop`, `--check` to
report what would change without writing anything, and `--remove` to unregister.

### Option B — the manual steps

**1. Clone it somewhere stable** (this path becomes your install path):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mrdhira/dsh-session-metrics.git ~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-session-metrics
cd ~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-session-metrics
```

**2. Build it.** `pnpm install` runs the `prepare` script, which builds `lib/**` — the part DSH
actually loads. It is generated; never hand-edit it.

```bash
pnpm install
```

**3. Register it with your profile** — the dependency and the bundle name, with an absolute path:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "dsh-session-metrics": "link:/Users/<you>/.dsh/plugins/dsh-session-metrics"
  },
  "dsh": {
    "profile": {
      "bundles": [
        "dsh-session-metrics"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

**4. Install the link, then restart DSH:**

```bash
cd ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop && pnpm install
```

Nothing needs adding to `cordis.patch.yml`: the bundle declares its own Loader row.

> **Restart, don't reload.** The host half loads once per app process, so a host-side change needs a
> full quit and reopen (`⌘Q`, then reopen). A page reload does not pick it up. A client-side (UI)
> change needs the bundle toggled in the plugin manager.

### Verify it is really working

A strip should appear below the composer with `cost`, `saved` and a peak indicator. If it does not:

- `lib/v1/index.js` exists — if not, `pnpm install` did not finish building;
- the profile's `package.json` names `dsh-session-metrics` in **both** `dependencies` and
  `dsh.profile.bundles`;
- DSH was **restarted** after installing.

An `unpriced` chip means a working install with no matching rate card — not a failure. See
[Configure](#configure).

### Configure

**A fresh install needs no configuration.** Rate cards ship for `deepseek-account`,
`deepseek-official`, `netra-runtime` and `openrouter`, so the cost chip works immediately. OpenRouter
ships **only the models its own catalog marks free** (the `:free` suffix and the free-models router)
at zero rates; its paid models deliberately carry no card, because DSH reports no prices for them and
a fabricated rate is worse than a named gap.

Rates are edited in the GUI: **Plugins sidebar → `dsh-session-metrics`**. The same table can be set
in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: session-metrics
  name: dsh-session-metrics
  config:
    display: { currency: USD, primaryProvider: deepseek-account }
    budget: { sessionUsd: 5, warnAt: 0.75 }
    providers:
      - id: my-router
        models:
          - model: some/model
            rates: { flat: { cacheHit: 0.01, cacheMiss: 0.1, output: 0.25 } }
        billing: { windows: [] }      # no peak concept
```

Rates are USD per 1M tokens. A model takes **either** a `flat` row **or** a `peak` row with
`offPeak`. A provider with no `billing.windows` is flat and shows no peak chip.

> **A `providers:` list in your patch replaces the shipped cards** rather than adding to them. Pin your
> own providers and the OpenRouter free cards stop shipping with them — add a card for each pair you
> need, or let **Seen, unpriced** name the ones you missed.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `display.currency` | `USD` | `USD` or `CNY` |
| `display.primaryProvider` | — | hides the provider chip when the session uses this provider |
| `display.chips` | all | which chips to show, and in what order: `peak`, `time`, `cost`, `saved`, `provider`, `budget` |
| `budget.sessionUsd` | off | per-session ceiling; omit to disable |
| `budget.warnAt` | `0.75` | fraction of the budget at which the strip warns |

The full rate-card format, the shipped cards and the reasoning behind them are in
[`docs/pricing.md`](docs/pricing.md).

## How it Works

Costs are derived from the Host's own `tokenUsage` projection — the same source the stats pills read
— so this plugin adds interpretation, not a second ledger. Cache savings compare each cache-hit token
against the rate that would have been paid on a miss, per the card in effect. Peak and off-peak
windows resolve in the provider's own timezone, holidays included, and the countdown is computed once
a minute while the detail view is open rather than on every render.

Two surfaces, one projection:

- **the strip**, below the composer: cost, cache savings, the peak state with your local time, the
  provider when it is not your configured primary, and budget progress;
- **the detail**, on click: the cost breakdown (cache-hit / miss / write / output), cache savings and
  blended rate, the rate window with a countdown, cost per step, cost per model when a session
  switched models, and the projections each figure came from.

The plugin deliberately does **not** render session token totals, cache-hit rate, context percentage,
turns, steps or tok/s — the shipped pills own those. [`docs/data-sources.md`](docs/data-sources.md)
records which projection feeds which figure, which is what keeps the two from drifting back into
duplication.

### Requirements

- **DSH** with the Web GUI, and a profile you can edit (`~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/`).
- **Node.js 22+** and **pnpm** to build from source. The built artifact needs nothing extra at
  runtime.

### Development

```bash
pnpm install                  # deps + build (prepare)
pnpm run build                # rebuild lib/**
pnpm test                     # 111 tests: 105 pass, 6 skipped without a session log
pnpm run typecheck            # three projects: host, browser half, tests
pnpm run test:fast            # host logic only — the quick loop
pnpm run test:dom             # the UI half under jsdom
DSH_SESSION_LOG=<path>.jsonl.zstd pnpm run test:replay   # replays a real session
```

```
src/host/*.ts         host half: config schema, projection, ledger, pricing  -> lib/v1/index.js
src/client/index.cts  browser half: strip, detail panel, pricing page        -> lib/v1/client.js
types/dsh.d.ts        the DSH surfaces this plugin uses (the app ships no .d.ts)
build.mjs             esbuild: ESM host half, CJS browser half + loader h

plugins.description: Switch DSH's built-in web_search between the DeepSeek Search API (/v1/tools/search) and the default account search, with live fallback, a settings page and a sidebar switch.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-plugin-deepsearch

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-plugin-deepsearch)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-deepsearch)
[![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/github-SeaViod%2Fdsh--plugin--deepsearch-181717?logo=github)](https://github.com/SeaViod/dsh-plugin-deepsearch)

Switch DSH's built-in `web_search` between the **DeepSeek Search API** (`POST /v1/tools/search`) and DSH's default account search — with automatic fallback, a settings page, a sidebar switch and a model-facing tool.

English | [中文说明](README.zh.md)

- **ON (`deepseek-api`)** — the built-in `web_search` tool is served by the DeepSeek Search API. This is a paid API: successful requests are billed by DeepSeek; check the current pricing in your DeepSeek console before enabling it.
- **OFF (`builtin`)** — the default DSH route: server-side account search (one search consumes one model turn).
- Switching is **immediate** and survives restarts: the mode is persisted in `$DSH_HOME/deepsearch-mode.json`.
- **It never makes search unavailable.** With no key, a 401, a network error, or 429/5xx retries exhausted, the provider falls back to the previous (or another available) search provider and reports the reason in `lastError`.
- **Zero runtime dependencies** — only `node:` builtins and the global `fetch`. No build step.
- Settings page and sidebar switch are localized in **English and Chinese**.

## What it does

The plugin has two halves that work together:

| Half | File | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Host | `index.js` | Registers the model tool `deepsearch`, registers a search provider (default id `deepseek-search-api`), routes `web.searchProviderId` on/off, exposes four HTTP routes under `/deepsearch/`, and resolves the API key. |
| Browser | `client.js` | Hand-written bundle loaded through `window.__ModuleLoader__.load(...)`: the settings tab and the sidebar footer switch. |

`cordis.patch.yml` is the bundle patch: a `dsh plugin add` or plugin-market install puts the package into the profile's `node_modules` (recorded in the profile `package.json` under `dsh.profile.bundles`), and the bundle layer applies this patch at boot — you do not need to edit the profile patch by hand.

## Three entry points

| Entry point | Where | What it is for |
|---|---|---|
| Settings page | **Settings → Built-in plugins → DeepSeek Search** | switch, status details, endpoint test, API key editor |
| Sidebar switch | Footer of the left sidebar | one-click toggle that shows the current route (`API` / `builtin`) |
| Model tool | `deepsearch` (`status` / `on` / `off` / `search` / `fetch` / `check`) | toggle the route or run a search from a conversation |

## Install

### From the plugin market

Search for **dsh-plugin-deepsearch** (or "DeepSeek Search") in the DSH plugin market and install it. The storefront uses the package's `dsh.bundle.patch`, so the host half is registered automatically. After installing, the new settings tab appears under **Settings → Built-in plugins → DeepSeek Search**; a browser page reload may be needed the first time so the client bundle is picked up.

### From the command line

```pwsh
# Install into the default profile
dsh plugin add dsh-plugin-deepsearch

# Or target a profile explicitly: `web` for a `dsh web` server
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-deepsearch
```

Installing for the **Desktop app** uses the desktop profile / the in-app plugin market UI (the Desktop app keeps its profile under its own DSH home; no user-home path has to be typed by hand). The plugin's browser half declares `dsh.client.platform: "web"`, which is what the desktop shell also loads.

If you are installing from a checkout rather than the registry, `npm pack` the folder and `dsh plugin add` the resulting tarball.

### Upgrading from 0.1.x

0.1.x had no bundle patch; it was installed by hand with one insert row in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: deepsearch
      name: dsh-plugin-deepsearch
```

0.2.0 ships `dsh.bundle.patch` (`cordis.patch.yml` at the package root). A `dsh plugin add` or plugin-market install does **not** write an insert row into the profile patch: it installs the package into the profile's `node_modules`, records it in the profile's `package.json` under `dsh.profile.bundles`, and the bundle layer applies the package's own `cordis.patch.yml` at boot. **Remove the old hand-written insert row before installing 0.2.0 as a bundle** — a leftover hand-written row plus a bundle install would load the plugin twice. Mode and key files under `$DSH_HOME` are kept, so the switch state and the key file survive the upgrade.

The profile name depends on the client: use `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-deepsearch` for a `dsh web` server; the Desktop app uses the `desktop` profile and its plugin-market UI. Do not type a full profile path — let `dsh plugin` resolve it.

### Uninstall

Remove the package from the profile (or uninstall it from the plugin market). The plugin does not add other files to the profile. The state file `$DSH_HOME/deepsearch-mode.json`, the diagnostics file `$DSH_HOME/deepsearch-diag.json` and the optional key file `$DSH_HOME/deepsearch-key.txt` can be deleted, or left in place if you plan to reinstall.

## Configuration

Configuration is read from the `config` block of the plugin's entry in the profile patch, and is normalized so that invalid values fall back to the defaults instead of throwing:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: deepsearch
      name: dsh-plugin-deepsearch
      config:
        apiKeyEnv: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
        count: 8
        retryCount: 1
```

All keys are optional. The table below matches the host config schema; the `config` block is also what a bundle install can carry.

| Key | Default | Normalisation / meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `apiKey` | `''` | API key given inline. String, trimmed; empty means "unset". Not recommended: it stays in the patch file. Never echoed back by any route. |
| `apiKeyEnv` | `'DEEPSEEK_API_KEY'` | Name of the credentials reference / environment variable to resolve. Must match `/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/`, otherwise the default is used. |
| `baseURL` | `'https://api.deepseek.com'` | API base URL. Trimmed; must parse as an `http(s)` URL; trailing slashes are stripped. |
| `searchPath` | `'/v1/tools/search'` | Search endpoint path (appended to `baseURL`). Trimmed, forced to start with `/`; a `?` or `#` rejects the value; empty falls back to the default. |
| `fetchPath` | `'/v1/tools/fetch'` | Page-fetch endpoint path (same rules as `searchPath`). |
| `keyFile` | `''` | Key file for the file-based key. `''` means `$DSH_HOME/deepsearch-key.txt`; `~/...` expands to the home directory; a relative path resolves under `$DSH_HOME`; anything else is used as an absolute path. |
| `count` | `8` | Number of search results. Integer, clamped to 1..50. |
| `needContent` | `false` | Ask the search API for page content (direct `deepsearch search` calls only). Only a strict `true` enables it. |
| `timeoutMs` | `30000` | Timeout per HTTP attempt. Integer, clamped to 1000..120000. |
| `retryCount` | `1` | Extra attempts after the first one (on 408/429/5xx). Integer, clamped to 0..3. |
| `retryDelayMs` | `1200` | Delay between retry attempts. Integer, clamped to 100..10000. |
| `maxFetchChars` | `20000` | Maximum characters returned by `fetch`/the `search` tool when content is requested. Integer, clamped to 1000..200000. |
| `providerId` | `'deepseek-search-api'` | Search provider id to register. Must match `/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$/` and must not collide with an existing provider, except for the plugin's own re-registration. |
| `fallbackProvider` | `''` | Preferred fallback provider id used when switching OFF. Empty means auto-detect (the previously active provider, then the first available provider that is not ours). |
| `fallbackOnError` | `true` | When the Search API call fails, fall back to another provider. Only a strict `true` enables it. |
| `language` | `'auto'` | `auto` / `en` / `zh`. `auto` resolves from `DSH_LANGUAGE`, `DSH_LOCALE`, `LANG`, `LC_ALL` (Chinese locales map to `zh`, everything else to `en`). |
| `checkQuery` | `'DeepSeek'` | Query used by the "tes

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin: dispatch work to DSH agents from Claude Code / Codex — native subagent progress, in-host worker sessions with per-tier presets, and a multimodal bridge that lends the text-only harness vision and image generation.
plugins.readme_text:
DSH Crew

A DeepSeek Harness plugin: dispatch work to DSH agents from Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok, without giving up the host's native subagent UI.
Native Progress UI • Tier Policy & Escalation • Dispatch Guardrails • Jobs Board • In-Host DSH Sessions • Vision & Image Gen (Native-First) • One-Click Install

npm: @zseven-w/dsh-crew · Current plugin release: 0.1.0-rc.11 · Tested with DSH 0.1.1-rc.1

English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Français · Español · Deutsch · Português · Русский · हिन्दी · Türkçe · ไทย · Tiếng Việt · Bahasa Indonesia


The DSH Crew settings page — host integrations, dispatch policy, execution and the multimodal bridge

## Why DSH Crew DSH Crew is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) — an open-source agent harness. It makes DSH agents dispatchable from Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and Grok: the orchestrator keeps its own model, the work runs on a real DSH agent with that harness's tools, sandbox, presets and session history, and the host still shows it as a native subagent with live progress. What runs the work is a DSH agent, not a bare model call. Tiers (`flash` / `pro`) select how much capability that agent gets from the harness's configured roster — DeepSeek V4 Flash and V4 Pro today — so a change of model in DSH needs no change here.
### 🧵 Native Progress UI Workers appear as regular subagents in Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok — dispatch count, running step, tool calls and token usage all show up in the host's own task panel, plus a claude-hud statusline segment: `⚙dsh 1▶pro 2m14s 21.7k/606 ✓3`. ### 🎚️ Tier Policy and Escalation `flash` for mechanical work, `pro` for reasoning, `effort` from `off` to `max`. `tier_policy` can clamp every dispatch to one tier at the tool layer, and `escalate_on_failure` retries a failed flash run once on pro — based on evidence, not on guessing difficulty up front.
### 🏛️ In-Host DSH Sessions With the bundle installed in a DSH profile, each worker is a first-class DSH session: visible in the Web UI, grouped by working directory, mounted with the Agent preset you choose per tier. Without DSH running, dispatch falls back to a standalone DSH runtime, so CI and headless environments still work. ### 👁️ Vision and Image Generation DSH's models are text-only. `describe_image` now prefers DeepSeek's own VL model (`deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`) whenever a key is available, then falls back to the CLIs you already have — Claude, Codex, Grok, Antigravity — or any OpenAI-compatible API you configure. `generate_image` borrows the same CLIs' brush. Pasted images stay visible in the conversation and reach the model as text.
### 🛡️ Dispatch Guardrails Every dispatch is checked before anything spawns. Worker→worker nesting is capped at origin-chain depth 3 and cycles are refused; a second worker on a workspace another job already holds is refused with the holder's info — never silently queued. Refusals are readable errors: wait or re-scope, don't bypass. ### 📋 Jobs Board The DSH Crew panel doubles as a jobs board: every worker job — running or finished — is listed with tier, effort, live progress and tokens, held workspaces show their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (e.g. a hub restart) is surfaced as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.
### 🔌 Custom Providers Bring your own endpoint (Base URL + API key + models) or a local command template. Each provider has a connectivity test that checks reachability and auth, then makes one real vision call so you find out now, not mid-task. ### 📦 One-Click Install The settings page installs and updates the Claude Code plugin, the Codex role files and the Antigravity / Grok agents, skills and commands for you — marketplace registration, permission allowlist, HUD wiring, absolute paths rendered for this machine — and restores them just as easily. Every settings file is backed up first.
## How it works ``` Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok (orchestrator, keeps its own model) └─ ds-flash / ds-pro ← native subagent shell (progress shows in the host's task UI) └─ MCP: dsh_run_worker(tier, effort, cwd, worker=) ├─ worker="agy"/"grok" → that external CLI runs the task (explicit opt-in) ├─ hub reachable → session inside DSH (visible in the Web UI, grouped by cwd) └─ otherwise → dsh-jsonrpc-agent runtime (worker.cordis.yml) └─ DeepSeek V4 Flash / Pro (DSH SDK, event stream → progress and token stats) ``` ## One run, two views Dispatch fans out. Below, eighteen workers translate this README in parallel: the host counts them as its own subagents, while the harness runs them as real sessions.

Claude Code sees dsh-crew workers as native subagents, with a statusline segment tracking running tiers, elapsed time and tokens.

The DSH Crew panel sees the same run from the harness side: which host dispatched each job, its tier and effort, live progress and token usage.

The panel is also the jobs board: running and finished jobs stay listed with tier, progress and tokens, held workspaces name their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (a hub restart) surfaces as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.

## Install Install into a DSH profile from npm: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add @zseven-w/dsh-crew@latest dsh web ``` Or, for local development straight from the source tree: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-crew dsh web ``` The `link:` protocol symlinks the profile dependency to this repository, so rebuilds are visible immediately. ### Configure DeepSeek credentials (standalone only) In hub mode — the installation above — workers run inside the DSH instance and use the DeepSeek credentials it is already configured with. Nothing else to set up. Only the standalone fallback needs a key of its own: dispatching from a host with no DSH instance running launches a worker runtime as a separate process. Obtain an API key from [platform.deepseek.com](https://platform.deepseek.com) and write it to `~/.config/dsh-crew/.env`: ``` DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-... ``` ### Verify ```bash node scripts/smoke.mjs ``` The smoke test dispatches one cheap job through whichever path is available — the hub when a DSH instance is running, s

plugins.description: Edit and mix speech, music, and sound effects in one shared editor session.
plugins.readme_text:
# SoundCraft Use

## Plugin marketplaces

This plugin belongs to **AIGC content creation**.

| Category | Marketplace | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full-stack development | [Full Stack Plugins](https://github.com/partme-ai/full-stack-plugins) | Architecture and UI design, code understanding, quality checks, code review, workflow governance, and server operations |
| AIGC content creation | [Full AIGC Plugins](https://github.com/partme-ai/full-aigc-plugins) | Image, video, audio, music, 3D, and multimodal content creation |

![SoundCraft Use — audio editing with verified artifacts](assets/official-logo.png)

> Edit speech, music, and sound effects in one shared editor session, with explicit tracks, sample ranges, and checks that survive save and reopen.

[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-0.1.0--dev.20261019.1-1A73E8)](#positioning)
[![Skills](https://img.shields.io/badge/skills-10-00A67E)](#skills)
[![MCP servers](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP%20servers-1-6E56CF)](#mcp-tools)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-green)](LICENSE)

[English](README.md) | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [Install](#installation) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Skills](#skills) · [MCP tools](#mcp-tools) · [Limits](#troubleshooting)

## Positioning

`soundcraft` lets an agent work on audio the way an editor does: inspect the session, select real tracks and clips, cut, fade, level, mix, export, then reopen the project and check what actually changed. It wraps the native SoundCraft engine and CLI in ten skills and one embedded editor, and keeps native execution, host rendering, and listening acceptance as separate claims.

This is an installable development candidate. Production promotion is blocked, the package is recorded as local-unreleased, and the recorded technical regressions use synthetic signals rather than a full creative acceptance.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Plugin ID | `soundcraft` |
| Display name | SoundCraft Use |
| Version | `0.1.0-dev.20261018.5` |
| Stage | Installable development candidate, production promotion blocked |
| Native engine | SoundCraft 0.7.0 via `soundcraft-cli` |
| Marketplace | `soundcraft-marketplace` |
| License | Apache-2.0 |

## Installation

### Prerequisites

- Codex is the host with recorded same-session evidence. Other hosts are not accepted.
- Node.js 24 or newer is required by the embedded editor. The distributed package already contains the editor build; no Rust toolchain and no `npm install` are needed at runtime.
- Native file workflows use `soundcraft-cli`, which is not installed by this plugin. Query the actual version and command schema before running a recipe.
- The first Git-based launch needs network access or an existing verified editor cache. Complete release ZIPs can start offline from bundled assets.
- Source builds additionally need the project JavaScript dependencies, the Rust `wasm32` target, and a `wasm-bindgen` CLI matching `Cargo.lock`.

### From the plugin marketplace

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add partme-ai/full-aigc-plugins
codex plugin add soundcraft@full-aigc-plugins
```

The repository also ships its own marketplace metadata (`soundcraft-marketplace`) pinned to `v0.1.0-dev.20261018.5`. Restart the host, open a new task, and ask for a read-only session inspection first.

## Quick start

1. Open the editor with an absolute workspace path: “Open SoundCraft for this folder and show me the current session.”
2. Wait for `editor_status` to report `attached: true` before editing. A successful tool response does not mean the page has rendered.
3. Work from real object IDs. Ask for one bounded operation, such as “on the Voice track, split at 2 seconds and add a 50 ms complementary linear crossfade”.
4. Save the project, reopen it in a new process, and re-inspect. Then bounce the mix and check the decoded audio rather than the dialog text.

```text
Inspect: List tracks, clips, sample rate, and any selection I should not reuse.
Edit: Cut the Voice clip at 2 s and crossfade 50 ms on both sides.
Level: Match two speakers to the same perceived level without clipping.
Deliver: Bounce a 48 kHz 24-bit WAV and confirm its length and format.
```

Direct CLI form for file tasks, using one argv argument per method:

```bash
soundcraft-cli info input.wav
soundcraft-cli run --in session.scraft --cmd 'session.inspect={"detail":"full"}' --save out.scraft
```

## What you can build

| Workflow | Built-in path | Verifiable output |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Clean up a podcast episode | `soundcraft-podcast-cleanup` | Edited speech, pauses, and loudness with a reopened project |
| Mix voice over music | `soundcraft-voice-over-mix` | Dialogue clarity and music bed checked as separate tracks |
| Level multiple speakers | `soundcraft-dialogue-leveling` | Per-speaker gain decisions and a clip-level recheck |
| Cut and join audio | `soundcraft-audio-edit` | Trim, join, and fades verified against source offsets |
| Shape a music demo | `soundcraft-music-demo` | Track balance, pan, and basic effects on editable clips |
| Deliver a format | `soundcraft-audio-delivery` | Sample rate, bit depth, naming, and decoded output |
| Preserve sync while gating silence | `soundcraft-voice-silence-gaps` | Visible gaps with later speech still on the original timeline |
| Repeat a short sound exactly | `soundcraft-finite-audio-loop` | Exact total count, sample length, and seam check |
| Work from a playbook | `soundcraft-scenario-playbooks` | Eight recipes with real methods, parameters, and checks |

## Skills

### Session and playbooks

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `soundcraft-editor` | Open the real editor in an MCP Apps host or host browser and share one workspace session |
| `soundcraft-scenario-playbooks` | Eight recipes for voice level, cut fades, interview quotes, stem delivery, reversed effects, DC offset, and polarity |

### Speech production

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `soundcraft-podcast-cleanup` | Edit spoken content, pauses, and loudness for a podcast episode |
| `soundcraft-voice-over-mix` | Balance narration against a music bed without losing intelligibility |
| `soundcraft-dialogue-leveling` | Unify level and tonal continuity across several speakers |

### Editing and delivery

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `soundcraft-audio-edit` | Trim, join, and fade clips while checking source offsets |
| `soundcraft-music-demo` | Balance multiple tracks, set pan, and apply basic effects |
| `soundcraft-audio-delivery` | Choose sample rate and bit depth, name files, and verify the export |

### Timeline utilities

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `soundcraft-voice-silence-gaps` | Turn long low-level regions into visible gaps without shifting later dialogue |
| `soundcraft-finite-audio-loop` | Repeat a short checked sound an exact number of times and expand it later |

## MCP tools

`.codex-plugin/mcp.json` starts one stdio server, `soundcraft-editor`, from `ui/bootstrap.mjs`. The adapter adds three stable tools and passes through the pinned engine's command catalog.

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `open_editor` | Open the editor for an absolute `workspace`; the first call binds the workspace |
| `open_browser_editor` | Return an `editorUrl` for the same session when the host has a built-in browser |
| `editor_status` | Report whether the editor actually attached and is ready to accept edits |

Inside the session, the engine catalog in `ui/catalog.lock.json` provides `list_commands`, the `execute` wrapper, batch execution, session open/save, audio import, mix bounce, and UI automation tools. Query the live schema before calling; the skill recipes show the wrapper as `execute {"command":"…","params":{…}}`.

## Configuration

| Setting | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` | Expanded by the portable `plugin.json` and `mcp.json` |
| `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` | Expanded by the Claude Code manifest and root `.mcp.json` |
| `CRAFT_EDITOR_UPDATE=off` | Use the bundled editor only and skip the update query |
| `CRAFT_EDITOR_CACHE_DIR` | Alternate absolute cache directory; default is `~/.cache/full-aigc/editors` |
| `CRAFT_WORKSPACE_ROOT` | Workspace root when the adapt

plugins.description: A portable memory protocol for AI agents — load it as standing rules; a curation discipline + reference spec + optional cap hook.
plugins.readme_text:
**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

# Engramory

[![CI](https://github.com/tinqiao-oss/engramory/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/tinqiao-oss/engramory/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Python 3.9+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.9%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/)

**An opinionated, zero-infrastructure memory *protocol* for small-scale, local,
file-based agent memory** — a strict curation discipline plus a validator
(`tools/engramory_doctor.py`), loaded as **standing rules** (`CLAUDE.md` /
`AGENTS.md` / your host's rules file). It is not a database, a framework, or a
relevance-loaded skill. Memory is a folder of small, human-readable markdown files
plus one always-loaded index. No database, no embeddings, no server — just
plain-text files you can open, read, edit, and diff in any editor (the live store
itself stays git-ignored).

> *Engramory* — coined from *engram* (the physical trace a memory leaves in the
> brain) + *memory*. Here: one file = one fact.

> ⚠️ **Unrelated projects share this name.** *engram + memory* is an obvious
> coinage and at least one other repository arrived at it independently. This
> project is only ever `tinqiao-oss/engramory` (npm: `dsh-engramory`); a same-named
> repo under a different owner is not a fork, a mirror, or a newer version of it.

> 🤖 **Are you an AI agent, asked to install or check this?** Start at
> **[AGENT-SETUP.md](AGENT-SETUP.md)**, not at the install steps below. It is the
> procedure for working out what your host can actually enforce, whether a store
> already exists, what you must not touch, and what to tell the user — the parts
> agents reliably get wrong when improvising.

> **Status: 0.12.1 — experimental.** The hard index cap (a `PreToolUse` hook) is
> deterministic for the matched direct-edit tools (`Edit | Write | MultiEdit`) but
> NOT a global write guard (shell tools — Bash, PowerShell, a background Monitor
> command — plus MCP file tools, external editors, and sync clients bypass it);
> the discipline loads as standing rules the model follows, so it's
> best-effort, not guaranteed on every task (see [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) §8). Assumes a
> single writer / serialized writes. Don't rely on it as a "mandatory, reliable,
> cross-agent" memory layer yet.

---

## What this is — and is NOT

Engramory is **not a new memory architecture**. The "markdown files + a small index
loaded into context + the model curates it" pattern is now the mainstream shape
for agent memory, and it ships in several places already. Engramory stands on:

- **Claude Code native auto-memory** — the same markdown-`MEMORY.md`-index +
  lazy detail-file pattern; its system prompt even uses the same
  `user | feedback | project | reference` type vocabulary (per
  [anthropics/claude-code#58840](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/58840);
  the *public docs* describe only the index + topic files). Engramory is a
  disciplined superset of this default.
- **[basic-memory](https://github.com/basicmachines-co/basic-memory)** — markdown
  source-of-truth, YAML frontmatter `type`, `[[wikilink]]` graph, local-first.
- **[obsidian-second-brain](https://github.com/eugeniughelbur/obsidian-second-brain)**,
  **[claude-memory-compiler](https://github.com/coleam00/claude-memory-compiler)**
  ("a loaded index beats vector search at personal scale"), and the broader family
  of markdown-memory skills.

What Engramory contributes is the **opinionated bundle + the discipline**, not the
primitives. Do not claim novelty on markdown, frontmatter, wikilinks, a loaded
index, one-file-per-fact notes, or curation hygiene — all are prior art.

## What's actually differentiated

1. **A role/purpose ontology, headed by `feedback` = procedural memory.** The
   semantic / episodic / **procedural** split is established prior art — the CoALA
   taxonomy, and a named procedural type in LangMem and mem0 — so Engramory does not
   claim the category. What it does is make procedural `feedback` the *spine* of a
   deliberately tiny, hand-authored, human-readable set, with required **Why:** /
   **How to apply:** lines, instead of auto-extracting it into a vector/graph store.
   The contribution is the packaging and discipline, not the ontology.

2. **The curation contract as concrete behaviour** the protocol applies (model-followed, not a hard gate): dedup-before-write,
   update-don't-duplicate, delete-when-wrong, and a negative-scope rule ("don't
   store what git/CLAUDE.md/the code already records"). Surveys consistently name
   *modify/delete/forget* as the most under-implemented memory operation — Engramory
   makes it the spine.

3. **A bounded index designed not to silently rot.** The index loads every session and
   Claude Code reads the first 200 lines / 25 KB (documented behavior), so an unbounded index silently
   drops memories off the end. Engramory warns at 150 lines / 20 KB, compacts-or-asks
   before 200 / 25 KB, and ships a hard `PreToolUse` hook backstop (it blocks only
   *growth* past the cap — shrinking/compaction edits always pass). Both the line and
   byte caps apply — whichever is hit first triggers (an index can be under the line
   count yet over on bytes when the lines run long).

   Claude Code has since followed up on this natively: v2.1.186 (released
   2026-06-22) reminds the agent to compact the index when it nears the cap, and
   v2.1.210 (released 2026-07-14) turned an over-cap write into an explicit error
   instead of a silent truncation. Both are after-the-fact alerts, though — the
   write still lands, and entries past the cap stay invisible until someone
   compacts. Engramory's hook denies the write *before* it happens, so a write
   through the matched edit tools never leaves the index over-cap in the first
   place (writes outside them — a shell, an MCP file tool — are not gated; see the
   status note above and SKILL.md §8). The native alerts validate the direction
   and make a welcome second layer — and older versions and other hosts still
   have neither.

## How it compares

| | storage | recall | human-readable | typed ontology | curation discipline | bounded index | infra |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Engramory** | md files | loaded index → open file | ✅ | ✅ role-based (4) | ✅ contract (model-run) | ✅ 150/200 + hook | none |
| CC auto-memory | md files | loaded index → open file | ✅ | ✅ same 4 types | partial (auto) | ~200-line window* | none (built-in) |
| basic-memory | md + SQLite | semantic/FTS search | ✅ | ✅ freeform type | schema + overwrite checks | ❌ (no loaded index) | SQLite + embeddings |
| obsidian-second-brain | md vault | index-first + search | ✅ | folder-typed | ✅ reconcile/lint | partial | none |
| mem0 / Zep | vector/graph DB | semantic | ❌ (DB) | typed (prefs/episodic/proc.; Zep custom) | auto-extract | n/a | DB + embeddings |
| [agentmemory](https://github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory) | SQLite + vector index (+opt. graph) | hybrid BM25+vector (+opt. graph), RRF | ❌ (DB/engine) | ✅ 4-tier lifecycle (work./epis./sem./proc.) | auto (capture + dedup + decay) | n/a | iii engine (local) + opt. embeddings |

Engramory's lane: **minimalism + actionable role typing + curation discipline, zero
infra.** It does *not* try to out-search basic-memory, out-scale mem0, or
out-capture agentmemory — those solve a different problem (auto-capture /
auto-ingest at volume) at a different cost point. agentmemory is the closest
heavyweight foil: also local-first, but it bets on automatic capture (lifecycle
hooks) + hybrid retrieval (BM25 + vectors + optional graph) on a SQLite/`iii`
engine, where Engramory bets on hand-curation + a tiny always-loaded index and
ships no engine at all.

\* Claude Code's [memory docs](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/memory)
document this exactly: *"the first 200 lines of `MEMORY.md`, or the first 25KB,
whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation."* Other hosts
vary, so the window stays configurable via the hook's env vars.

# dsh-multi-agent-gateway

**Free Token —— 把各平台的免费额度，装进 DSH 的模型选择器。**

一个插件管起所有「AI Agent 平台」的账号：统一账号管理、每日签到、额度/积分拉取、
多账号智能路由；把各平台的模型**按平台分组**上报到 DSH 对话框的**原生模型选择器**，
并在每个模型名后标注**积分消耗倍率**。六个平台的适配器**已全部实现**。

不是独立 Nginx，也不是外部代理进程 —— 请求全部在插件内部转发，账号凭证只存在本机。
（本地 OpenAI 兼容网关属于**后续计划**，见[路线图](#路线图)。）

## 理念：Free Token

各平台为了拉新，会持续放出免费额度：OpenCode 的匿名免费层、Qoder / WorkBuddy 的
每日签到积分、Trae 的赠送额度……这些「免费 token」分散在六个客户端里，每个都要单独
登录、单独签到、单独查余额，最后往往是**放着过期**。

这个插件的立场很简单：

- **免费额度不该被浪费，也不该被平台 UI 绑架** —— 账号收进来、模型接进 DSH、
  签到与额度查询自动跑；
- **默认不烧钱** —— 模型默认一个都不勾，勾选并保存后才出现在选择器里
  （见 [`docs/MODELS.md`](docs/MODELS.md) §6.5），避免「白嫖」变成「意外扣费」；
- **福利跟进是长期承诺** —— 哪个平台出了新的免费模型或签到活动，适配器就跟着更新。
  各平台接口并不公开，我们坚持逐个真机验证，而不是照抄文档。

> 一句话：**能白拿的 token，一个都别浪费；拿不到的时候，我们自己写适配器。**


## 界面：五页 + 浏览器登录

设置页现在是**独立一页**（设置 → 多 Agent 网关），内部按「你此刻要回答的问题」分五页：

| 页 | 回答什么问题 |
|---|---|
| **总览** | 现在健康吗？刚才那条花了多少？ |
| **账号** | 这个平台有哪些账号 / 模型？ |
| **任务** | 签到和活动任务跑得怎么样？ |
| **日志** | 刚才那次为什么失败？ |
| **设置** | 那些不常动的东西（含版本更新） |

**添加账号不用手抄 token**：账号页点「打开登录页」→ 浏览器里完成平台登录 → 回来稍等
几秒（会自动轮询），或点「刷新登录状态」→ 插件自己去换 token 并建账号
（token 不经过浏览器，加密落盘）。

| 平台 | 登录形态 |
|---|---|
| OpenCode | 设备码（显示 user_code，前端自动轮询） |
| WorkBuddy / 国际版 | 外链（`auth/state` → 打开登录页 → `auth/token?state=`） |
| Qoder / Qoder CN | 设备码 + PKCE |

> 两种形态都会**自动轮询**（3～5 秒一次）：浏览器里授权完成后回来即可看到变绿；
> 「刷新登录状态」只是手动补充入口，不是必点步骤。

**模型表**按「免费 → 厂商 → 倍率」排序，**默认一个都不勾** —— 勾选并「保存并生效」
之后才进选择器；还没勾过时可以点「按推荐预选」（OpenCode 推免费，其余平台推全部）。
每行可单独改上下文长度、可单独「测一次」，状态列显示 可用 / 地区受限 / 不可用 / 未探测。
上游声明了思考档位的模型，选择器里还能选 `off / low / medium / high…`。

## 它解决什么

| 你现在的麻烦 | 这个插件怎么办 |
|---|---|
| 有五六个平台、十几个账号，每个平台一套登录/签到/查额度 | 一个配置页全管起来，按平台分组 |
| 某个号限流了 / 额度用完了，会话当场报错 | 同 Agent 内自动换号重试，用户无感 |
| 每天要手动去点签到、领活动任务积分 | 定时任务自动跑，流水可查 |
| 模型下拉里一堆同名模型，看不出哪个贵 | 按 Agent 分组，后面缀 `(×2)` / `(免费)` |

## 支持情况

六个平台的适配器**全部实现**，没有一个是「占位骨架」：

| Agent | 签到 | 额度 | 模型目录 | 对话 | 备注 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **OpenCode** | 上游无 / 可配 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ 流式 + 思维链 | 匿名免费层零凭证可用；签到接口可填 `checkInPath` |
| **Qoder** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | 签到 `/sash/api/v1/me/campaigns`、额度 `/sash/api/v2/me/usage` |
| **Qoder CN** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | 同上，独立产品线与账号体系 |
| **WorkBuddy** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | 签到 + 余额 + 会话头校验 |
| **WorkBuddy 国际版** | 上游无 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | 上游确实没有签到接口，如实回报「不支持」 |
| **Trae** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ 流式 | 协议层已实现，**默认隐藏**（尚未真机验证），显式配置后可启用 |

> **关于签到与活动任务**：opencode.ai 官方 Console 没有签到接口，国内反代平台则常见
> 「签到 + 活动任务」形态。所以本插件把接口路径做成**可配置**的：填了
> `upstream.checkInPath` / `tasksPath` 就真去调；没填就明确回报「上游没有这个接口
> （这不是故障）」，**绝不伪造签到结果**。详见 [`docs/OPENCODE-API.md`](docs/OPENCODE-API.md)。

### 「免费模型不要 key」——对，插件做到了**一个字段都不用填**

**不登录、不填 API key、不填凭证** —— 账号卡片里只填一个标签就完事，
模型选择器里选 `OpenCode · xxx (免费)` 直接聊。

为什么以前会 403、现在能过：上游那句 `FreeTierError`（*"can only be used from
within OpenCode"*）是**营销话术**，它实际校验的是**请求形状**。消融实验实测出来的
**过门三件事**：

| 条件 | 去掉会怎样 |
|---|---|
| `stream: true` | **403** —— 免费层只接受流式 |
| 请求里有一个叫 `read` 的工具 | **403** |
| 规范的 `x-opencode-session`（`ses_…` 降序编码） | **403** |

其余（`Authorization`、`x-opencode-request`、`x-opencode-project`）**去掉照样过**。

插件在「账号没有 key」时自动补齐这三样（`upstream.freeTierMode: 'auto'` 默认值），
`stream: true` 本来就是它的固定行为，`read` 工具 DSH 本来就发 —— 所以是真的零配置。
机制细节、实测报文、消融表见 [`docs/OPENCODE-API.md`](docs/OPENCODE-API.md) §1.5–1.6。

**实测证据**（`npm run test:free`）：空凭证账号 → 200 → 正文「收到」+
`reasoning_content` + usage，**全程没有任何 key**。

**边界**：匿名通道**只对免费模型有效**；付费模型在它上面会直接
`401 Missing API key`。要用付费模型就走登录/API key。上游随时可能再改门禁 ——
被拒时错误信息会把那三件事列出来，不会让你瞎试。

**另外**：模型目录完全免凭证，所以模型选择器里的分组与倍率
**一个账号都不加也能显示**，只是发不出请求。

**Trae 为什么默认隐藏**：适配器本身是能跑的（协议层、签到、余额、流式对话都实现了），
但本机没有 Trae 账号、没有一次真上游验证 —— 露出来只会让你点到一个没验证过的东西。
真机验证通过后，把 `trae` 加进 `src/config.ts` 的 `DEFAULT_VISIBLE_AGENTS` 即可显示，
别处不用改。

**扩展方法**见 [`docs/EXTENDING.md`](docs/EXTENDING.md)：新增一个平台只需加一个适配器
文件 + 在 `adapters/index.ts` 加一行，核心调度一行都不用改。

## 路线图

| 方向 | 说明 | 状态 |
|---|---|---|
| **新平台 / 新福利跟进** | 哪个平台放出新的免费模型、签到活动或赠送额度，就补对应适配器；接口以真机验证为准 | 持续进行 |
| **本地 OpenAI 兼容网关** | 增加本地端点（`POST /v1/chat/completions`、`GET /v1/models`），让 Cursor / VS Code / 任意 OpenAI SDK 也能用上这些账号与免费模型；端口可配、默认只绑 `127.0.0.1` | 规划中，未发布 |
| 界面与可用性 | 五页设置界面 + 左侧导航入口，继续打磨 | 持续进行 |

> 现阶段它是 **DSH 插件**，不是独立服务：请求由宿主进程调进来、在进程内转发。
> 等网关功能落地后，才会额外暴露一个可被外部客户端直连的端点。

## 架构（分层模块化）

```
                        ┌──────────────────────── DSH ────────────────────────┐
   对话请求 ──▶ ctx.llm ──▶ src/llm/adapter.ts（每 Agent 一个 provider 路由）
                        │            │                                    │
                        │            ▼                                    │
   模型选择器 ◀───────────│  src/runtime.ts（总装：模型缓存 / 分组 / 倍率标签）   │
                        │            │                                    │
   客户端配置页 ◀─ src/remote.ts ─┼─▶ core/router.ts  多账号路由（换号/降权/恢复）│
                        │            ├─▶ core/scheduler.ts 定时任务管理器    │
                        │            ├─▶ core/tasks.ts  活动任务引擎         │
                        │            └─▶ core/accounts.ts 账号（AES-256-GCM）│
                        │                       │                          │
                        │                       ▼                          │
   工具 ◀────────────────┘            src/adapters/*.ts（每 Agent 一个适配器） │
                        └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**新增 Agent 只需要在 `src/adapters/` 加一个文件 + 在 `adapters/index.ts` 加一行。**
核心调度（路由 / 定时 / 任务 / 网关 / UI）一行都不用改。

## 数据落在哪

默认 `<DSH_HOME>/multi-agent-gateway`（`DSH_HOME` 一般是 `~/.dsh`）：

| 文件 | 内容 | 丢了会怎样 |
|---|---|---|
| `.master-key` | AES-256-GCM 主密钥（0600） | **账号密文再也解不开**，要重录 |
| `accounts.enc.json` | 账号与凭证（整份加密） | 要重录账号 |
| `state.json` | 额度缓存、健康、模型缓存、任务游标（明文、无敏感信息） | 重算，无损失 |
| `task-log.jsonl` | 任务执行流水（可删） | 历史记录没了 |

**安全边界（说清楚，不吹）**：密文与密钥分文件，防的是「配置被云同步 / 被 grep 到明文
token / 备份泄露」。它**不是硬件密钥库** —— 能读该目录的本机进程同样能读密钥。

## 开发

```powershell
node scripts/build.mjs      # TypeScript → lib/（零依赖，用 Node 自带的类型擦除）
npm test                    # 宿主测试 478 + 客户端契约 63 + 冒烟
node test/live-opencode.mjs # 真机管线：打真实 OpenCode 目录核倍率（需要联网，只读公开接口）
```

改完 `src/` **必须重新构建**（`lib/` 是产物）；改完 `client/` 也要重跑构建，
然后重启 DSH（宿主在启动时扫描 `dsh.client` 声明）。

|---|---|
| `node scripts/build.mjs` | 54 个 TS 文件 → `lib/`，零不可擦除语法 |
| 宿主测试（`npm test`） | **478/478** 通过（核心 + 六个适配器 + 推理档位 + 签到记账 + 额度刷新 + 日志采样） |
| 客户端契约测试 | **63/63** 通过（端点、描述符、volatile 路径、真 `apply(ctx)`、**无参端点零参数**、真渲染 ModelList、登录弹框五态） |
| 假宿主冒烟 | 通过（provider 路由 / 5 个工具 / **模型上报策略真的改变选择器内容** / 密文落盘） |

| 真机管线（`npm run test:live`，联网） | 真实模型目录 + 倍率；设备码登录实测发起成功、未授权正确返回 `pending` |
| 真实 DSH 进程（headless profile） | 通过（**零 `did not activate`、零配置校验错误**） |
| **真实浏览器**（Edge + 真 web profile） | 通过 —— 客户端 bundle 在 boot combo 里、`apply` 正常激活、控制台零本插件错误 |

### 模型不是全塞进去：**默认一个都不报**

上游实测 85 个模型，全进下拉的话免费那几个会被淹没。所以每个 Agent 有一份上报策略
（设置页里是三个按钮 + 一个带搜索的勾选列表）：`selected`（默认，**不勾不报**）/
`free` / `all`。勾选只是草稿，点「保存并生效」才真正写配置并重发 provider。
详见 [`docs/MODELS.md`](docs/MODELS.md) §6.5。

# @hitzhangjie/dsh-plugin-session-delete

DeepSeek Harness 只提供「归档」:归档的会话永远留在磁盘上。这个插件补上缺失的那一步——**真正彻底删除一个会话**,入口在侧栏会话行的 `...` 菜单里。

一个 DSH **bundle**(声明了 `dsh.bundle.patch`),所以 `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add <path>` 安装后会被自动选入 profile 层,不需要手写 `cordis.patch.yml` 行。

---

## 功能

- **侧栏会话菜单项**:`sidebar.workspaces.session.menu.item` 槽位里的红色「删除会话…」,和内置的 置顶 / 重命名 / Fork / 归档 用同一套 `MenuItemButton` 呈现。
- **两步确认**:第一次点击把标签变成「确认永久删除「<标题>」?」,5 秒不确认自动复位;第二次点击才真正删除。悬停的提示文字也说明了后果。
- **先停活**:删除前通过归档的 `stopActivity` 瀑布停止运行中的工作(durable archive 集合会挡住这些停止所引发的任何唤醒),再等会话落盘安静后继续。
- **拒绝仍有 fork 子会话的会话**:子会话的 header 里记着父 id,删掉父会话会让这条血缘悬空,所以直接拒绝并把子会话 id 返回给界面。
- **本地零残留**,按顺序清理:
  1. 事件日志目录 `<persistence root>/<projectKey>/<sessionId>/`(先按 header 的 cwd 精确算路径,再扫描 session root 兜底)
  2. 投影缓存 `<home>/storages/session_projcache/sessions/<id>.json`
  3. 会话的 spill 目录 `<tmp>/dsh-spill-*/session-<sha256(id)[:12]>/`
  4. 工作区记账 `Workspace.detachSession(id)`
  5. 归档 / 置顶集合中的该 id
  6. 活的 store 条目(如果 store 暴露了 detach)
- **立即从侧栏消失**:删除成功后宿主发出 `api-session/removed`,同时浏览器半区调用客户端 `sessions.refresh()` 重新拉取权威列表——冷会话(本次进程没打开过)不会发出任何 disposal 帧,只有重新拉取才能让它的行消失。
- **写者占用时不留半成品**:文件仍被活的写句柄占住时,id 会记入 `<home>/plugins/session-delete.pending.json`,下次启动(此时所有会话都是冷的)自动补删。

## 安装

```powershell
# 1) 检出
git clone https://github.com/hitzhangjie/dsh-plugin-session-delete.git

# 2) 装进你使用的 profile(桌面版 Harness 固定使用保留 profile desktop)
dsh plugin --profile desktop add "file:<仓库所在路径>/dsh-plugin-session-delete"
```

`dsh plugin` 用的是桌面安装自带的那套运行时,它有权管理 `desktop` profile;npm 全局安装的 CLI 会拒绝针对 desktop 的启动与管理请求。

然后完全退出并重启 Harness。Bundle 的 patch 会把行插进 profile 树:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: hitzhangjie-session-delete
      name: '@hitzhangjie/dsh-plugin-session-delete'
```

> 行名必须是**裸包名**:`dsh-client-modules` 只把包的浏览器半区挂到「模块说明符正好是裸包名」的 Loader 行上,而 profile 解析层负责把裸包名解析到 profile 自己的 `node_modules`。写成相对路径(`./lib/index.js`)只会加载宿主半区,菜单项不会出现。

## 架构

| 半边 | 文件 | 作用 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Host | `lib/index.js` | 注册 loopback 精确路由 `POST /api/hitzhangjie/session-delete`,校验请求来源后执行整套删除。profile 插件没有 `harness.handle` / `host.call` 通道,所以浏览器半区用同源 `fetch` 调这个路由。 |
| Client | `lib/client.js` | 通过 `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })` 注册工厂(bundle id 必须等于包名),往 `sidebar.workspaces.session.menu.item` 注册菜单项,渲染两步确认,调用宿主路由并刷新会话列表。 |

**请求防护**:精确路由在 `webServer.match()` 里优先于应用自己的 `/api` 前缀路由,因此这个 handler 自带守门——`Sec-Fetch-Site` 为 `cross-site` / `same-site` 一律拒绝;带 `Origin` 时必须是 loopback 主机且端口等于本进程 `webServer.port`;没有 `Origin` 与 `Sec-Fetch-Site` 的本机进程被接受(web server 只监听 loopback)。会话 id 另有一层严格字符白名单。

**删除失败而非静默**:`not-found`(会话不存在)、`has-children`(有子会话)、`list-failed`(读不到会话列表,失败关闭而不是假定没有子会话)、`invalid-id`、`forbidden` 都会以 409/403 返回结构化原因,界面直接显示。

## 开发

```powershell
# 宿主半区冒烟测试:stub ctx + 临时 DSH_HOME,不碰真实会话
node test/host-smoke.mjs
```

- 宿主半区改动需要重启 Harness;浏览器半区改动 `dsh-client-modules` 按文件修订号重新服务,刷新页面即可。
- 浏览器半区是纯 JavaScript(无 JSX),只能 `require` 平台基线模块:`react`、`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives`(Module Loader 包的隐式 external)。

## 已知边界

- 已经上报的遥测无法撤回,本插件只清理本地状态。
- 别的会话正文里提到该会话的文字属于别的会话,不动。
- 删掉父会话被拒绝,所以子会话 header 里的 `parentSession` 不会悬空;反过来,子会话被删掉后,父会话的分支记录仍保留。
- 正好处于「活的写句柄仍占文件」的极端时序下会走 `deferred` 路径:文件在下次启动时补删。
- 投影缓存路径假定默认 storage 根(`<home>/storages`);profile 把 storage 根搬到别处时,这一个缓存文件会留下(会话已经没了,没有读者)。

---

# @hitzhangjie/dsh-plugin-session-delete (English)

DeepSeek Harness ships archive only: an archived session stays on disk forever. This plugin adds the missing operation — a real, irreversible **session delete** — behind one entry in the sidebar session-row `...` menu.

It is a DSH **bundle** (it declares `dsh.bundle.patch`), so installing it with `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add <path>` selects it as a profile layer automatically; no hand-written `cordis.patch.yml` row is needed.

**Features.** A red `Delete session…` row registered into `sidebar.workspaces.session.menu.item` with the same `MenuItemButton` presentation the built-in actions use; a two-step inline confirmation that disarms itself after five seconds; running work stopped first through the archive `stopActivity` waterfall; sessions with forked children refused (their child headers name the parent); and local state removed with no residue — event-log directory, projection-cache entry, spill directories, workspace accounting, archive/pin membership, and the live store entry when the store exposes one. A file still held by a live writer is journaled to `<home>/plugins/session-delete.pending.json` and reaped on the next start.

**Install, restart, done.** The row name must be the bare package name: `dsh-client-modules` attaches a package's browser half only to the Loader row whose specifier is exactly the bare package name, and profile resolution maps that name into the profile's own `node_modules`.

**Guards.** The exact route wins over the app's `/api` prefix route, so it guards itself: `cross-site` / `same-site` `Sec-Fetch-Site` is refused, a present `Origin` must be loopback on this process's `webServer.port`, and session ids must match a strict character whitelist. Refusals come back as structured JSON (`not-found`, `has-children`, `list-failed`, `invalid-id`, `forbidden`) and are shown in the menu.

**Verify without a harness**: `node test/host-smoke.mjs` runs the host half against a stub context and a temporary `DSH_HOME`.

## License

MIT

plugins.description: Runtime evidence that helps agents trace, profile, and burn down hotspots in application and native code, GPU kernels, and inference stacks.
plugins.readme_text:
flameox

Bounded local runtime evidence for coding agents.

Flameox coordinates profilers, benchmark tools, trace processors, and direct local targets. It turns an explicit artifact or command into bounded evidence while keeping durable preservation optional. The agent chooses hypotheses and experiments; Flameox records observed inputs, execution provenance, typed evidence, coverage, and limitations. There is no workspace to initialize or project configuration to maintain. Pass exact artifact paths to analysis and an explicit argv plus absolute working directory to capture. Flameox does not search parent directories, edit project files, or provide a hosted service. ## Quick start Configure an MCP client with the global setup command: ```console npx flameox@latest setup ``` Setup detects supported clients and asks which configurations to update. For automation, select clients explicitly, for example `--client codex --yes` or `--all --yes`; `--dry-run` reports the paths and actions without writing. Setup preserves unrelated client configuration and does not change project files. See [the npm package guide](npm/README.md) for details. Update existing MCP registrations with: ```console npx flameox@latest update ``` `update --check` reports available updates without changing configuration. Updates preserve each client's provider extras and settings, verify the new environment before changing release pins, and report which clients need a restart or reconnect. Use `--client codex` to select one client, or `--version 0.2.8` to select a specific release, including for rollback. The Python CLI exposes the same `flameox update` command. For direct CLI use, pass exact artifact paths or an explicit command: ```console uvx flameox analyze preview_artifact /absolute/path/to/artifact.json uvx flameox capture --provider direct --cwd "$PWD" -- python benchmark.py ``` To launch the stdio MCP server manually: ```console uvx flameox mcp serve ``` For local development, clone the repository, install its development dependencies, and inspect the available tools: ```console git clone https://github.com/morluto/flameox.git cd flameox uv sync --extra dev --extra memory --extra trace --extra cpu uv run flameox mcp inspect ``` ## Evidence and storage Analysis and unpreserved capture use bounded session scratch. Session `analysis_id` values expire when evicted or when the server stops. Explicit preservation creates the user-level Flameox data directory and stores native bytes and a canonical evidence bundle by SHA-256. Set `FLAMEOX_DATA_DIR` to choose another location. Preservation is optional; it does not imply full console-output retention. Flameox distinguishes observed, derived, and inferred claims. Profiles guide exploration but do not establish causality or performance improvement. Confirmatory claims require representative workloads, declared metrics and estimands, compatible identities, preserved samples, and a semantic oracle. ## MCP The MCP server has no workspace binding. It exposes named analysis and capture tools through the same operation registry as the CLI. Analysis tools accept explicit sources; capture tools accept a typed target and provider. Tool schemas expose operation-specific fields directly. Inspect the catalog with `flameox mcp inspect`; use `--tool TOOL_NAME` for focused schemas and examples. The complete contract and current tool catalog are in [the interface guide](docs/interfaces.md). Tools return their full bounded results inline, including failures and recovery actions. Preserved evidence has a durable `evidence_id`; `inspect_evidence` returns its redacted metadata and replay sources inline. Capture takes argv, not a shell string. A direct target supplies an absolute working directory and bounded environment overrides. Results may include `next_page`; replay its named analysis tool and arguments unchanged. Capture continuations read collected artifacts and do not rerun the target. MCP work belongs to the live request, so cancellation applies directly and no detached job survives a restart. ## Documentation - [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) describes process and package boundaries. - [Storage and evidence](docs/storage-and-evidence.md) defines preservation and provenance. - [Investigations](docs/investigations.md) covers experiments, comparison, and evidence quality. - [Adapters](docs/adapters.md) documents provider compatibility and integration policy. - [Runtime safety](docs/runtime-safety.md) covers limits, recovery, integrity, and privacy. - [Interfaces](docs/interfaces.md) defines CLI and MCP contracts. - [Testing](docs/testing.md) describes test selections and known proof gaps. ## Development Flameox requires Python 3.12 or newer and uses the committed `uv.lock`. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for development setup and contribution guidance. ```console uv run ruff check src tests tools uv run ruff format --check src tests tools uv run mypy src tests tools uv run pytest -q ``` Flameox is licensed under the MIT License.

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-mcp-hub

DSH 插件：**可视化 MCP 服务器管理 + 多格式导入**。

在 Web GUI 的 **设置 → MCP Hub** 里管理 MCP 服务器：查看列表与连接状态、启动 / 关闭、
测试连接、增删改，并把 Codex / Claude / Cursor / VS Code 的 MCP 配置一键导入。

## 解决的问题

DSH 里每个 MCP 服务器是一行 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` 的 Loader 条目，
平时要手改 YAML。本插件提供一个面板来做这件事，并且**能直接吃各家客户端的配置格式**，
不用手工翻译成 DSH 的写法。

## 功能

| 功能 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| 列表可视化 | serverName、传输方式、目标（URL / 命令）、启用状态、加载阶段、已注册工具数 |
| 启动 / 关闭 | 写回配置文件并触发热重载；关闭立即断开该服务器工具，开启立即连上 |
| 连接测试 | 真握手 `initialize` → `tools/list`，报告工具数与耗时；失败给出可读原因 |
| 增 / 删 / 改 | 表单编辑，含 stdio 与 streamable-http 两种传输 |
| **多格式导入** | Codex TOML、`mcpServers` JSON、VS Code `servers` JSON、顶层单对象 JSON |
| 导入来源 | 粘贴文本、填绝对路径读取、扫描本机已知位置（Codex / Claude / Cursor / Gemini / VS Code） |
| 密钥保护 | 导入时把 `PASSWORD` / `TOKEN` / `KEY` / `SECRET` 等值替换为占位符，并提示补填 |

### 支持的导入格式

**1. Codex（`~/.codex/config.toml`）**

```toml
[mcp_servers.idea]
type = "http"
url = "http://127.0.0.1:64342/stream"

[mcp_servers.mysql-dev]
type = "stdio"
command = "/usr/bin/npx"
args = ["-y", "mysql-mcp-server"]

[mcp_servers.mysql-dev.env]
MYSQL_HOST = "dev.example.com"
MYSQL_PASSWORD = "secret"     # 导入后变成占位符，需在面板补填
```

**2. Claude Desktop / Cursor 等 `mcpServers` JSON**

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "idea": { "enabled": true, "type": "remote", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:64342/stream" }
  }
}
```

**3. 裸 JSON（无外层键）**

```json
{ "idea": { "url": "http://127.0.0.1:64342/stream", "type": "http" } }
```

**4. VS Code（`.vscode/mcp.json`，允许注释与尾逗号）**

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "idea": { "type": "http", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:64342/stream" }
  }
}
```

传输别名会被归一化：`http` / `remote` / `streamable-http` / `sse` → `streamable-http`；
`stdio` / `local` → `stdio`。缺 `type` 时按 `command` / `url` 自动判定。

## 三种导入方式

| 方式 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| 粘贴配置文本 | 把上面的任意格式粘进文本框 |
| 从本地文件导入 | 填路径（支持 `~`），或点「扫描本机已知位置」后按行读取 |
| 扫描本机已知位置 | 探测下面的已知路径并显示各有多少台 |

### 会扫描哪些位置

按平台给出各自真实的位置（不会把三个平台的路径混列一遍，避免显示不存在的位置）：

| 工具 | 位置 |
| --- | --- |
| Codex | `~/.codex/config.toml` |
| Claude Code | `~/.claude.json`、`~/.claude/settings.json` |
| Cursor | `~/.cursor/mcp.json` |
| MCP CLI | `~/.config/mcp/config.json` |
| **Gemini / Antigravity** | **`~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json`** |
| Gemini（旧位置） | `~/.gemini/settings.json` |
| Antigravity | `~/.gemini/antigravity*/mcp_config.json`、`~/.antigravity/mcp_config.json` |
| VS Code | `~/.vscode/mcp.json`、用户级 `mcp.json`（按平台） |
| Windsurf | `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json` |
| Claude Desktop | macOS `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/…`；Windows `%APPDATA%\Claude\…`；Linux `~/.config/Claude/…` |

两个容易忽略的点：

- **Gemini / Antigravity 的真实配置在 `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json`**，不在
  `~/.gemini/settings.json`。后者通常只剩 `{"mcpServers": {}}`（空），
  `~/.gemini/config/` 目录里有个 `.migrated` 标记文件，正是从旧位置迁过去的痕迹。
  只扫旧位置会永远发现不了这份配置。
- **跳过没有 MCP 条目的文件**。`~/.gemini/config/config.json`、
  `~/.claude/settings.json` 这类文件装的是主题、权限、`statusLine`，
  列出「0 台」只会让人以为插件找错了地方，所以扫描结果里不出现。

> 顺带：Antigravity 的 `~/.gemini/antigravity/mcp/<服务器名>/*.json` 是**工具 schema
> 缓存**（里面是 `xdebug_get_stack.json` 这类单个工具的描述），**不是** MCP 配置，
> 插件不会去读它们。

### 导入前可以逐条勾选

解析结果会列成一个**可勾选清单**，只有勾中的才会写入。默认规则：

- 与已有服务器**重名**的条目默认**不勾**（面板上会显示 `idea → idea-2` 这类改名提示），
  避免在不知情的情况下多导一台重复的进来；
- 不冲突的条目默认勾选；
- 未勾中的条目**不会占用 serverName**，你之后再单独导入它时仍是原本的名字
  （不会变成 `idea-2`）。

清单上方有「全选 / 全不选」。底部实时显示「已勾选 N 台」。

**读取文件时不会把文件原文回传界面。** 像 `~/.codex/config.toml` 这种文件，绝大部分内容
（`model_provider`、`sandbox_mode`、`approval_policy` …）与 MCP 无关；把它们倒进文本框既是
噪音，也可能把 `env` / `headers` 里的密钥显示到浏览器上。

所以「读取」是**就地解析**：解析在 Host 侧完成，界面只收到解析出的服务器清单。面板显示
「已从 /path 解析出 N 台服务器」，配合勾选清单一起看。解析永远在 Host 完成，
Client 只拿到规划后的结果 —— 这也是 `lib/selftest.mjs` 里那条
「返回值不含文件原文」断言在守的行为。

### 已有的服务器：接管（adopt）

如果某台服务器的行写在**别的插件**的配置文件里（例如 `cordis.patch.yml` 由
`dsh-mcp-manager` 写），本插件按设计不去改别人的文件，所以它在面板上是只读的
（标「外部配置」，按钮禁用）。

点该行展开后的 **接管** 按钮，可以把它搬进本插件名下：

1. 先在来源文件旁生成备份 `<file>.bak-<时间戳>`；
2. 从来源文件里**行级摘除**这一行（保留注释与其余内容，不做整文件重写）；
3. 并入 `mcp-hub.yml`，此后可正常启停 / 编辑 / 删除。

摘除只动目标行：`lib/adopt-e2e.test.mjs` 会断言「除目标行外逐行一致」，包括注释。

写入前会加与宿主 `dsh-config-editor` **同一把锁**（`<file>.lock`），
并用原子写落盘，避免两个写入方互相覆盖 —— 详见下面设计说明第 3 条。

### 导入时的两个提醒

- **密钥变占位符**：`env` / `headers` 里名字含 `pass` / `secret` / `token` / `key` /
  `credential` / `auth` 的值会被替换为 `__DSH_MCP_HUB_SET_ME__`，条目标为「待补密钥」，
  需要你在面板里手动填回。
- **远程传输的 `env` 会被忽略**：`dsh-mcp-client` 的 `streamable-http` 分支只读
  `url` 和 `headers`，没有 `env` 字段。遇到这种配置会给出**告警**（而不是静默丢弃），
  提示你改写成 HTTP header。反之，`stdio` 传输不支持 `headers`，同样会告警。

## 数据放在哪

本插件**独占**一个文件，默认位于 **profile 目录内**：
`$DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/mcp-hub.yml`（权限 0600），可通过行的 `dataFile` 覆盖。

> **为什么放在 profile 目录里，而不是 `$DSH_HOME/mcp-hub.yml`：**
> 数据文件持有 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` 行，而 dsh 启动时的兼容性预检会
> **从声明该行的文件自身**向上解析这个裸包名：
>
> ```js
> createRequire(pathToFileURL(<include 文件>)).resolve.paths('@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client')
> ```
>
> 文件放在 `$DSH_HOME` 下，会一路向上找到 `$DSH_HOME` 的**父目录**的
> `node_modules`。如果那里残留一份旧 dsh 安装（例如工作区 `package.json` 里写着
> `@deepseek-ai/dsh: ^0.1.2-rc.1`），就会命中旧版 `dsh-mcp-client`；peer 校验
> 失败后 dsh 会**整体禁用这个 include**：
>
> ```
> dsh: disabling profile plugin row "mcp-hub-servers": its included file
> <...>/mcp-hub.yml reaches an incompatible plugin, and that file is never rewritten
> ```
>
> 症状很隐蔽：文件写得进去、面板也能列出来，但**重启后里面的服务器不会被挂载**。
> 放进 profile 目录后，向上命中 `$DSH_HOME/profiles/node_modules` 与 dsh 自身
> 安装，版本与运行时一致。由 `lib/datafile-path.test.mjs` 守着这条。
>
> 从旧位置升级时会**自动迁移**：检测到旧文件有内容而新位置为空就搬过来，并把旧
> 文件改名为 `mcp-hub.yml.migrated-<时间戳>` 保留（不删）。

它不会去改 `profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`，因此可以和别的 MCP 管理插件共存
（例如 `@js2hou/dsh-mcp-manager`）而不会互相覆盖。

### 和同目录的 `cordis.patch.yml` 会不会冲突？

**不会**：两个文件在同一个目录里，但 dsh 是**按确切文件名**逐个读 patch 层的
（`readProfilePatches` 里写死 `join(context.home, "cordis.patch.yml")` 等），
**从不扫描目录**，所以两份内容各自独立生效、互不覆盖。实测（两个文件各放一台
不同名字的服务器）：两台的 fiber 都是 `active`，且各自**只出现一次**。

但有一个**重名**风险要留意：两份文件是独立的两层，若在 `mcp-hub.yml` 里放一台
与 `cordis.patch.yml` 中**同名**的服务器，dsh 会加载两台不同的服务器却共用同一个
`serverName`，工具名（`mcp__<name>__*`）会互相打架。面板对此有三道防护：

- 导入时同名条目**默认不勾选**，并显示 `idea → idea-2` 的改名提示；
- `add` / `update` 拒绝重复的 `serverName`（返回 `duplicate-server-name`）；
- 新导入的条目会避开外部行已占用的 **id**（`mcp-idea-2` 而不是撞上 `mcp-idea`）。

所以正确的做法是：用面板的**接管**把那几台**搬**过来（移动 + 备份），
而不是在 `mcp-hub.yml` 里手工再写一遍。

文件通过 bundle 里的一行 `cordis:include`（`path: './mcp-hub.yml'`）挂进 Loader；
面板的每次写入都会调用该 include 的 `refresh()`，由 Cordis 对条目做增量 reconcile
—— 这正是「开关某个服务器而不重启进程」的机制来源。

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[设置 → MCP Hub 面板] -->|RPC /mcp-hub| B[Host 插件]
  B -->|读写| C["~/.dsh/profiles/web/mcp-hub.yml"]
  C -->|cordis:include| D[Cordis Loader]
  D --> E["dsh-mcp-client × N"]
  E --> F[ctx.tools: mcp__name__tool]
```

## 安装

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add /home/yyh/yyh/dsh-mcp-hub
```

或让 Agent 用 `plugin_manager` 的 `install_bundle` 安装本目录。

装好后重启或在 GUI 里应用，然后打开 **设置 → MCP Hub**。

## 开发与自测

```sh
node lib/rpc-binding.test.mjs      # RPC 注册契约：10 项
node lib/selftest.mjs              # Host 侧逻辑：90 项
node lib/client-smoke.mjs          # Client 侧渲染：68 项
node lib/loader-integration.mjs    # 真实 Cordis Loader 集成：34 项
node lib/adopt.test.mjs            # 行级摘除：21 项
node lib/adopt-e2e.test.mjs        # 接管端到端（沙箱）：19 项
node lib/adopt-path.test.mjs       # 写入目标不得来自环境变量：19 项
node lib/lock.test.mjs             # 写入锁与宿主的互斥性：13 项
node lib/datafile-path.test.mjs    # 数据文件位置 + 与 cordis.patch.yml 共存：17 项
node lib/platform.test.mjs         # 跨平台 + Gemini/Antigravity 发现 + 误报防护：33 项
```

共 324 项。这些脚本都不依赖第三方包，也不会触碰真实 profile 文件（都在临时目录里跑）。
其中 `loader-integration.mjs` 用真实的 `cordis-plugin-loader` + app-boot 的
`cordis:include` 建树，验证了「改文件 → 单条目热启停」这条主链路。

## 设计说明

- **零依赖**：YAML 读写、TOML 解析、MCP 握手探测全部自己实现，只用 Node 内置模块。
  这样插件不往 profile 的 `node_modules` 里塞东西，也不受 `pnpm` 安装策略影响。
- **不碰别人的文件**：只写自己的 `mcp-hub.yml`；`cordis.patch.yml` 里的其他行只读不改。
  （唯一的例外是用户主动点「接管」，见上文，且有备份与白名单校验。）
- **不改外部条目**：不在本插件配置文件里的 MCP 行（例如别的插件或 bundle 定义的）在列表里
  标记为「外部配置」，只读，避免两个插件抢同一行。
- **UI 只用主题 token**：不引入任何 Harness Client 包，明暗主题都跟随宿主。
- **探测是真的**：连接测试会真的握手并列出工具，不做乐观假设。

### 六个容易踩的坑（都已踩过并加了回归测试）

**1. `cordis:include` 行上的 `!!js` 不会被求值。**
`Include` 是一个 `EntryGroup`，而 Loader 的 `internal/config` 钩子对 EntryGroup 直接
提前返回（`if ((this.runtime?.callback)?.[EntryGroup.key]) return config`）。所以
`path: !!js dshHomePath(...)` 会留下一个未求值的 `{__jsExpr}` 对象，Include 拿去
`new URL()` 就变成 `[obj
