plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-sync

DSH 跨设备同步插件。通过**使用者自己的私有 HTTPS Git 仓库或 SFTP 服务器**同步会话、附件、配置及选定工程，支持在线安全范围应用、离线恢复及经确认的插件升级。

- 当前版本：**0.6.0**；许可证：MIT。
- 公开源码／安装包：https://github.com/vxdeus/dsh-sync
- 公开软件与私人备份完全分开：发布包不含作者的同步仓库、服务器连接信息、账号、密钥、令牌、会话、附件或工程数据。
- 首次安装没有预配置远端。安装、启动及打开面板不自动上传或下载；已有本机配置不会被安装初始化覆盖。

## 环境与安装

需要带插件管理器的 DeepSeek Harness，运行时 Node.js **24 或更高版本**。SFTP 另需本机可用的 OpenSSH `ssh` / `sftp`。在线应用及插件升级取决于宿主提供的接口；不可用时明确禁用，不会绕过授权或降级为直接覆盖会话文件。

在 DSH 插件管理器中安装 GitHub Release 的 `dsh-sync.tgz` 或带版本号安装包，并核对同一 Release 的 `SHA256SUMS`。随后**完全退出并重新打开 DSH**，再刷新原有网页。仅刷新网页不能保证更新宿主插件的模块缓存。

入口：**设置 → 跨机同步**，或侧边栏底部的**同步**。

## 配置自己的存储

配置文件位于当前 `DSH_HOME` 下的 `dsh-sync.json`；未设置 `DSH_HOME` 时为用户目录下的 `.dsh/dsh-sync.json`。它只留在本机，不进入同步快照。请在本机编辑，勿将真实配置提交到公开源码仓库或贴入聊天。

### 私有 HTTPS Git

新建仅自己／授权协作者可访问的私有数据仓库，使用独立同步分支。下面仅是**不可连接的占位示例**，请替换仓库和账号：

```json
{
  "backend": "gitee",
  "repoUrl": "https://git.example.invalid/your-account/private-sync.git",
  "branch": "dsh-sync",
  "username": "your-account",
  "token": "",
  "privateRepoConfirmed": false,
  "profiles": ["desktop"],
  "includeAttachments": true,
  "maxExtraBytes": 209715200,
  "extras": []
}
```

`gitee` 是保留的 Git 后端配置名，界面也沿用 Gitee 标签。Git 传输使用 HTTPS 用户名／令牌认证；不同提供商的兼容性和权限要求需自行验证。

令牌可只设置在本机环境变量 `DSH_SYNC_TOKEN`，或写入本机配置的 `token` 字段。使用最小必要仓库权限，不把凭据嵌入 URL。**亲自确认数据仓库为私有后**才将 `privateRepoConfirmed` 改为 `true`；这是本机确认声明，插件不会自动查询或更改远端可见性。

**不得将本项目的公开源码仓库作为个人同步目标。** 插件会拒绝此目标。切换仓库、分支或账号会隔离 Git 工作副本；更换旧设备配置后建议先下载核对，不强制推送覆盖远端。

### 自己的 SFTP 服务器

不提供托管服务器、共享账号、预置主机公钥或私钥。每台设备自行生成／保管密钥，并由服务器管理员授权设备公钥。在本机配置：

- `backend`：`sftp`。
- `sftp.host`：自己的服务器域名或地址；`port`：SSH 端口。
- `sftp.username`：自己获授权的服务器用户。
- `sftp.remoteRoot`：安全的 `/data/` 子目录，例如 `/data/my-sync`；须按服务器 **SFTP 可见路径**配置。
- `sftp.privateKeyPath`：本机私钥绝对路径，私钥不经过网页、不进入同步。
- `sftp.hostKey`：通过可信独立渠道核对的完整 `ssh-ed25519` 服务器公钥。不要关闭主机身份校验，也不要盲目信任首次网络扫描结果。

密钥需可用于非交互式 OpenSSH 认证。账户、密钥和目录访问权限由使用者管理。Git 和 SFTP 备份相互独立；切换存储不会搬运或删除旧备份。面板保存存储选择不会自动传输。

## 日常使用

### 源设备上传

1. 先检查状态与同步范围。工程／额外文件须手动添加自定义映射，例如逻辑名 `my-project`。
2. 可执行**本地预演**：它会扫描并暂存本机数据；已配置 Git 时还可能创建本地提交，**不是只读检查**，但不推送或访问远端。
3. 明确确认后上传。仅当显示远端回读／哈希核验成功时，才视为备份成功。超时后可能显示待确认，不自动重复推送。
4. 同一时刻只在一台设备编辑。不是实时双向同步，也不自动合并两台设备的分叉历史。

### 目标设备下载与恢复

1. 安装兼容版本插件，并配置自己的仓库凭据或 SFTP 授权。各设备按**相同逻辑名**映射工程，本机目标路径可以不同。
2. 默认在线模式只应用宿主允许的安全范围：冷历史通过原生接口导入；已加载、分叉、格式不支持的会话及忙碌工程保留，运行时配置等推迟应用。查看未应用项，不能将部分应用当成全量成功。
3. **仅下载／离线恢复**只产生暂存计划，不覆盖现有会话或工程。检查结果后完全退出 DSH，再运行该结果给出的恢复命令。需可运行 Node.js 24+；不要在另一台机器复用生成的本机恢复脚本。
4. 恢复核对源哈希及下载时的目标基线，覆盖前验证备份；冲突时停止，不自动改权限。内容相同的只读附件保持原样。失败计划不可重跑，先检查日志并重新下载。
5. 恢复中失败会尝试回滚，仍可能出现需人工处理的不完整回滚。请保留日志和备份；本插件不替代独立备份。

离线计划会记录本次宿主端口并检测监听，但仍须自行确认**所有相关 DSH 进程已退出**。不提供自动关机、自动关闭 DSH、配套桌面宿主补丁或一键授权新设备的功能。

下载尚未完整应用时会阻止后续上传，避免用旧本机快照覆盖远端。不要轻易勾选覆盖未应用远端内容；只有核对并明确接受丢弃风险后才能使用此选项。

### 跨设备插件升级

快照可携带已安装插件的精确版本、支持的本地安装包和升级说明。目标设备下载后仅检测差异；**用户选中具体插件并再次确认后**才交给宿主插件管理器安装。模型调用另需本次插件管理授权。

不自动批准依赖构建脚本，不自动降级，不自动重启。远端说明及本地插件包都属于不受信任输入，请先核对来源；安装插件意味着允许代码在宿主环境执行。若返回待重启，由使用者手动重启。安装后重新下载恢复计划，以免使用安装前的旧基线。

## 同步范围、隐私与限制

- 包含：指定 profile 的安装声明／锁文件、允许的会话与 `storages` / `state` 文件、`.agent-presets`、可选附件、已有 `dsh-pet` 配置和明确添加的自定义项。
- 不直接复制：`node_modules`、模型／OAuth 登录凭据、`integrations`、IM 聊天存储、运行时、缓存、同步配置、私钥和令牌。插件包按白名单另行归档，不直接归档 profile。
- 本机搜索覆盖诊断与额度预测缓存不跨机覆盖；真实费用账本与搜索用量日志仍在允许范围内。
- 默认排除工程依赖、Git 历史和构建产物。凭据路径过滤不能识别任意正文中的秘密。**会话、附件、插件配置、脚本和工程可能本来就包含隐私／密码；上传前自行审查。**
- 私人快照及默认 Git 提交可能记录设备主机名、系统用户名和配置账号，并非匿名同步。私有 Git / SSH 提供访问控制和传输保护，**不提供客户端端到端加密**。Git 历史可能保留已删除的内容；SFTP 历史快照和未引用对象暂不自动清理。
- 目录名及部分文本中的用户目录可做占位符转换；压缩历史内部路径和自定义工程内容不保证跨盘符自动修复。迁移后可能需重新定位工程。
- 单项自定义同步默认上限 200 MiB；缺失、超限或未映射项目可能阻止上传，避免静默丢失旧备份。
- IM 机器人历史不在同步范围内；同步 DSH 会话不等于两个 QQ 机器人自动续接话题。

## 模型工具

| 工具 | 用途 |
|---|---|
| `dsh_sync_status` | 只读检查配置、范围及插件升级提醒 |
| `dsh_sync_extras` | 添加／移除／查看本机工程映射，不传输 |
| `dsh_sync_upload` | 明确要求后上传；`dryRun: true` 本地预演 |
| `dsh_sync_download` | `mode: online` 安全在线范围；`mode: offline` 下载并生成离线计划 |
| `dsh_sync_update_plugins` | 仅安装用户明确确认的当前计划中所选插件 |

## 开发与发布

```sh
node scripts/test.mjs
node scripts/verify-public.mjs
node scripts/release.mjs
node scripts/smoke-package.mjs
```

隔离测试使用合成临时数据，不需要真实用户配置或访问真实仓库。Windows 的符号链接测试取决于系统权限；若沙箱重写 junction 元数据，必须在正常 Windows 环境复核，不能通过移除安全断言宣称测试通过。原生宿主集成测试需单独配备支持的 Host，默认不访问真实 profile。

打包使用 npm 标准格式及显式文件白名单，并核对归档成员、字节和 SHA256。不上传任何备份，不执行 `npm publish`，不自动创建 GitHub Release。公开发布步骤及市场提交见 `PUBLISHING.md`，版本说明见 `CHANGELOG.md`。

plugins.description: A DeepSeek Harness plugin: global search across session content, ordered by content time.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-session-search

**English** | [中文](README.zh.md)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that searches the
**content** of every session — not just session titles — and orders hits by the **time of the
matched record**, newest first.

It adds a first-class search destination to the sidebar (a panel icon beside *Plugins* and
*Schedules*, plus a full-width results page) and a `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+F` shortcut. Clicking a hit
opens its session.

```
┌─ sidebar ─┐  ┌─ main ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Plugins  │  │  Search session content                                    │
│ ▸ Search  │  │  [ 会话                                            ]        │
│  Schedules│  │  All · My prompts · Replies · Tool output   ☐ subagents    │
│           │  │  43 hits · 8 sessions · 4 ms                               │
│           │  │ ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
│           │  │ 2026-09-11 01:55   user   修改 FreeCAD MCP 服务端口         │
│           │  │   我在使用这个 mcp 服务[插件]，但是端口被占用了…            │
└───────────┘  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## Why this plugin exists

Stock DSH can already *search* sessions — the sidebar search box is wired to a real
content-search pipeline:

```
WorkspaceBrowser → sessions.search(query) → ctx.remote.session.search
  → SessionController.search → ctx.sessionQuery.searchSessions(…)
```

It only ever finds titles because **three independent things** are true at once:

| # | Fact | Where |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The content backend is **switched off** in the stock profile — `openAt: never`. The shipped comment says it plainly: *"the Web sidebar search matches titles and workspace names only."* | the `session-query-sqlite` row in `dsh-base/cordis.patch.yml` |
| 2 | That backend tokenizes with FTS5 `unicode61`, which treats **an entire CJK run as a single token**. Measured on a real machine: `光速太慢，星际文明无法成为整体` yields exactly two tokens, `光速太慢` and `星际文明无法成为整体` — so `MATCH '光速'` and `MATCH '星际'` both **return nothing**. The `trigram` tokenizer is no help either: it rejects 2-character queries. | verified locally against SQLite 3.53.4 |
| 3 | Even with the backend enabled, the wire shape is `{ items: [{ sessionId, snippet }] }` — **each hit's `time` is dropped at that layer**, and ranking is relevance-first (`time` is only a tie-breaker). | `dsh-api-session-controller/lib/index.js` |

So "order results by content time" is **not achievable through any shipped public remote**, and
for CJK content the shipped engine is the wrong tool regardless. This plugin therefore builds its
own index on the host: it incrementally parses every session transcript, keeps each record's text
together with **that record's own `time`**, matches by substring (correct for both CJK and Latin
text), and sorts by time. It needs **no profile configuration changes**.

---

## Where the search entry lives — and why

DSH's Web/desktop UI has **no global top bar** and **no global command palette** (`/` commands are
the composer's slash menu and are bound to the current session). Only three global seats are
available:

| Seat | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **`sidebar.panellist` icon + its matching `main` panel** | ✅ **Used here.** This is DSH's first-class "global panel" mechanism: the sidebar owns the button, the label and the selected state, and the list `id` maps directly to the `main` panel `key`. The shipped **Plugins** (order 0) and **Schedules** (order 10) panels work exactly this way; this plugin slots in between at order 5. `replaceRisk: none` — it cannot be clobbered by an upgrade. |
| `sidebar.footer.action` (next to Settings) + a `shell.overlay` dialog | ⭕ Viable alternative, better suited to a "spotlight" quick-search. Costs you hand-built overlay, focus and Escape handling, and leaves little room for snippets. |
| `sidebar.workspaces` (where the existing search box lives) | ❌ **Not used.** It is a `single` seat occupied wholesale by `ui-workspace`, with `replaceRisk: shadows-shipped-ui` — taking it means replacing the entire shipped session browser and breaking on the next DSH release. |

A **`Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+F`** shortcut (registered through `dsh-client-shortcuts`) selects the panel from
anywhere. It is bound on the **desktop profiles only** on purpose: on the Web profiles the shipped
`session.fork` (`dsh-client-ui-workspace`) already owns `KeyF + primary+shift`, and the shortcut
registry validates a definition's defaults across every *declared* profile, throwing
`Conflicting shortcut defaults` from whichever plugin registers second. See
[Compatibility](#compatibility) for what that cost once.

For **searching inside the session you are reading**, the entry point is the `list` seat
`conversation.session.header.utilities` — the right-aligned action row of the conversation header.
It is additive (`replaceRisk: none`, ids `open-in-app` / `schedule-catalog` /
`session-log-download` already sit there), always in reach, and needs no new global chrome. The
find bar and the result dialog share one `shell.overlay` entry — the frame-wide layer documented as
"the additive seat for a frame-wide surface of your own" — so they float above every column without
stealing one.

---

## Install

This package is a standard DSH **bundle** (`dsh.bundle.patch` + `dsh.client` in its manifest).
Install it with the plugin manager:

```
plugin_manager action=install_bundle target="<absolute path to this repo>"
```

That writes the package into the profile's `dependencies` and `dsh.profile.bundles` and links it
into the profile's `node_modules`. You do **not** need to hand-edit the profile's `package.json` or
`cordis.patch.yml`.

Disable or remove it again:

```
plugin_manager action=set_bundle    target=dsh-session-search enabled=false
plugin_manager action=remove_bundle target=dsh-session-search
```

### Mounting it manually instead

Add a row to the profile's own `cordis.patch.yml` (the `name` may be a bare package specifier, a
path relative to the patch file, or an absolute path):

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: session-search
      name: 'dsh-session-search'
```

> **A note on reloading.** The Harness loads plugin rows through Node's ESM loader, which caches
> both the resolved package entry and the module itself for the lifetime of the Host process.
> Re-enabling a row that previously failed re-runs the *cached* module, so a fix on disk is not
> observed until the app restarts — `dsh-hmr` can activate a **new** row, but it cannot swap a
> JavaScript module generation for an already-loaded package. `lib/entry.js` exists to work around
> this during development: it re-imports `lib/host.js` behind an mtime-keyed query, so host-side
> edits take effect on the next activation. In normal use it is simply the entry point.

---

## Usage

### Global search

1. Click the magnifier icon in the sidebar (between *Plugins* and *Schedules*), or press
   `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+F`.
2. Type a query. Matching is **substring**, case-insensitive, and works for CJK (a 2-character
   query matches inside a longer run, which the shipped FTS5 engine cannot do).
3. Narrow the results with the chips — *All* / *My prompts* / *Replies* / *Tool output* — and the
   *Include subagent sessions* toggle (off by default; subagent sessions routinely outnumber your
   own). The **session scope picker** at the top lists only the sessions that actually matched the
   current query, with hit counts (`title (12)`), so scoping to one of them is one click; with no
   query it lists recent sessions.
4. Click any hit to open it **with its context**: the matched record plus four records before and
   after, the match highlighted and untruncated. Use previous/next to move between hits, and
   *Open session* to jump to the session itself.

### Find in the conversation (Ctrl/Cmd+F)

Press `Ctrl/Cmd+F`, or click the magnifier in the conversation header's right-aligned utilities.
A small floating bar appears, searches the transcript, paints **every match** and scrolls the
active one into view:

- `Enter` / `Shift+Enter`, or `‹ ›`, cycle matches; `Esc` closes and clears the highlights.
- The match counter s

# dsh-settings-arranger

**English** | [中文](#中文) --- ## 中文 设置页左侧那一列分区导航，插件装多了就变成一长条：顺序由各插件注册时写死、不能改，官方分区和一堆插件分区混在一起。这个插件给它加上**拖拽排序**和**自定义分组**，排布按浏览器保存，刷新不丢。 ### 功能 - **拖拽排序**：任意分区条目拖到任意位置，分组与普通条目混排也行。 - **分组**：把相关分区收进一个组（比如把「追问 / 通知 / 喵记忆」收成「系统增强」），点组头展开。 - **组内排序 / 跨组移动 / 拖出一级**：整理模式下组内条目同样能拖，可拖进别的组，也可拖回一级。 - **新建 / 重命名 / 删除分组**，同名会就地报错。 - **恢复默认**：一键清空排布，回到原生顺序（二次确认）。 - **两套视图**：平时收起成组头、点开是下拉菜单；点「整理导航」进整理模式，组内条目全部内联铺开，方便拖。 ### 效果图 日常使用：分组收起成一行，点开是带图标的浮动下拉菜单。 ![设置页导航：三个分组（模型提供 / 样式插件 / 系统增强）收起成一行，点开的「系统增强」下拉里列出追问、通知、喵记忆、bili 设置、备份与迁移、提示词优化设置、dsh-git-idea 配置，每项带原图标](assets/normal-mode.png) 整理模式：点右上角「整理导航」，组内条目全部铺开，可直接拖动排序。 ![整理模式：分组展开为小标题样式、成员条目内联缩进、行尾有 ⋮⋮ 拖拽把手与重命名/删除按钮，底部是「＋ 新建分组」与「恢复默认」](assets/edit-mode.png) ### 安装 ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-settings-arranger ``` 装完刷新 Web GUI（或重启 dsh），bundle 会随包里的 `cordis.patch.yml` 自动注册。 > 用 GitHub 源安装：`dsh plugin --profile web add github:HelloQingTao/dsh-settings-arranger` ### 用法 1. 打开 **设置**，点右上角的 **整理导航**。 2. 点 **＋ 新建分组** 起个名字。 3. 把条目拖进组里，或把分组头拖到别的位置；组内条目可以再拖去别的组，或拖出一级。 4. 点 **完成** 退出整理模式，点分组头就能展开下拉菜单。 排布存在浏览器的 localStorage 里（键 `dsh.settings-arranger.v1`），**按浏览器与站点隔离**，换浏览器或换端口要重新整理。 ### 兼容 - dsh `0.2.0-rc.2` 实测通过。 - 纯客户端插件，只操作 DOM，不改任何其它插件的代码；同名的分区顺序仍由各插件自己的 `order` 决定，本插件只是在渲染后再重排。 ### 许可证 [MIT](LICENSE) --- ## English The settings dialog's left nav grows into an unmanageable list once you install a few plugins: order is baked in at registration time and official sections sit interleaved with plugin ones. This plugin adds **drag-to-reorder** and **custom groups**, persisted per browser. ### Features - **Drag to reorder** any section, mixing groups and plain rows freely. - **Groups**: collect related sections into one group (e.g. put "Follow-up / Notifications / Meow Memory" under "System"). Click the group head to expand. - **Reorder inside a group, move across groups, drag back out** — all available in arrange mode. - **Create / rename / delete groups**, with inline duplicate-name validation. - **Reset to default** — clears the layout and returns the native order (with confirmation). - **Two views**: normal mode collapses groups into heads with a floating dropdown; clicking **整理导航 (Arrange)** switches to edit mode where every member is laid out inline for dragging. ### Screenshots Normal mode — groups collapse into a single row; clicking one opens an icon-carrying dropdown. ![Settings nav: three groups collapsed into one row; the "系统增强" dropdown lists its members with their original icons](assets/normal-mode.png) Arrange mode — click "整理导航" in the top-right corner; all members expand inline and can be dragged. ![Arrange mode: groups become compact section headers, members are indented inline with drag handles and rename/delete buttons, and the footer holds "+ New group" and "Reset to default"](assets/edit-mode.png) ### Install ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-settings-arranger ``` Refresh the Web GUI (or restart dsh); the bundle registers itself through the shipped `cordis.patch.yml`. > From GitHub: `dsh plugin --profile web add github:HelloQingTao/dsh-settings-arranger` ### Usage 1. Open **Settings** and click **整理导航** in the top-right corner. 2. Click **＋ 新建分组** and name the group. 3. Drag entries into it, or drag the group head elsewhere; drag members across groups or back to the top level. 4. Click **完成 (Done)** to leave arrange mode, then click a group head to open its dropdown. The layout lives in the browser's localStorage (key `dsh.settings-arranger.v1`), so it is **per browser and per origin** — a different browser or port starts fresh. ### Compatibility - Tested with dsh `0.2.0-rc.2`. - Pure client-side: it only touches the DOM and never modifies other plugins' code. Section order is still declared by each plugin; this plugin simply re-lays-out the rendered nav. ### License [MIT](LICENSE)

# dsh-plugin-verispring

Verispring three-role session architecture plus a bundled local knowledge graph (manon), substantially improving main-session context and reducing premium model API costs.
[中文](README.zh.md) | English

## What it enforces

| # | Gate | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Dispatch spec gate | `subagent` / `subagent_fork` requires the dispatch spec content to have appeared in the session (a read result containing the spec's first-line marker; state is persisted in the session log and survives restarts) |
| 2 | Resident scout (reachability) | The first dispatch of a session is pinned to the scout role at runtime (`description` is a display label only). The authoritative fact is **reachability**, not the description prefix: while a reachable scout exists, another scout dispatch is denied with a `send_message` reuse pointer (a scout waiting for a question showing finished/inactive is normal — `send_message` cold-resumes it); once it becomes unreachable (an `end` with a non-`completed` stop reason, or `send_message` reporting unavailable) the next dispatch is automatically re-roled to scout and the map is re-injected. Child roles are persisted at spawn (`session-state/<child session id>.json`) and restored from the record and the session title after reloads |
| 3 | Map first + baseline | Non-scout dispatch requires `<session workspace>/.project-map.md` (project root = `.git`/`.manon` present; otherwise fail-open); a `write`/`edit` of that file registers the current HEAD as the map baseline, and dispatch is denied while HEAD has advanced past it (the denial points to a scout incremental recheck plus a full `write` rewrite to re-register). A map without a registered baseline is denied too — no fail-open, so a stale map cannot stay valid forever. Fail-open only when `CASEOS_SCOUT=0` or HEAD cannot be read |
| 4 | Brief lint + executor cap | The executor brief is a result description, not a research request: briefs containing research wording (`BRIEF_LINT_TERMS` in `gates/dispatch-gate.js`) are denied with directions to `send_message` the scout instead — **negated mentions are exempt** (a negation within 6 characters before the hit, e.g. `不要通读实现` / `禁止先调研`). Running executors per leader session are capped (default 8); exceeding it is denied with "end the turn and wait for receipts". Both have kill switches (`CASEOS_BRIEF_LINT=0`, `CASEOS_MAX_EXECUTORS`) |
| 5 | Pinned model | Routes are enforced at runtime per role: the first dispatch uses the panel's scout route, later ones the executor route; explicit `provider`/`model` on the call is ignored. `subagent_fork` is always denied |
| 6 | Commit gate | `git commit` requires a prior read of `~/.dsh/specs/代码写作规范.md`; the shape is forced to `-F file -- explicit paths`, with `timeout`/`env`/`nice`/`nohup`/`stdbuf` style wrappers seen through |
| 7 | Leader scope | The leader's tool face shrinks to the review five (`bash`/`edit`/`write`/`read`/`read_image`) plus the dispatch face (`subagent`/`send_message`/`interrupt_agent`/`list_agents`), intersected with the tools that actually exist in the leader's view (desktop serves them from the preset layer, headless from the root layer); dispatch tools are shadowed by slim definitions; `subagent-base` is unconditionally denied at the root layer (if the routing executor ever breaks, the model has no fallback to sneak through). Scout and executor subagents get the full face of the `verispring-subagent` preset, and scouts are hard-denied `edit`/`write` through the dispatch request. Kill switch `CASEOS_SCOUT=0` drops the scout part of the division clause |
| 8 | Leader guard | Two kinds of runtime handling. **Denials (unchanged):** while a child is running, `sleep`/loop-waiting in `bash` is denied, and a second `list_agents` in the same turn is denied. **Hints (since 1.3.66):** `edit`/`write` outside the whitelist (`.project-map.md`, paths containing `/reports/`, `~/.dsh/AGENTS.md`, plus `CASEOS_LEADER_WRITE_ALLOW` prefixes) and `bash` change commands — `git commit/push/merge/rebase/restore/stash` (only `git stash list` / `git stash show` stay silent), `npm`/`pnpm` publish/install, `sed -i`/`perl -i`, `rm -rf`, workspace redirects — are **no longer denied**: the call runs as usual and one notice is appended after the tool result via the host `tools/post-execute` `additionalContexts` ("clear-boundary code and writing tasks go to an executor subagent; the leader does small fixes, the map, reports and verification writes"), at most once per turn, recorded to the monitor as `leader-write-hint` (rule + summary). Subagent sessions are unaffected. Kill switch `CASEOS_LEADER_GUARD=0` |
| 9 | Scout relay | The three loops that used to exist only in the prompt: `ask_scout` lets an executor hand a location/fact question to the resident scout and waits for the fresh answer (sender is the leader agent, since `sendMessage` authorizes by lineage); the closing "结构增量" (structure delta) section of a non-scout child is forwarded to the scout automatically; a failed child (`error`/`aborted`/`refusal`) writes a checkpoint that the plugin attaches when the leader continues it. Non-scout subagents get an injected ≤4-line locator discipline (`ask_scout` when a scout is reachable, "write it into your report" otherwise) plus the mandatory structure-delta section. Kill switch `CASEOS_SCOUT_RELAY=0`; `CASEOS_ASK_SCOUT_TIMEOUT_MS` bounds the wait |
| 10 | manon bridge | Resolves the local graph CLI (`MANON_KG_BIN` > bundled `manon/manon-kg` > legacy `~/manon/manon-kg`) and, when present, injects per role: the scout gets the full surface (commands, sourced invocation rule, ownership discipline), the leader gets one line ("graph facts come from the scout"), the executor gets one line — **manon is scout-owned; leader and executors never invoke it directly**; semantics in `~/.dsh/specs/Manon调用规则.md`. **The load-bearing part is the invocation rule**: dsh's subprocess service strips KEY/TOKEN-shaped env vars from children (anti-leak), so a bare `manon-kg sync` always fails with a missing key — the injected form sources `~/.dsh/manon.env` inside the bash command first (the scrub only strips the first hop; grandchildren inherit freely). Secret values never pass through or get printed |
| 11 | Secret hygiene | Credential/env files (`manon.env`, `verispring.env`, project `.env*`) cannot be read via `read` or echoed via `cat`/`sed` and friends (matched per command segment, so the sanctioned `source` prefix and pipes on manon output are not false positives); whole-environment dumps — bare `env`/`printenv`, `ps eww`, `/proc/*/environ`, `docker inspect` without `--format` — are denied |
| 12 | Runtime monitor | Role drift, gate denials, scout reachability changes and subagent start/end (role + route + stop reason, recorded only after a successful start) are appended to `~/.dsh/verispring-monitor.jsonl`, so audits no longer require decompressing session logs |

### Environment variables

| Variable | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `CASEOS_SCOUT` | on | `0` drops the scout part of the division clause and the map freshness/baseline gate |
| `CASEOS_BRIEF_LINT` | on | `0` disables research-wording denials on executor briefs |
| `CASEOS_MAX_EXECUTORS` | `8` | running-executor cap per leader session (`0` blocks every executor dispatch). The default equals the host's own `maxActiveSubagents` default of 8 (the scout counts toward the host limit), so with the scout running the 8th executor may be refused by the host with `ACTIVATION_LIMIT_REACHED` |
| `CASEOS_LEADER_GUARD` | on | `0` disables the leader runtime denials at assembly time |
| `CASEOS_LEADER_WRITE_ALLOW` | empty | `:`-separated extra path prefixes the leader may `edit`/`write` |
| `CASEOS_SCOUT_RELAY` | on | `0` unregisters `ask_scout` and stops forwarding/checkpointing/prompt injection |
| `CASEOS_ASK_SCOUT_TIMEOUT_MS` | `600000` | how long `ask_scout` waits for the scout's answer before returning a timeout |

### Monitor events

`kind` values in `~/.dsh/verispring-monitor.jsonl`: `subagent-start` / `subagent-start-failed` / `subagent-end` / `subagent-error` (lifecycle + role + route), `child-route-updated`, `role-route-mismatch`

plugins.description: In-conversation workflow run timeline for the DeepSeek Harness web GUI
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-workflow-ui

[![CI](https://github.com/zuiyouli/dsh-workflow-ui/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/zuiyouli/dsh-workflow-ui/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)

DeepSeek Harness Web GUI 的对话内工作流运行时间线：把官方 `workflow` 工具卡与 `workflow-run` 聊天节点替换成横向时间线——轨道 + 阶段站 + 子代理药丸 + 循环弧线 + 并行带，且**开跑之前就能看到全部计划**。

English documentation in [README.en.md](README.en.md)。

![dsh-workflow-ui 截图](docs/screenshot.png)

窄窗口自动换行（同排弧 + ↩ 回边徽标）：

![dsh-workflow-ui 换行模式](docs/screenshot-wrap.png)

## 功能

- **对话内嵌卡片** — 每次 workflow 运行一张卡，长在对话流里，无需打开任何面板。
- **计划先行** — 客户端扫描 workflow 脚本（`phase()` 调用、`parallel()` 块、阶段回访），开跑前就渲染出全部计划站点、药丸占位与依赖弧线。
- **并行带** — `parallel()` 阶段渲染为抬升轨道，fork/merge 接头为圆角弧。
- **弧线** — 非相邻前向边与循环回边在轨道上空飞行：弧道按跨度分配（短跨低道、相交上推）、8px 圆角拐点、落地箭头；落入运行中站点的弧点亮为 march。宽屏画完整弧线；窄屏换行时只画同排弧，跨排回边由 `↩` 徽标承担。
- **药丸折叠** — 单站超过 5 个子代理自动折叠为「＋N」展开片；展开状态跨实时刷新保留；隐藏药丸里有运行中的会在折叠片上闪呼吸点。
- **药丸跳转子会话** — 点击药丸按 DSH 0.2.1 契约（`openSession({parentSessionId, childSessionId, mode})`，mode 传 `unknown` 由工作区自行解析）直达对应子会话；支持键盘聚焦与 Enter 触发。
- **自带 agent 预设** — 安装即向名册添加 `Workflow 编排` 预设（标准全量工具 + "多步任务主动用 workflow"的 persona 指引），卸载即移除。
- **DSH 官方图标** — StateDot 状态点（done/error = 6px 实心核，running = 中性 spinner 弧，pending = idle 点）、官方 ListPen 卡头图标、1px Check/Close 标记。
- **子代理药丸** — 逐 agent 状态 + 表情（运行中张望/眨眼），结算勾，未启动的计划占位。
- **主题与无障碍** — 经 DSH 别名 token 适配亮/暗主题，全链路尊重 `prefers-reduced-motion`，状态字形带 `aria` 标签。

## 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:zuiyouli/dsh-workflow-ui
```

安装后重启一次 dsh（组合变更），再刷新页面。要求 DSH `>=0.1.0-rc.5`；已在 `0.2.0-rc.2` 与 `0.2.1-rc.2` 实测，web profile。

装好后建议切换到自带的 **Workflow 编排** 预设（新会话选择器里），模型会对多步任务主动使用 workflow 编排。

## 原理

两个 keyed 槽位以 `priority: -1` 影子官方渲染器（官方默认 `0`，priority 最低者渲染；本组件崩溃会自动 abdicate 回退官方）：

- `conversation.chat.node` key `workflow-run` — 数据来自官方 Definition 对持久化事件（`tool-workflow/run-start|agent-start|agent-end|run-end`）的投影，本插件只换呈现。
- `tool.call.toolview` key `workflow` — 渲染不可见标记（该行经 CSS `:has` 隐藏，0.2.1 起连同 turn-process 流程头一并隐藏），并把工具入参的脚本元数据 stash 进模块 store，供运行卡做计划先行渲染。

样式以 `<style data-plugin>` 一次性注入、卸载时移除；类名全部 `zcf-` 前缀。颜色落在 14 个局部 `--color-*` token，映射到 DSH `--dsw-alias-*`。

## 开发

零依赖，Node >= 20。

```bash
npm run check     # 语法检查 + 单元测试 + 构建 + lib 检查 + 门面冒烟
npm run preview   # 生成 docs/preview/preview.html（亮/暗卡片）
```

无头截图预览：

```bash
chrome --headless=new --virtual-time-budget=3000 --screenshot=shot.png docs/preview/preview.html
```

布局常量参考 ZCode 的公开工作流呈现设计（站宽 168 / 间距 192 / 灯心 +17，弧基 26 / 道距 14，6–8px 圆角接头，120/160/200/320ms 运动 token）。状态点与图标复现 DSH 官方 `dsh-client-ui-primitives` 的形制（StateDot、ListPen、Check、Close）。本插件与 ZCode、DSH 官方均无隶属关系。

## 路线图

迭代方向与版本主题见 [docs/roadmap.md](docs/roadmap.md)（下一版 v0.3.0：完成态折叠摘要 + 耗时/循环指标 + 失败复盘）。

## 边界说明

- 工具行只作为隐形数据源存在；时间线卡是会话中的唯一入口。
- 宽屏单排画完整弧线；换行模式只画同排弧，跨排依赖以 `↩` 徽标提示。
- 完成后卡片默认收成一行复盘摘要（阶段/进度/循环/失败定位/耗时，耗时需上游时间字段支持）；状态词为内置中文，locale 通道暂未接。
- 只读消费 workflow 事件，不保存任何平行编排状态。

## 许可

[MIT](LICENSE) © zuiyouli

## 构建与注入

(prebuilt - no build step required)

plugins.description: DSH Desktop 冷启动开机动画插件 · Arknights 风格 HUD boot sequence for DeepSeek Harness (dsh-cold-boot)
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-cold-boot · DSH 开机动画

给 **DeepSeek Harness** 的界面加一段 44 秒的冷启动演出：黑底、等宽字、扫描线与 glitch，
六场戏、四句英文人声，音效全部用 Web Audio 现场合成。纯 DOM + CSS，**零运行时依赖**，
装完下次打开就播（点画面或按任意键跳过）。

> 非官方同人作品，与 DeepSeek 官方无关。产品名与鲸鱼标识归其权利人所有 —— 见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。

![开场](docs/img/1-cold-boot.png)
![标识与光扫](docs/img/2-whale-sweep.png)
![三栏全貌](docs/img/3-overview.png)
![授权通过](docs/img/4-authorization.png)
![定格名牌](docs/img/5-final-plate.png)

## 安装

| 方式 | 怎么做 |
|---|---|
| 应用内插件市场 | 在市场里搜 **dsh-cold-boot**，一键装 |
| npm | `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-cold-boot`（预构建，免构建授权） |
| 本地 tgz | 下载 `dsh-cold-boot-<版本>.tgz` → DSH 的插件页「从本地文件安装」 |
| 源码 | `git clone` 后 `npm run build`（`prepare` 钩子也会自动构建），再从目录安装 |

关掉 / 只播一次（浏览器控制台）：

```js
localStorage['dsh-cold-boot'] = 'off'    // 永不播
localStorage['dsh-cold-boot'] = 'once'   // 每个标签页只播一次；删掉这个键就恢复每次开机都播
```

装完在 profile 的 `package.json` 里会多一条 `dsh.profile.bundles` 记录
（本机是 `%APPDATA%\dsh-desktop\harness\profiles\web`，`patchReload: live`，不用重启）。
想关掉就把它从 bundles 里去掉，或者直接卸载。

## 看效果（不装插件也能看）

```bash
npm run standalone     # → preview-standalone.html（1.7MB 单文件，引擎 + 四句人声全内联）
```

双击打开即可，不需要服务器、不依赖相对路径（可以随便拷给别人）。

| 控件 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| ▶ 从头播 | 整段 **44 秒**跑一遍（点画面、按任意键都能跳过） |
| ⏭ 跳过 | 直接走收尾流程 |
| 时长 32s / 44s / 56s | 整段压缩或拉长，人声音高不变、语速跟着缩放 |
| 🔊 / 🔇 | 开关音效与人声（浏览器拦自动播放，点一下才有声音） |
| ① ~ ⑥ | 定格在六场戏的任意一场 |

`npm run frames 16000 34000` 会生成 `dev/frame-<ms>.html` 定格页 —— 改完时间轴先拿它逐帧核对。

## 六场戏（基准 44000ms）

| 时刻 | 场 | 画面 |
|---|---|---|
| 0–7.6s | ① | 冷启动字幕（COLD BOOT / 冷启动序列 · 逐项自检 / SEQUENCE 00）+ 日志开始打字 |
| 2.6s / 12.8s | ①③ | 人声 1「Uplink established. Terminal boot sequence initiated.」；人声 2「Self-check complete…」 |
| 8.0–12.8s | ② | 标识逐笔描线（六边形线框 → 鲸鱼 → 一道光扫掠过 → DSH 字标落下）、档案栏、幽灵编号 07 |
| 13.4–26.2s | ③ | 三栏全貌 + 标题 DEEPSEEK HARNESS + 副标题 + 代号 + 日志 18 行 + 进度条与六盏步骤灯 |
| 23.6s | ③ | 人声 3「Permission proxy armed. Session handover standing by.」 |
| 26.2–30.6s | ④ | 权限校验面板：六条 scope 逐行落（workspace-write OK / 9 industrial modules ON / MCP ONLINE / modbus write ASK / credentials LOCKED / session OK），右侧百分比推到 100 |
| 31.6–40.2s | ⑤ | 授权通过：三个同心环 + AUTHORIZATION GRANTED + 一道红细线（全片唯一的红）；33.8s 人声 4「System ready. Welcome back, Engineer.」 |
| 41.2s | ⑥ | 白闪 → 切三栏 → 41.8–44s 干净名牌停 2.2 秒 → 0.9 秒淡出，露出 DSH 界面 |

**场景层之间是先出后进**（前一块淡完才开始下一块），不会出现两块面板同时半透明。

## 里面有多少「真的是 DSH」

不是套壳文案，几个读数是对着本机实际安装抄的：

* **鲸鱼**＝ DSH 桌面端 `resources\icon.png` 里那只抠出来的，不是网上随手找的图；
* **v0.11.1**＝ `DSH Desktop.exe` 的 ProductVersion；**30 loaded**＝ profile 里 `dsh.profile.bundles` 的条数；
* 场① 第二行 `81 SKILLS · 30 PLUGINS · 9 MCP · $ dsh doctor`、场③ 的 `DSH desktop v0.11.1 · web profile`
  与 `dsh doctor` 日志行，都可以按你自己的机器改（改 `DEFAULT_LOG` / `TEXT` 常量即可）；
* 三条读数（CONTEXT / PERMISSION / TOOLS）跟着动画时间走，不是写死的静态条。

## 人声与音效

* 四句人声：**英文**，Windows SAPI（Zira，Rate −4 ≈ 比常速慢 45%）+ `scripts/voice-fx.py -ann`
  提亮到参考素材的频谱（F0 190Hz / 质心 1063Hz）。文件 `audio/en/L1..L4-zira-rm4-ann.wav`，
  实测 7.16 / 7.74 / 7.34 / 6.63 秒。**每句时长写进了 `DEFAULT_VOICE[].dur`** ——
  漏写会退回 3900ms 的假设值，就是之前「两个声音」的根因（第三句实际说到 24.87s，压上第四句）。
* 音效（`createSound()`）：低频底噪、终端 blip、glitch 噪声、白闪、收尾 chime 全部用 Web Audio
  现场合成，不带素材；音量比人声低 12~20dB，说话时自动 duck。
* 语音时刻表 2.6 / 12.8 / 23.6 / 33.8s，末句 40.4s 收，白闪 41.2s —— 每句都留 ≥800ms 余量。

## 插件形态

| 文件 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `lib/client.js` | 浏览器半边（1.7MB）：引擎 + CSS + 四句人声（base64 WAV）全内联，`window.__ModuleLoader__.load({...})` 外壳 |
| `lib/index.js` | 宿主半边（<1KB）：空实现 + 名字与版本，只为让 cordis 认得这个 bundle |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | 往 profile 里插一条 `#dsh-cold-boot` |
| `icon.png` | 512×512 插件图标（同一只鲸鱼 + HUD 细框） |

宿主侧不碰任何东西（不读文件、不发请求、不注册工具），所以**权限上只要 workspace-write 就够**。
前端只用到 DSH 客户端自带的 `ctx`/`React`/`host.call`/`styles.insert`，没有额外 peer 依赖。

## 文件

| 路径 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `src/boot-animation.js` | **引擎**（唯一事实来源）：时间轴 `T`、日志/步骤/人声文案、CSS、`play()` |
| `src/client-glue.js` | 插件外壳：把引擎挂上 `window.DSHBootAnimation`，给插件半边的调用面 |
| `src/host-half.js` | 宿主半边源码（空实现） |
| `audio/en/L1..L4-zira-rm4-ann.wav` | 四句英文人声（16bit 单声道 22.05kHz） |
| `scripts/build-plugin.mjs` | 打 `lib/`（内联音频、查语法、查同步）；`--check` 只校验 |
| `scripts/build-standalone.mjs` | 打 `preview-standalone.html`（引擎 + 人声 data URI 内联） |
| `scripts/build-frames.mjs <ms...>` | 生成 `dev/frame-<ms>.html` 定格页（自检用） |
| `scripts/make-icon.py` | 用抠好的鲸鱼遮罩画插件图标 |
| `scripts/voice-fx.py` · `scripts/voice-analyze.py` | 人声染色 / 量化（numpy） |
| `docs/img/` | README 里那五张图 |

## 引擎 API

```js
var handle = DSHBootAnimation.play({
  duration: 44000,          // 整段时长；相位按比例缩放
  sound: true, volume: 0.55,
  soundBase: '', voiceBase: '',   // 装成插件后指向只读资源路由
  voice: [{ src, dur, text, meta }],
  log: [...], steps: [...], rail: [...],
  skipOnClick: true, oncePerSession: false, seek: null, onDone: fn
});
handle.finish();   // 跳过
handle.destroy();  // 立刻摘掉遮罩
```

改时间轴只需要动：相位表 `T`、步骤灯时刻 `STEP_AT`、日志 `DEFAULT_LOG`、人声 `DEFAULT_VOICE`
（CSS 里的 `--t-*` 变量与 `T` 一一对应，两处要一起改）。

## 已验证 / 已知

* 六场戏 + 结尾定格逐帧截图核对（1280×800 与 512×900 两种窗口）；量尺（`getBoundingClientRect`）
  确认窄窗下标题单行不溢出、档案栏一行一条、日志底部不被步骤灯压住。
* 实跑收尾、点击跳过、`destroy()` 三条路径都实测会摘掉 `#dsh-boot-animation` 与 `<style>`，不会留黑屏。
* 打包体积：`lib/client.js` 1.7MB → tgz **830KB**（四句人声内联占 1.2MB）。
* 踩过的坑：`animation` 是简写，**收尾的 `dsb-keep` 必须写在各元素自己的规则里**（分组规则会覆盖入场动画）；
  淡出动画只能 `forwards`，配 `both` 会在延迟到点前就按不透明显示；`inset:auto` 会把前面的
  `left/top` 一起重置，居中元素要把它写在 `left/top` **之前**。

## 许可

MIT（见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)）。人声由 Windows SAPI 合成、音效现场生成，仓库里不含任何第三方素材。

plugins.description: Native Rapid-MLX provider for DeepSeek Harness (dsh) — dsh reads model facts from the server instead of your settings.yaml.
plugins.readme_text:
# @raullenchai/dsh-provider

A native [Rapid-MLX](https://github.com/raullenchai/Rapid-MLX) provider for
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) — so `dsh`
gets its model facts from the server instead of from whatever you typed into
`settings.yaml`.

[![CI](https://github.com/raullenchai/rapid-mlx-dsh-provider/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/raullenchai/rapid-mlx-dsh-provider/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

> **Status: published to npm** as
> [`@raullenchai/dsh-provider`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@raullenchai/dsh-provider).
> The end-to-end `dsh` run in [Verified](#verified) was on an M3 Ultra against
> `dsh 0.1.0-rc.7`; `dsh 0.1.0-rc.8` is API-compatible — the `LlmAdapter`
> contract is byte-identical and the only changes are additive — and the
> adapter is re-verified against rc.8 at the protocol and unit-test level.
> DSH is still a developer preview that moves fast, so treat this as tracking
> a moving target, not a frozen compatibility promise.

## What it does for you

DSH can already talk to a local Rapid-MLX server through its generic
`openai-completions` provider. That route works — but it knows nothing about
your model beyond what you hand-wrote:

```yaml
# what the generic route makes you maintain, by hand, per model
llm-pi-ai:
  providers:
    rapid-mlx:
      baseURL: http://localhost:8000/v1
      defaultContextWindow: 262144      # you looked this up. is it still right?
      models:
        - id: qwen3.6-35b-8bit
          contextWindow: 262144
          reasoningEfforts: {off: none, low: low, medium: medium, high: high}
```

Rapid-MLX's `/v1/models` already publishes all of that and more. This adapter
reads it, so:

**1. Nothing to hand-write, and nothing to re-write when you switch models.**
Swap what `rapid-mlx serve` is running and `dsh` follows. No re-running setup,
no stale numbers.

**2. The reasoning control tells the truth.** Rapid-MLX reports whether a model
actually has a reasoning parser. A model that can't reason no longer shows an
off/low/medium/high selector that does nothing.

**3. Compaction is timed with the capacity that actually fits this Mac, not a
number that drifted.** This is the one that quietly costs you.
`dsh-compaction-basic` asks the provider for the route's capacity and compacts
at `thresholdRatio × capacity` (0.8 by default). The provider prefers the
server's **`max_model_len`** — Rapid-MLX's memory-fitted ceiling (what fits in
unified memory: weights + KV cache), in the vLLM/SGLang-standard field — over
the native `context_window`, and falls back to `context_window` on an older
server that doesn't report it. So compaction is timed to what the machine can
actually hold, not the model's advertised window (which it may not have room
for) and not a hand-written number copied from another model.

## Install

Needs Node ≥ 22.15 (dsh imports Node's Zstd stream API without declaring it)
and a running Rapid-MLX server.

```sh
# From npm:
dsh plugin --profile web add @raullenchai/dsh-provider

# …or straight from source — the package ships plain JS with no build step:
dsh plugin --profile web add github:raullenchai/rapid-mlx-dsh-provider

export RAPID_MLX_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000/v1     # optional; this is the default
dsh web
```

Then point the agent at the route:

```yaml
# $DSH_HOME/settings.yaml
agent-default-model:
  provider: rapid-mlx
  model: qwen3.6-35b-8bit
```

Verified: that command installs and activates as a profile layer against
`dsh 0.1.0-rc.7`. To hack on it locally instead, see
[Local development](#local-development).

## Model management (v0.2.0)

Beyond the provider route, the plugin registers five tools and a `/rapid-mlx`
command so the agent can see and manage models without leaving the session.
The split follows which surface actually owns each fact: served-model facts
come from the structured HTTP `/v1/models`; the download cache and pull/remove
are CLI-only, so those — and only those — shell out to `rapid-mlx` through the
harness subprocess seam.

| Tool | Source | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `rapid_mlx_serving` | HTTP `/v1/models` | The model(s) served right now, deduped, with context window, reasoning/tool parsers, MoE/hybrid, and modalities. |
| `rapid_mlx_cached` | `rapid-mlx models --cached` | Downloaded models and their on-disk size. |
| `rapid_mlx_pull` | `rapid-mlx pull <name>` | Download a model (alias or HF repo id). Cancellable; no fixed deadline. |
| `rapid_mlx_remove` | `rapid-mlx rm -y <name>` | Delete a cached model to free disk. |
| `rapid_mlx_health` | HTTP + `rapid-mlx --version` | API up? CLI reachable? Reported as two independent facts. |

`/rapid-mlx` prints a one-shot overview: health, the served model and its facts,
and total cache disk usage.

The CLI is resolved from the `cliCommand` config (default `rapid-mlx` on
`PATH`, or `$RAPID_MLX_CLI`); set it to an absolute path if the binary is not on
the harness's `PATH`. `rapid_mlx_pull`/`rapid_mlx_remove` are the only tools
that change anything on disk, and they run non-interactively (`rm` is forced
with `-y` because the subprocess seam ignores stdin).

## Verified

Against `dsh 0.1.0-rc.7` on an M3 Ultra:

- Installs and **activates as a profile layer** (no "declares no `dsh.bundle`"
  warning; the entry shows up in `dsh --profile headless --dump-config`).
- Registers the `rapid-mlx` route with `ctx.llm` and serves real queries.
- Plain chat, a single tool call, and the multi-step bug-fix task that gates
  Rapid-MLX releases — the last one fixed the bug and made the target repo's own
  test pass, verified independently, in 36 s on `qwen3.6-35b-8bit`.

## Not done yet

Being explicit, because the point of the adapter is to *use* what the server
says and some of it is still only read:

- `recommended_sampling` — should be applied automatically per model.
- `tool_call_parser` — should let `dsh` fail fast on a model that cannot emit
  `tool_calls`, instead of looping.
- `is_hybrid` / `is_moe` / `capabilities` — read, not yet acted on.
- **Memory-aware capacity.** Today `resolveModel()` reports the model's
  *advertised* context window. On a Mac the real ceiling is unified memory, and
  reporting that instead is the biggest remaining win — it needs Rapid-MLX to
  expose a usable-capacity figure first.
- Images are not carried through `stream()` — but they now **refuse** with
  `LlmError(..., 'UNSUPPORTED')` rather than being dropped, per the cookbook.
  Text, reasoning and tool calls are carried.
- The route is registered as `rapid-mlx`. If your `settings.yaml` also declares
  a `rapid-mlx` provider under `llm-pi-ai`, the two compete for one route name
  (`registerAdapter` owns provider exclusivity). Use one or rename ours.

## Conformance with the official adapter contract

Built against
[`docs/cookbook/adding-an-llm-adapter.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/main/docs/cookbook/adding-an-llm-adapter.md)
and its "protocol obligations" section. Each item has a test:

| Obligation | How it is met |
|---|---|
| `usage` before `finish`, nothing after `finish` | usage is buffered and flushed at end-of-stream, so a trailing usage-only chunk cannot reorder it |
| Tool-call `arguments` are raw JSON strings end to end | fragments stream as `argumentsDelta` and reassemble unparsed |
| Block indexes in first-seen order, reused per block | verified across a reasoning-then-text response |
| Errors take exactly two sanctioned paths | transport/protocol failures **throw** `LlmError` with a stable code; nothing ends the stream quietly |
| Honor `options.signal` | passed to `fetch` and to the SSE reader; an `AbortError` is re-thrown unchanged, not reclassified |
| A field the provider cannot honor throws `UNSUPPORTED` | image content refuses instead of being narrowed away |
| Config is a schemastery schema with env fallback | `export const Config`, fed from `cordis.patch.yml` via `!!js process.env.RAPID_MLX_BASE_URL` |

`finish.replayState` is not emitted: Rapid-MLX needs no native response ids
or signatures on follow-up calls, so there is nothing lossless to project.

plugins.description: Design and restructure interfaces while keeping an editable FigCraft document.
plugins.readme_text:
# FigCraft Use

## Plugin marketplaces

This plugin belongs to **AIGC content creation**.

| Category | Marketplace | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full-stack development | [Full Stack Plugins](https://github.com/partme-ai/full-stack-plugins) | Architecture and UI design, code understanding, quality checks, code review, workflow governance, and server operations |
| AIGC content creation | [Full AIGC Plugins](https://github.com/partme-ai/full-aigc-plugins) | Image, video, audio, music, 3D, and multimodal content creation |

![FigCraft Use — interface design in your agent workspace](assets/official-logo.png)

> Design, restructure and hand off an interface inside your agent host, with the editable FigCraft document and its tokens kept as the source of truth.

[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-0.1.0--dev.20261019.1-1A73E8)](https://github.com/full-aigc-plugins/figcraft-plugin/releases)
[![Skills](https://img.shields.io/badge/skills-11-00A67E)](#skills)
[![MCP tools](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP%20tools-26-00A67E)](#mcp-tools)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-green)](LICENSE)

[English](README.md) | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [Install](#installation) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Skills](#skills) · [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

## Positioning

`figcraft` turns a page requirement into an editable interface document and carries it through design system, responsive layout, prototype and handoff. The plugin bundles a source-built FigCraft Web with same-session MCP automation and workspace file operations; it does not re-implement the design engine or claim pixel fidelity it has not checked.

| Property | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| Plugin ID | `figcraft` |
| Version | `0.1.0-dev.20261018.3` |
| Status | Development preview; all-host acceptance still open |
| Editor runtime | Node.js 24, started from `ui/bootstrap.mjs` |
| Editor baseline | FigCraft `v0.6.0` fixed source plus this plugin's automation build |
| Optional CLI | `figcraft-cli`, used by recipe scripts as `--cli` |
| License | Apache-2.0 |

## Installation

### Prerequisites

- Node.js 24 on `PATH`; the bundled stdio MCP server runs on it.
- Network access on the first editor launch. The plugin downloads and verifies the pinned editor archive; a complete release ZIP already contains it, so no Rust toolchain and no `npm install` are required.
- `python3` on `PATH` only if you run the optional recipe scripts that ship with four skills.
- `figcraft-cli` only if a recipe should drive the native CLI; the plugin does not install it.
- A host that supports plugins or stdio MCP. Embedded panels additionally require MCP Apps or a built-in browser.

### From the plugin marketplace

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add partme-ai/full-aigc-plugins
codex plugin add figcraft@full-aigc-plugins
```

Restart the host, open a new task, and ask FigCraft to open the editor for your workspace.

### Other host manifests

| Host | Manifest | Path base |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standard Agent Plugins 1.0.0 | `plugin.json`, `mcp.json` | `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` |
| Codex | `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.codex-plugin/mcp.json` | plugin root relative to `cwd` |
| Claude Code | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json` | `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` |

Kimi (`kimi.plugin.json`), DeepSeek Harness (`dsh/`) and the WorkBuddy example (`hosts/workbuddy/mcp.json`) are also present. In a development checkout you must build the editor assets first; cloning the source is not an installed runtime.

## Quick start

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Install plugin] --> B[Restart and open a task]
    B --> C[open_editor]
    C --> D{editor_status ready?}
    D -->|No| C
    D -->|Yes| E[create_node / set_properties]
    E --> F[inspect_document / get_node]
    F --> G[save_file]
    G --> H[export]
```

1. Open the editor with an explicit `workspace` argument.
2. Build the first frame with `create_node`, then style it with `set_properties`; complex structures go through `run_command` or `batch`.
3. Read `inspect_document` for structure and `screenshot` for the actual image.
4. Save with `save_file`, reopen with `open_file`, and confirm the layers are still editable.
5. Export for handoff only after the reopened document matches what you approved.

## What you can build

| Workflow | Built-in path | Verifiable output |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Low-fidelity wireframe | `figcraft-wireframe` | Structured frames and blocks, no invented content |
| Design system with variables | `figcraft-design-system` | Component library, states, colour and text variables |
| Light and dark token card | `figcraft-light-dark-token-card` | Semantic aliases with CSS or JSON delivery |
| Responsive layout | `figcraft-responsive-layout` | Auto-layout frames with wrap and overflow handled |
| Clickable prototype | `figcraft-prototype-flow` | Pages connected with entry, back and overlay states |
| Import an existing Figma file | `figcraft-import-fig` | Imported nodes plus a loss report for fonts and images |
| Editable chart | `figcraft-signed-bar-chart` | Positive, negative and zero values as editable bars |
| Swappable icon button | `figcraft-swappable-icon-button` | Instance swap and boolean visibility, text kept separate |
| Developer handoff | `figcraft-dev-handoff` | Annotations, measurements, CSS or React references |

## Skills

| Skill | What it does |
| :--- | :--- |
| `figcraft-editor` | Open FigCraft in the host, check same-session MCP, diagnose workspace save |
| `figcraft-wireframe` | Turn a page requirement into a low-fidelity wireframe or first interface |
| `figcraft-responsive-layout` | Mobile, tablet and desktop adaptation, auto layout, wrap and overflow |
| `figcraft-design-system` | Component library, button states, colour and text variables, light/dark themes |
| `figcraft-prototype-flow` | Connect pages into a clickable prototype with entry and overlay states |
| `figcraft-import-fig` | Import Figma `.fig`, REST file JSON or SVG and report fidelity loss |
| `figcraft-dev-handoff` | Editable UI, annotations, assets and CSS or React references |
| `figcraft-scenario-playbooks` | Recipes for login, plan card, metric component, navigation, container, dialog, empty and error states |
| `figcraft-light-dark-token-card` | Light/dark theme and semantic colour tokens with real command bindings |
| `figcraft-swappable-icon-button` | Icon swap plus hideable icon, with return-ID binding and re-check |
| `figcraft-signed-bar-chart` | Editable bars including positive, negative and zero values |

Skills come from the independent `figcraft-skills` source and are pinned by `scenario-candidates.json` with per-skill SHA-256 digests.

## MCP tools

One bundled server, `figcraft-editor`, speaking **stdio**. The local HTTP listener only serves the editor page and its same-session bridge. The catalogue exposes 26 tools: 21 agent-callable tools and 5 `_editor_*` bridge tools the panel uses internally.

| Family | Tools | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Session | `open_editor`, `open_browser_editor`, `editor_status` | Open the editor and confirm that it attached |
| Discovery | `list_commands` | List live command IDs, parameters and enabled state |
| Command gateway | `run_command`, `batch` | Run one command, or an ordered batch |
| Authoring | `create_node`, `set_properties` | Create nodes and set their properties, returning IDs |
| Inspection | `inspect_document`, `get_node`, `inspect_ui` | Document tree, one node, and interface state |
| Selection and input | `select`, `pointer`, `key`, `type_text` | Select objects and drive the same input paths as a user |
| Files | `open_file`, `save_file`, `export`, `screenshot` | Open, save, export and capture the canvas |
| History | `undo`, `redo` | Step back and forward one change |

## Configuration

| Setting | Where | Effect |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `workspace` argument | `open_editor` / `open_browser_editor` | Binds the task folder; paths outside it are refused |
| `CRAFT_EDITOR_UPDATE=off` | stdio MCP `env` | Use the bundled editor only; no download attempt |
| `CRAFT_EDITOR_CACHE_DIR` | Environment | Absolute directory for verified editor archives |
| `CRAFT_WORK

plugins.description: Run Python on the local CUDA GPU from DeepSeek Harness: device status, foreground and detached jobs, durable logs, and a measured peak-VRAM figure per run. / 在 DSH 里直接跑本地 GPU 的 Python 任务：设备状态、前台/后台作业、日志与峰值显存统计。
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-cuda

Run Python on your local NVIDIA GPU from **DeepSeek Harness**.

Three tools plus one skill, so an agent can do numerical work on the GPU instead of
occupying the CPU: device status, foreground and detached runs, durable logs, and a
measured peak-VRAM figure for every run.

> 中文说明见 [README.zh.md](README.zh.md).

## What you get

| Name | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `cuda_status` | device memory, utilization, GPU processes, every CUDA-capable Python on the machine, recent jobs |
| `cuda_run` | submit Python source (`code=`) or a `.py` file (`script=`, plus `args=`); foreground or `background=true` |
| `cuda_job` | follow one job: `logs` / `wait` / `kill` / `info`, by exact id, unique prefix, or `latest` |
| skill `cuda-compute` | the local terrain, how to write the code, the traps — loaded on demand by the model |

Every run gets its own directory under `~/.dsh/gpu-runs/<job-id>/`:

```
script.py        a copy of what actually ran
_runner.py       the wrapper that records resource facts
stdout.log       full stdout (the tool returns only a tail)
stderr.log       full stderr
job.json         the durable record: pid, cwd, argv, timestamps, status
result.json      written by the wrapper: ok, exit_code, elapsed_s, peak VRAM
```

`peak_alloc_MB` comes from `torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()` inside the child, so the
number is measured, not estimated. A program can read `DSH_CUDA_JOB_DIR` to write its own
artifacts there — they are listed back to the model automatically.

## Five design decisions worth knowing

1. **Exceeding the foreground budget promotes a run to background instead of killing it.**
   A two-hour simulation should not die because the caller stopped waiting. The result comes
   back with `status: running` and a note; follow it with `cuda_job`. Only an explicit
   cancellation actually terminates.
2. **Background runs are detached** and survive a harness restart — again on purpose,
   because long compute should not be tied to a UI lifecycle. The cost is that "leftover"
   jobs are found by asking, which is what `cuda_status` is for.
3. **A detached run's outcome is settled from `result.json`.** No parent is left to record
   the exit code, so once the pid disappears the wrapper's own fact sheet decides
   `done`/`failed`; only its absence means `lost`.
4. **The skill is registered through a borrowed provider.** The catalog keeps the summary
   and every load re-reads the file, so editing the skill body needs no restart. Skill
   registration is a soft dependency: a deployment without `ctx.skills` still gets the tools.
5. **`lib/engine.js` imports nothing from DSH**, so the engine is driven directly by plain
   Node in the test suite — see below.

## Install

The package lives in a workspace directory. Install it through the harness rather than by
hand-editing the profile (the bundled `cordis-plugin-development` skill explains why):

```
plugin_manager  action: install_bundle  target: <absolute path to this directory>
```

**Bundle code is only loaded at harness startup** — restart DSH after installing or editing.
(The installer's `applied` result means the config was written and the entry imports
cleanly; it does not mean the tools are already visible to a running agent.)

## Configure

Precedence for every setting: explicit plugin config → environment variable →
`~/.dsh/cuda.json` → built-in discovery.

| Environment variable | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `DSH_CUDA_PYTHON` | interpreter to use | discovered |
| `DSH_CUDA_RUNS_DIR` | where job directories live | `~/.dsh/gpu-runs` |
| `DSH_CUDA_TIMEOUT_MS` | foreground budget | `300000` |
| `DSH_CUDA_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS` | ceiling for a caller-supplied budget | `1800000` |
| `DSH_CUDA_MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS` | output returned to the model per stream | `12000` |

`~/.dsh/cuda.json` is the convenient place for a machine-specific interpreter (an embedded
Python, a conda env):

```json
{
  "pythonPath": "C:\\path\\to\\python.exe",
  "pythonCandidates": ["C:\\path\\to\\python.exe"],
  "runsDir": "D:\\gpu-runs"
}
```

A malformed file is ignored rather than fatal.

### Interpreter discovery

With nothing configured, the plugin probes every `python`/`python3` on `PATH` and a few
usual install locations, then picks the first candidate that exists. `cuda_status` reports
what each one can actually do (`torch` version, CUDA availability, device name, bf16), and
the probe result is cached for an hour.

An interpreter only counts if it has `torch` **with CUDA**. A system Python without torch
is reported but never chosen. Embedded interpreters shipped with image-generation tools
(ComfyUI, Stable Diffusion WebUI) work well — point `DSH_CUDA_PYTHON` at them.

## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness, Node 22+
- **Any** CUDA-capable NVIDIA GPU — the card model does not matter, and nothing here is tuned for
  one. `cuda_status` reports the model, memory, compute capability and bf16 support at runtime, so
  the documents deliberately do not hard-code them.
- **The one real constraint is driver ↔ torch.** A CUDA build of PyTorch needs a driver at least as
  new as the CUDA runtime it was compiled against; if `torch.cuda.is_available()` is `False`, that
  mismatch (or a CPU-only torch wheel) is the usual cause. `cuda_status` shows the driver and each
  interpreter's CUDA availability side by side, so the problem is visible before writing any code.
- A Python with `torch` + CUDA. The rest (numpy, triton, scipy…) is optional.

For **writing custom kernels** the plugin's skill documents what actually works: use
[`triton`](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton) if it is installed. `numba.cuda` needs
`libNVVM` (shipped with the CUDA Toolkit) and fails with
`NvvmSupportError: libNVVM cannot be found` when the Toolkit is absent — a common trap.

## Tests

110 checks across three suites. All of them run with plain Node — no harness restart, no
test framework:

```bash
node test/selftest.mjs    # 36  engine, against the real GPU
node test/harness.mjs     # 46  plugin: mock context drives apply(), then the tools run
node test/lossless.mjs    # 28  every tool value crosses the wire (see below)
```

- `selftest.mjs` covers both run modes, promotion, cancellation, log tails, artifact
  collection and argument validation on real hardware.
- `harness.mjs` builds a fake cordis context with exactly the surface the plugin uses, so
  `apply()` and every tool branch are exercised without the harness.
- `lossless.mjs` deserves its own line: DSH refuses a tool value that is not lossless JSON
  (`visitJsonValue` in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-gateway` rejects `undefined`, `NaN`, `-0`,
  class instances, array holes and cycles). A single `undefined` field is enough to make a
  perfectly working tool answer `value is not lossless JSON`, and no mock-based test
  catches it. The suite reimplements that rule verbatim and adds six deliberately broken
  values to prove the check itself has teeth.

## Known limits

- **Windows/WDDM**: `nvidia-smi` reports no per-process VRAM and mixes graphics processes
  into the GPU process list. `cuda_status` says so rather than pretending otherwise.
- **Concurrency**: `cuda_run` is registered as not concurrency-safe, so the harness will not
  overlap two runs; large concurrent jobs would compete for VRAM anyway.
- **No CUDA Toolkit integration**: `nvcc` is never invoked. Everything runs through the
  interpreter, which keeps the plugin zero-install.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

# read-figure

Give a **text-only model** a pair of eyes — and a fixed contract for what those eyes must report.

`read-figure` is a DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that contributes exactly one tool, `read_figure`:

> Hand it the path of a figure on disk → it asks a vision model to transcribe that figure under a
> **fixed three-section protocol** → it returns the transcription as **plain text** in your context →
> you answer from it.

It does not solve the problem for you, and it should not. It does something narrower and much harder
to get right: **making "what is in this figure" clear enough to be quoted, challenged, and audited.**

---

## Why this exists

DSH can already send an *attached* image to a vision-capable model. What nobody had done is this:

- A text-only model (say `deepseek-v4-pro`) that is **given an image path** can neither see the
  image nor ask anyone who can to look at it.
- Even with a transcription, there is **no contract for its quality** — the reader cannot tell what
  was genuinely observed from what was guessed.
- Scanned exam figures routinely contain **stray black specks connected to nothing**. A human
  dismisses them as scanner noise at a glance. A text-only model cannot see the image, so it reads
  the speck as a particle, a hinge, or a label symbol — and **invents a mass that does not exist,
  invalidating the entire force analysis.**

That last point is why this plugin exists. One CPhO figure carries an isolated **3×3 px ink blob,
6 px in area**, in its upper-right corner; the problem statement itself warns
"treat it as scanner noise, not a particle." That warning is exactly what a model which cannot see
the image most needs, and most easily misses.

---

## What it produces

A fixed three-section handoff whose headings are reproduced verbatim:

```markdown
# 识图交接件 · 第 1 题

> 由 read-figure 自动生成，视觉模型 `deepseek-flash`，<timestamp>.
> 源图：`figures/1.jpg`（1536×2711px，183 KB）
> 分工：图像描述与复述由看图模型完成，物理解答由纯文本模型完成。**本文件不含任何解答。**

---

### 一、图的结构（逐项描述）
Connections → every component and its label → geometry and coordinate system. No vague wording.

### 二、复述
One paragraph of physical situation, then three lists: given / sought / conditions not in the figure.

### 三、⚠ 读图置信度声明
- **高置信**：…
- **不确定**：an isolated speck about 6×10 px at the upper right, touching no line,
  judged to be scanner noise. **If you are the text-only model reading this:
  do not introduce an extra particle or hinge because of it.**

---

## 给纯文本模型的执行说明（请一并遵守）
1. Do not fill in the figure from common sense …
2. Prefer a symbolic solution …
3. If a conclusion depends on an "uncertain" item, stop and say so …
4. Ask a follow-up list …
5. Close the answer inside the derivation sentence …
```

The protocol body is **a markdown file** (`prompts/figure-handoff.zh.md`), not strings buried in code.
Edit it directly, or point `promptFile` / `extraInstruction` at your own version —
**70% of this plugin's value is the protocol, not the few hundred lines of HTTP code.**

Three **real** outputs — verbatim, from actual runs on 2026-10-17, with only the local
absolute paths redacted — live in [`examples/`](examples/). They show both modes
(whole-figure handoff, and a targeted follow-up) and why `maxTokens` defaults to 32000:
the reasoning chain was **92.8%** of the completion on the scanned page.

---

## Install

### 1. Let the plugin manager do it (recommended — this is how the repo was verified)

Ask the agent to call `plugin_manager`, or use the equivalent CLI package operation:

```
plugin_manager install_bundle  https://github.com/Amethyst-Leafs/dsh-read-figure
plugin_manager install_bundle  ./path/to/read-figure        # a local directory, for development
```

`install_bundle` runs `pnpm add` against the profile and appends the row declared in
`cordis.patch.yml` to the profile's bundle stack — **no hand-editing of profile files**.

**Restart dsh afterwards.** Host plugins mount when the process starts, so `read_figure` only
appears after a restart. (Measured on the desktop profile: the second install returned
`application: restart-required`, i.e. nothing failed at mount time. The first attempt returned
`failed` because this package's `Config` was not a Standard Schema yet.)

### 2. Manual mount

Add one row to the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: read-figure
  name: read-figure
  config:
    model: deepseek-flash
    apiKey: sk-…            # see "Credentials" below
```

### 3. Not installed at all (zero-install evaluation)

The CLI and the plugin share every code path, so you can judge the protocol before mounting anything:

```bash
node bin/read-figure.mjs --img figures/1.jpg --img figures/2.jpg --out out/handoff.md
```

---

## Configuration

| Key | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `baseUrl` | `https://api.deepseek.com` | any OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` endpoint |
| `model` | `deepseek-flash` | vision model name |
| `apiKey` | `''` | when empty, `READ_FIGURE_API_KEY` then `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` |
| `maxTokens` | `32000` | already above the observed ceiling (~29k characters of reasoning at `effort: high` on a 3094×1526 scan); **lowering it re-creates the empty-answer bug** |
| `reasoningEffort` | `high` | `low` / `high` / `max` |
| `timeoutMs` | `180000` | per-request timeout |
| `promptFile` | `''` | empty uses the packaged `prompts/figure-handoff.zh.md` |
| `extraInstruction` | `''` | appended after the protocol, for every call in the session |
| `handoffDir` | `''` | when set, `outPath` must resolve inside it |
| `writeHandoff` | `false` | reserved: write by default |

### Credentials

A **running** DSH cannot see a shell variable exported after it started.
If an environment variable does not take effect, write `apiKey` directly into the `cordis.patch.yml` row.

---

## Using the tool

### First pass

```json
{ "imagePath": "output/…/figures/1.jpg", "label": "第 1 题" }
```

Several figures: `{"imagePaths": ["figures/1.jpg", "figures/2.jpg"], "label": "第 1、2 题"}`

### Directed follow-up

When the handoff lists an uncertainty, **do not re-run the whole transcription** — ask about it:

```json
{
  "imagePath": "figures/1.jpg",
  "question": "The longest rope hanging from B's left side — does it end at m₂ or m₃? What difference would each reading make?"
}
```

A follow-up answers that one question only, and requires the vision model to cite **position and
observed shape/pixel magnitude**. If both readings are defensible it says so, and states what
physical picture each one implies.

---

## Design notes

- **Transcribe only, never reason.** The first hard rule of the protocol is "absolutely no problem
  solving." The moment the vision model starts computing, the handoff stops being an auditable
  observation record and degrades into an answer of unknown quality that the reader can neither
  verify nor challenge.
- **Uncertainty must be listed explicitly, with a guard sentence.** Reporting "there is a speck here"
  is itself **dangerous**: without "it is noise, do not add a particle for it," a text-only model will
  take it as real. Hence the protocol demands all five parts: position, pixel size, judgement,
  reasoning, and the guard sentence.
- **False positives are more dangerous than misses.** This comes from measurement: a mechanical
  speck detector's first run reported 7 candidates on one figure, all at `x≈1` or `y≈1` — cropped
  black edges of the scan. Injected as-is, the model would believe the problem has 7 extra labels.
  **Any mechanical evidence must pass a false-positive suppression rule before an LLM sees it.**
- **Thresholds do not scale with resolution.** It is tempting to scale the pixel threshold by image
  size. Don't. `figures/2.jpg`'s stray blob (area 1139) sits squarely *between* the letterforms
  (`figures/1.jpg`'s "A" is 871, `figures/2.jpg`'s "M" is 6756) — **no area cut separates blob from
  letter.** What separates them is *small and solid*: the letters are either ≥ 70 px in one dimension
  or hollow (fill ratio ≤ 0.47). A regression test pins this: a ceiling tuned to 1.jpg (area ≤ 600)
  drops 2.jpg's blob entirely.
- **Sizes come from the file header.** "How big is that speck" is a citable fact in the h

plugins.description: Time-shifting task delegation for DeepSeek Harness (dsh): plan tasks at leisure, they run unattended off-peak, come back to a report. Human-adjudicated, desktop + web.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-lowtide **Queue tasks when it's busy. They run on their own when it's cheap.** Semi-auto or full-auto, off the model's peak hours and peak prices. A must-have plugin for DeepSeek Harness. **English** | [简体中文](./README.zh-CN.md) | [繁體中文](./README.zh-HK.md) | [العربية](./docs/README.ar.md) | [Deutsch](./docs/README.de.md) | [Español](./docs/README.es.md) | [Français](./docs/README.fr.md) | [Italiano](./docs/README.it.md) | [한국어](./docs/README.ko.md)
--- ![hero](./assets/screenshots/hero.png)

Three tasks waiting in the queue, the price status glowing in the session header, auto-run when your window opens

## Introduction lowtide is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness (dsh)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh). The problem it solves is plain and perfectly natural: Usually, when you want an agent to do some work, you sit at the computer, send the agent an instruction, wait for the reply, and then review it by hand. But this workflow seems to forget that you have plenty of idle time — and a chance to dodge the peak/off-peak pricing that some models charge. With lowtide installed, the day goes like this: whenever a job crosses your mind during the day, toss it in the queue, glance at it, release it. The tasks pile up until the time you set (say, after 7 PM — that's when DeepSeek is at valley pricing), then run by themselves. Next morning you open the report: keep what went well, send back what didn't. That's all it is. But use it for a week and your working rhythm genuinely slows down — and don't forget, "time is money, efficiency is life"... A few key capabilities: - Four execution strategies: single, iterative, sampling, review — from "one pass is enough" to "run five candidates and I'll pick" - 168 unit tests + 10 end-to-end specs, CI green across ubuntu / windows × node 22 / 24 - One build artifact serves both desktop and web — install once, works on both - Off-peak execution lands in DeepSeek's valley hours: the same batch costs about half of what peak would ## A normal day with an agent might look like this… **Ten minutes before clocking out.** You've finished reviewing code, so you file three tickets for tomorrow: a refactor (iterative, 3 rounds), a weekly report (single), and a design you're unsure about (sampling, 4 candidates). Release them all, shut down, leave. Tomorrow at your desk, the morning report says: the refactor's done, the report's drafted, and four candidate designs sit side by side, each with its cost written out. **Friday night.** Queue a week's worth of chores in one go: dependency cleanup, missing tests, data scripts. Weekends are valley price around the clock. You go out; it works from home. Monday you check the report — retry what failed, merge what's good. **A 10 AM brainwave.** You're mid-conversation with the agent about an urgent bug when you think "hey, update the docs too." The intercept card pops up: running now costs peak price, tonight it's about half — the difference is spelled out. Click "queue for off-peak"; your draft survives untouched, and you go back to the bug. **An always-on server.** You've got a machine running dsh 24/7. Switch to L3 full-auto, then file tasks from anywhere through the API (`POST /ds-lowtide/tasks`). It runs them on schedule and writes the report. Nobody's watching, but the sandbox, the daily budget, and the file locks are all still there. **Deliverables for a client.** Use the review strategy: run once, then automatically open an independent session that tears the result apart through your chosen focus (say, "hunt for data-source errors"). In the morning you don't get a bare result — you get a result plus a critical review. **Living abroad.** You're in San Francisco; DeepSeek's peak is Beijing time, which for you lands in the evening and night before. Settings converts the official hours to your local clock, one click to adopt. You set windows by your own schedule, and the books always stay aligned with the official table. ## How lowtide works ``` ① Intake ② Adjudicate ③ Execute ④ Accept Whenever you have The queue dock When the off-peak When you're back: a moment: one-click groups tasks by window opens: five open the report — from the intercept workspace; triage preflight gates pass, results + diff card, or file a → line by line: → then sandboxed runs → + actual spend ticket (4 strategies) ✓approve ⏸defer one batch per window + money saved ✕drop / approve-all ``` A task's life: `pending-review → queued → preflight → running → done / failed / stale / timeout`, plus `deferred` (postponed) and `dropped` (soft-deleted, restorable). Step two is where lowtide differs from a "fully automated script": **every task must be released by your hand before it runs** (in L2, you release the whole batch at once, 30 minutes before the window). The machine cannot move itself into the run queue. Execution is automated; decisions are not. That's why you can safely be absent. ## A tour of the lowtide interface **The new-task modal.** Four strategies side by side, each with a plain-language hint; rounds, priority, and run mode ride along per task — no trip back to settings. Tasks land as "pending review". Nothing enters the queue without passing you. ![new-task-modal](./assets/screenshots/new-task-modal.png) **Advanced options.** Model, reasoning effort, priority from 0 to 9, fresh session or continue-previous, and the locked-files list — all in one small pane. Locked files, briefly: anything on the list gets sha256-checked before execution, and if it doesn't match what you filed, the task goes stale and refuses to run. Otherwise the file you queued against could be rewritten by another task while waiting, and this one would blindly stomp on it. ![advanced-options](./assets/screenshots/advanced-options.png) **Pick any model.** Batch runs default to the official `deepseek-flash` (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash; the retired `deepseek-v4-flash` name still routes there at Flash prices), but each task can pick its own model — anything connected to your Harness is in the dropdown, grouped by provider. Private providers work too. Non-official models have no public price table, so the ledger honestly says "price unknown"; add a price override in settings if you want the bookkeeping exact. ![model-picker](./assets/screenshots/model-picker.png) **The window editor.** Multi-segment, overnight, per-weekday — all fine. Underneath is a live 24-hour price band: red for peak, green for valley, and a marker showing where you are right now. Outside UTC+8, one click on "adopt official peak hours" converts Beijing time to your local clock. ![window-editor](./assets/screenshots/window-editor.png) **The settings page.** Window hours, tasks per batch, per-task duration cap, concurrency, daily budget, report history, autonomy level, price overrides — all graphical, no config files. The official pricing rules (including the new all-weekend valley) are explained in human language on the same page. ![settings](./assets/screenshots/settings.png) Three more pieces of UI appear in daily use: the **price pill** (session header — busy/idle, queue size; click it to edit windows), the **peak-hours intercept card** (type at peak, it appears; the price difference is spelled out; your draft survives), and the **execution report** (the morning briefing: savings first, anomalies pinned, candidates awaiting your pick, one-click Markdown copy). ## About lowtide workspaces Every task runs inside a workspace. That single dropdown decides three things. **Which files it can touch.** Tasks run in a sandbox whose boundary is the workspace directory. Pick wrong and at best it can't find the files; at worst it edits something it shouldn't. **Who it queues with.** Tasks in the same workspace run serially (two tasks never fight over one repo); different workspaces run in paralle

plugins.description: 峰谷倒计时：在 DSH 模型名称中显示 DeepSeek 峰谷状态与倒计时，支持实时预览与紧凑设置。
plugins.readme_text: # 峰谷倒计时 独立插件 **dsh-liao-peakclock**，当前版本 **0.1.1**，适配 **DeepSeek Harness 0.2.0-rc.2**。 在原生模型选择器中显示 `DS4.1F · 谷 2:30 · High`。峰时用琥珀色，谷时用青绿色；倒计时为小时:分钟，完整型号保留在悬停提示中。 ## 截图 桌面 DSH 中的实际模型按钮： 峰时与谷时的显示效果： 设置页包含当前状态、时间轴、显示偏好及可折叠的计费说明： 后两张截图来自插件独立预览，使用示例模型和时间；展示的是实际插件组件，按三倍分辨率渲染，点击可查看高清原图。 ## 安装 在 DSH 插件页选择“添加插件”，输入： ```text github:oliblue-evan/dsh-liao-peakclock ``` 或使用 CLI（将 `desktop` 换成自己的 Profile 名称）： ```sh dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:oliblue-evan/dsh-liao-peakclock ``` 仓库包含预构建产物，安装时无需编译源码。仅声明支持 DSH **0.2.0-rc.2**；其他版本须先核验兼容性。目前未发布 npm 包。 ## 使用 打开“插件 → 峰谷倒计时”： - 当前状态：峰/谷、秒级倒计时、下次切换时间和今日 24 小时时段轴。 - 显示偏好：常用选项与峰／谷双状态预览并排，短选项使用分段按钮，无系统下拉菜单；更多显示选项默认折叠。三套预设保留总开关、来源范围和提前时间。 - 倒计时：始终、临近切换或关闭；临近模式可提前 30／60 分钟显示，设置页仍保留完整的实时倒计时。 - 生效范围：所有可识别的 DeepSeek 模型，或仅 DSH 官方账号与官方 API 来源；第三方渠道不视为官方计费。 - 价格与规则：按需展开官方 API 的人民币价格快照、计费解释、峰谷规则与日历来源。 模型识别优先读取当前输入框所属会话的模型 ID；带渠道前缀和自定义显示名也可识别。ID 尚不可用时才以名称兜底。多个会话分别绑定各自输入框，不读取全局默认模型替代会话状态。 模型名称处通常按分钟刷新；设置页打开时共享时钟切换为秒级，关闭后恢复分钟级。页面隐藏时暂停前台时钟，唤醒时重新读取系统时间。 ## 时段与计费参考 北京时间，周一至周五 09:00–12:00、14:00–18:00 为峰时，不含中国法定节假日；其余时间、周末和法定节假日全天为谷时，调休周末仍按谷时。 这里提供的是 [DeepSeek 官方时段与价格](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/quick_start/pricing/) 参考；第三方渠道可能有不同倍率、套餐和计费规则，以渠道账单为准。插件不读取 API 密钥、不查询余额、不修改模型或实际扣费。 价格为 2026-10-15 核对的静态快照，附官方最新价格链接，不假称实时同步。节假日日历沿用上游的验证逻辑，临近年末或缺少年份时从固定 holiday-cn 数据源尝试补充；无法确定下一次切换时明确显示“待核实”。 ## 从旧版迁移 该独立包不会占用或修改原版 dsh-timeband 的包名、Loader ID 或样式所有权。 首次运行优先读取自己的存储；若尚无数据，会先尝试迁移独立试用版，再尝试迁移原本 `dsh-timeband` 的显示偏好、节假日日历和日历检查记录。旧数据保留；已有设置不会被旧数据覆盖。旧提醒、音效、弹出时间轴和更新检查不再包含在本包中。 安装新包前停用旧包，避免两套显示同时运行。建议保留旧包和 Profile 配置备份以便回滚。无需更改 DSH 宿主源码。 ## 开发与检查 Node.js 22+，npm： ```sh npm ci --ignore-scripts npm run compatibility npm run typecheck npm run build npm test npm run test:browser npm pack --ignore-scripts npm run test:artifact -- ./dsh-liao-peakclock-0.1.1.tgz ``` `compatibility` 仅核验精确目标 0.2.0-rc.2，不追随 npm latest，也不修改宿主。 `npm run preview` 提供仅浏览器使用的回归夹具：加载实际构建产物，以模拟会话验证别名、切换、开关、时间边界和卸载。它不是 DSH Web 实例，不读取真实 Profile、账号或对话。浏览器测试使用这一夹具；真实 SlotRegistry 生命周期和多会话隔离另有构建产物/DOM 测试。 客户端以 ModuleLoader 格式构建，运行时仅由宿主提供 React。模型身份来自公开的会话级 ModelDirectory；原生 ModelSelect 没有导出替换组件，因此显示层仍使用针对 rc.2 控件结构的窄范围 DOM 适配。它保留 React 原节点与原生事件，仅增加自有显示节点，禁用或卸载时恢复。宿主升级后需要重新核验控件结构；无法匹配的控件保留原生显示。 ## 来源与许可 派生自 [dsh-timeband v1.3.4](https://github.com/a961282799-crypto/dsh-timeband)，保留其节假日与时段基础逻辑，并重做显示、设置、会话绑定和验证流程。这是独立维护的衍生插件。 MIT，原版权和许可全文保留在 LICENSE；来源记录见 NOTICE。
